entries.title: Felix: Biography
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Felix: Biography MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Felix is Lynleit's long-standing friend and one of the MSF officers Fionn trusts as her personal bodyguards. He accompanies her on operations, official journeys, and casual outings. Lynleit reveals her secret recruitment of Kyrien only to Felix and Reiner. Felix regards Kyrien as a threat whenever the bodyguards are not close enough to protect her. He concedes only because Reiner chooses Lynleit's judgment, leaving Felix as the minority opinion. Felix never fully learns to trust Kyrien. Their recurring clashes turn protection into open friction, and Lynleit must reprimand Felix when his hostility interferes with the compartment she created. During an ordinary walk after lunch, he sees Lynleit collapse onto a city bench but never enters the Nameless Street she experiences while unconscious. Fionn's death, Lynleit's accusation, and the hunt for her arrest force Felix to decide whether loyalty means following the formal chain of command or protecting his friend. Kyrien later helps Lynleit contact Felix and Reiner from hiding, drawing them into her slow campaign to reclaim MSF from Helena. Serves alongside Lynleit as a friend and trusted bodyguard. Learns of Kyrien's secret recruitment. Accepts the arrangement without trusting Kyrien. Lends Lynleit his Rook after worrying about her Sparrow. Helps the hunted Lynleit reconnect with MSF. Felix

entries.title: Felix: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Felix: Conflicts MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Lynleit's judgment His distrust of Kyrien brings him into conflict with the friend he wants to protect. Attachment to Lynleit His hopes remain centered on Lynleit while familiarity and affection grow with Sherie. Reciprocating Sherie's teasing is easier than recognizing how important she has become to him. Felix

entries.title: Felix: Connections
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Felix: Connections MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Lynleit Friendship and persistent flirting He protects her as a long-standing friend and keeps testing her patience with flirtation. On church visits with her and Fionn, he cannot resist flirting with nuns. Reiner behaves; Felix keeps doing it until Lynleit loses patience. He tells her he only has eyes for her, but she does not accept his attempt to recast the reprimand as a request for romantic loyalty. Sherie Growing familiarity Their connection develops slowly from repeated professional encounters, with no meaningful personal relationship at the opening. Felix enjoys her company, responds to her teasing, and starts seeking her out. Still fixated on Lynleit, he can mistake Sherie's interest for practiced charm or an entertaining friendship. She gradually becomes someone around whom he need not always perform. His eventual movement toward her requires recognizing that he wants Sherie herself. At cards, he complains about Lynleit while Sherie interrupts his concentration without interrupting him. When he asks why she is looking at him that way, her reply leaves him without an answer. He begins remembering small details, wanting to tell her things, noticing her absence, and learning the changes in her voice. Flirtation remains easy while sincere speech becomes harder. Wanting her eventually has to change his choices over time. Their private game does not require a formal relationship. Her discretion and easy return to ordinary company become part of what draws him to her, while their claim that nothing happened gradually carries a shared history. Lynleit Their bond is friendship as well as service. Felix can protect, question, tease, and accompany her with a familiarity that a mere subordinate would not possess, but that closeness also makes her secret trust in Kyrien difficult for him to accept. Kyrien Felix sees Kyrien as an unverified threat inside Lynleit's private circle. Being outvoted makes him tolerate the arrangement, not trust the man. Potential sexual tension Lynleit Established asymmetry Felix overt, Lynleit deflecting Lynleit is one of the few people his charm cannot simply move into the response he wants. Familiar affection, physical ease, and repeated deflection keep his attraction active even when he respects the boundary she has made. He remains internally fixated on her while growing close to Sherie through work. Enjoying Sherie's company does not immediately change whom he imagines being intimate with; his attachment to Lynleit takes more than successful flirtation to loosen. Only Eyes for You develops a recurring problem during Lynleit and Fionn's church visits, with Felix and Reiner accompanying them. Reiner behaves, while Felix repeatedly flirts with nuns until Lynleit loses patience. He answers her eventual reprimand with 'I only have eyes for you.' The author identifies accumulated irritation as the comic cause, not jealousy. His reply redirects an objection he does not want to answer; it does not make her objection romantic. His wider flirting coexists with his persistent fixation on Lynleit and does not establish an attachment to any particular nun. The visits precede Fionn's death, but their exact placement and relation to his growing closeness with Sherie remain open. Sherie's 'Looks like you two have unresolved tension' in the card-game interlude is her teasing interpretation, not confirmation that Lynleit reciprocates. Felix's distraction by Sherie coexists with the same unresolved attachment. Potential sexual tension Sherie Author-confirmed direction Private games, mutual trust and uneven attachment Felix enjoys Sherie's company, answers her teasing, and gradually seeks her out while remaining internally fixated on Lynleit. His attention is responsive, but he may interpret Sherie's interest as habitual charm or their closeness as an entertaining professional friendship. Emotional investment can precede his recognition of its intimate possibility. His attachment to Lynleit has genuine weight and takes more than successful flirtation to loosen. Moving toward Sherie eventually means recognizing her own importance to him and wanting her without treating her as a substitute for Lynleit. He may offer a hopeful interpretation to reassure someone while still privately testing it. If a trusted person points out that his attachment to Lynleit is hurting Sherie, the author expects stunned recognition and surprise that he missed it; the actual exchange and its consequences remain unwritten. During their card game he complains about Lynleit while Sherie distracts him. His returning glance and failed answer to 'Like what?' provide a small interruption in his usual fluency, not a sudden transfer of allegiance or a confession. He remembers small details, wants to tell her things, notices her absence, and learns changes in her voice while his hopes remain organized around Lynleit. Flirting comes more easily than sincere speech. Recognizing that he wants Sherie must lead to sustained changes in his choices, not a single confession. Sherie's easy return to ordinary company after intimacy becomes part of her appeal. He can share their private code without turning her trust into boasting or a claim on her. Wanting Sherie in her own right does not require an official partnership; his lingering hopes about Lynleit can still wound her. In The Shared Night he acknowledges enjoying her company and respects their agreement not to touch or kiss when the pressure releases them. His enjoyment does not settle his divided attachment. They have no meaningful personal relationship at the story's opening. Sherie's diplomatic responsibilities increasingly overlap with Felix's work around Lynleit and MSF, bringing repeated encounters before either chooses closeness. Familiarity, respect, private jokes, and a compatible rhythm develop gradually. Her confident, playful dominance meets his expressiveness, improvisation, and willingness to challenge her. Humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals carry into affection and eventual adult intimacy. Care becomes particularly revealing when one stops performing and the other remains attentive. Readers can notice Felix building intimacy's foundations with Sherie while still imagining it with Lynleit; narration need not explain that contradiction. The later teasing challenge to Lynleit remains, but it neither starts their familiarity nor reduces Sherie's interest to winning him. This differs from Lynleit's strategic recruitment of Kyrien and their quieter recognition through restrained attention, protected secrets, and gradually accepted vulnerability. Both couples remain subplots beneath the political and supernatural story. Unresolved Tension supplies an early card-game scene draft and a linked panel sequence. Her observation about Felix and Lynleit, his denial, her 'Mm,' and the final unanswered 'Like what?' let a second, less acknowledged attraction enter the conversation. The cards give them an ordinary shared activity; no game, stakes, winner, room owner, or numbered phase is established. The Shared Night now preserves their no-kissing boundary after recovered choice; precise chronology remains unplaced. Their diplomatic and MSF obligations can produce substantive disagreements that attraction cannot settle. Establish ordinary company, especially her voice in his communications work, before a separation or dangerous assignment makes a delayed reply frightening. A failed familiar joke, reciprocal care, or a voluntary decision to stay can convey the later weight without extinguishing their pleasure. The particular disputes, danger, and separation remain unwritten; tragedy is not required. A restrained early musical motif may return with more space and unresolved harmony as a composition direction, not an assigned recording. Their later intimacy is a private, deniable game rather than a conventional formal romance. Cards, rematches and tactics acquire meanings only they share; "nothing happened" accumulates trust, embarrassment, tenderness and private history. Her rapid return to ordinary conversation can surprise him. "You're safe" names the freedom she finds with him, not a guarantee against disappointment. The early discovery encounter is author-directed but not drafted or dated. Its mechanics remain off-page. This later code must not be read back into the early card-game scene as an established habit. Sherie's Kyrie Eleison direction places a serious eventual reckoning beyond her enjoyment of manipulative social games. The particular catastrophe is undecided, and Felix is not assigned as its victim, cause or savior. Their genuine affection and trust remain; her wider mistakes must not turn every private exchange into a calculated exploitation. She starts without knowledge of magic, and her personal theme is not automatically their shared relationship motif. The Shared Night is a canonical encounter with draft dialogue and unassigned placement. Compelled dream activity cannot establish a preference or desire. Their familiar provocations persist, but acknowledging their enjoyment of one another helps restore a gap between impulse and action. Sherie steps away when she can. She does not kiss Felix in or outside dreams. Her intention is a stable, professional, plausibly deniable connection with minimized emotional dependency, not a formal romance. This contrasts with the unintended emotional closeness proposed for Lynleit and Kyrien's nonsexual dream. Felix

entries.title: Felix: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Felix: Strengths and weaknesses MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Felix jokes, flirts, and tries out explanations even when nothing depends on the answer. In danger he is often the first to offer an interpretation people can bear. He may not believe it yet; while reassuring them, he keeps looking for evidence and a meaning he can accept himself. He takes conflict personally and wants to make things right directly afterward. His hacking and communications work finds indirect approaches, making him the knight to Reiner's rook. Sherie's confident direction invites him to tease back. He enjoys her company and grows attached, while still imagining intimacy with Lynleit. The Shared Night He suspects that Sherie shares his dreams before she discovers the correspondence. Their usual jokes make the briefing worse. When the pressure eases, he respects their agreement not to touch or kiss. Their coffee plans do not settle his attachment to Lynleit. Playful flirt He turns tension into teasing, tests reactions openly, and treats charm as both genuine expression and useful disruption. Troublemaker Felix has difficulty resisting a chance to flirt even when the setting calls for restraint. During church visits with Lynleit, Fionn, and Reiner, his repeated advances to nuns become a recurring source of trouble. Personal loyalty He protects Lynleit as a long-standing friend and is openly suspicious of anyone he thinks may hurt her. Missed consequences If someone he respects points out that his attachment to Lynleit is hurting Sherie, his first response is stunned recognition and surprise that he failed to notice. That realization does not immediately settle his feelings. ENFP Ne-led reading; Fi tentative Suspected Felix

entries.title: Fionn: Biography
entries.subtitle: Magiarch and MSF founder
entries.text: Fionn: Biography Magiarch and MSF founder Fionn's Magi lineage has maintained an association with the Cult of Inanna for three thousand years. Father Mikhail knows its history. Fionn visits churches with Lynleit, accompanied by Felix and Reiner. Fionn creates MSF with a public intelligence purpose and a hidden structure prepared for magical crisis. He embeds cryptology into ordinary behavior: blue clothing initiates recognition, followed by an innocuous conversational challenge-response known only to top officers he trusts. He refuses to declare one uncontested successor because naming an heir would paint a target on that person. Within his family, he is the virtuoso of a hereditary blue-flame magecraft defined by control and subtle application. The family house is also a discreet residential node for MSF, with offices and a library supporting selected work without replacing the formal headquarters in Turon. Foreign Magiarchates, church actors, criminal Magi, and Helena pursue incompatible objectives around Fionn. Their pressures converge without one actor commanding the complete assassination. Several individually rational reasons persuade Fionn to delay acting until reasonable caution becomes his fatal mistake. Fionn withholds the deepest parts of his life from Helena. He considers this protection; she considers it exclusion. His secrecy also leaves the people around him unable to compare what they know about the threats he faces. After his assassination, Lynleit and Kyrien must interpret his unfinished plans, concealed MSF signals, and the agendas of several enemies. His refusal to name one successor creates the succession crisis he hoped to prevent. Helena knowingly assists part of the plot, but neither she nor any other participant controls the full outcome. Directs MSF publicly and serves as Magiarch in secret. Prepares the agency for a magical crisis. Delays acting while several political and supernatural threats converge. Leaves concealed safeguards and no uncontested successor. Development outline: rebuilding his household while MSF takes its later shape. Fionn

entries.title: Fionn: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: Magiarch and MSF founder
entries.text: Fionn: Conflicts Magiarch and MSF founder Delayed action Competing pressures keep him from acting as Magiarch in time. Succession Naming an heir would endanger that person; leaving the question open divides MSF after his death. Fionn

entries.title: Fionn: Connections
entries.subtitle: Magiarch and MSF founder
entries.text: Fionn: Connections Magiarch and MSF founder Lynleit His biological daughter and likely heir in practice, though he refuses to make any successor uncontested and leaves much of her inheritance unexplained. Converging agendas Criminal Magi, rival Magiarchates, church actors, and Helena may each enable a different part of the outcome without sharing one command structure or objective. Potential sexual tension Helena Established marriage Mutual, damaged by exclusion Fionn's affection and desire for Helena are genuine. He separates bodily and domestic closeness from the secrets he believes he must carry alone, never understanding that this division changes what their intimacy means to her. Their sexual tension survives inside a real marriage because attraction and grievance occupy the same private space. The closer they become physically, the harder it is for Helena to accept that Fionn still decides which parts of himself she is permitted to know. Fionn

The flame is a family discipline with a broad range of applications. Practiced method Precision before volume His distinction is virtuosity. Fionn can shape the flame through subtle, controlled applications that Lynleit has not learned to reproduce. Generational contrast Control and force Fionn represents the refined expression of the lineage. Lynleit possesses less finesse, but a greater willingness to manifest the flame at an unsafe scale. Irreplaceable force Beyond ordinary weapons The lineage becomes essential against threats that firearms cannot resolve: immortal or rapidly regenerating Holumns, bodies that move without being alive, and barriers that ordinary force cannot break. entries.title: Hiyu: Biography
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and intuitive investigator
entries.text: Hiyu: Biography Criminology student and intuitive investigator Hiyu studies criminology with Yulia, but his reputation comes from personal investigations instead of class rank. She masters the established discipline. He follows loose fragments, invents methods on the spot, and pursues possibilities that initially sound ridiculous. Their constant friction gradually becomes a working dependency. From the public fragments surrounding the disappearances, Hiyu suspects that magic may be involved. He has no hidden knowledge and does not know magic exists. The hypothesis fits his intuitive pattern strongly enough that he decides to enter the quarantined park for evidence, pulling a reluctant Yulia into the attempt. His hunch is directionally correct, but gives him no practical understanding of Holumns, the Spill, or survival inside the park. The conviction that lets him challenge an accepted explanation also puts both students in physical danger. Hiyu and Yulia become increasingly dependent on their different methods. He remains largely unaware that their need for one another is developing romantic weight. Survival must teach him that a correct idea can still be incomplete and dangerous. Suspects magic despite not knowing it exists. Persuades Yulia to enter the quarantined park. Finds more danger than his theory prepared him for. Keeps seeking Yulia's criticism without recognizing his attachment. Hiyu

entries.text: Hiyu: Connections Criminology student and intuitive investigator Yulia The procedural counterweight he complains around, relies upon constantly, and gradually becomes unable to investigate without. He does not recognize the emotional meaning of that dependence. Calibration His mind is excellent at opening possibilities and poor at deciding how much confidence, danger, or action a partial pattern deserves. Potential sexual tension Yulia Emerging arc Mutual, unequally conscious Yulia is the critic whose resistance makes an idea worth pursuing. He becomes dependent on her attention before he understands that the dependence is personal, leaving him oblivious to tension that is already changing how he seeks her out. A possible scene has them lean over the same evidence or reach for the same document while arguing. Yulia notices their proximity first; Hiyu continues the theory. Another possible beat has him keep turning toward her usual place while investigating alone. These are staging suggestions for their established attraction arc, not completed encounters or an established sexual relationship. Her objections must remain genuine, and the investigation must still matter. Hiyu

entries.title: Hiyu: Strengths and weaknesses

entries.text: Hiyu: Strengths and weaknesses Criminology student and intuitive investigator Hiyu is driven by possibility, contradiction, and the pleasure of making an unlikely pattern click. He constantly experiences eureka moments, builds protocols while using them, and abandons a clean path as soon as a stranger one becomes interesting. He has a reputation for ignoring women because ideas consume his attention so completely. This also leaves him oblivious to the romantic tension slowly forming with Yulia. Divergent inference He can connect fragments through possibilities other investigators reject too early, which is how a non-Magus with no knowledge of magic nevertheless suspects it. Improvised method Hiyu invents investigative procedures in response to the problem in front of him, making him flexible where Yulia is disciplined and unreliable where she is exact. Dangerous conviction A brilliant possibility becomes a plan before he has established whether the environment is survivable. Partial success makes him even more reckless. ENTP strong Ne Confirmed Hiyu

Failure condition Insight without calibration Correctly suspecting magic does not teach him what magic can do, how to gather evidence safely, or when an unexplained environment has already outmatched him. The Church and MSF each know more than they admit, leaving Leo to investigate the authorities controlling the answers without understanding the supernatural order behind them. entries.title: Kyrien: Biography
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Biography Independent operator and later MSF director Kyrien's father is a Narvean military-police commander who teaches him about weapons and officer conduct. At five, Kyrien points a Sparrow at a civilian and is sharply corrected. Years later, his father survives a fugitive's assault while protecting his officers, kills the fugitive in self-defence, and witnesses magic. He tells nobody. Officials connected to the Magiarchy fabricate a prosecution, then obtain sanction to murder him and present his death as suicide. His mother increasingly struggles with ordinary life, and he takes on much of her care. Kyrien works extra shifts and jobs to support her and pay competent lawyers. Their evidence prompts an inquiry that confirms deliberate distortion, but a closed national-security review protects the senior prosecutor and publicly vindicates him. Kyrien continues working and caring for his mother. Only later, after strangers humiliate her in a shop and she apologizes for failing to manage the shopping, does he decide to kill the prosecutor. The prosecutor is promoted to Prosecutor General. Kyrien's attempt at the appointment dinner fails partly because of a concealed connection to the magical world, without revealing magic to him. He escapes and is detained later on suspicion, not a conclusive case. Lynleit was nearly harmed at the dinner, but never tells him she attended. With his lawyer still representing him, she questions him and recognizes the suppressed injustice behind his family's case. She offers help obtaining release, paid confidential work, and arrangements for his mother's care, without unconditional immunity. He agrees reluctantly after negotiating the terms. Fionn is not told; Lynleit tells only Felix and Reiner in her circle. Felix clashes with Kyrien; Reiner remains watchful but accepts Lynleit's decision. During the failed river watches, Kyrien plays cards with her and begins learning her tells. Seeing her walk on water is his first unmistakable exposure to magic. He tells nobody; she initially only suspects what he saw. When Mikhail questions her about the breach, however, Kyrien tells him that Felix and Reiner also know. While Lynleit is in Cardiff, Kyrien protects Myka undercover at the Academy, relying on Felix and Reiner until Natalia intervenes. After Fionn's death he shelters Lynleit and helps her reconnect with the officers. Asked why he keeps risking his life without a reward, he answers: "Because there's a battle to be fought." Much later, once both openly acknowledge his knowledge of Magi, Lynleit offers a possibility of revenge against the Prosecutor General for a separate new offence, conditional on genuine proof. Kyrien recognizes her manipulation. Punishment need not bring any acknowledgment of the wrong done to his father. Kyrien stays with Lynleit after she loses the authority to compel him. They survive a shared curse following an incomplete attempt at intimacy, but she will not explain the proposed treatment. Months after Doom, the spontaneous park encounter becomes their first successful sexual act, distinct from later intercourse. When Lynleit inherits the Magiarchate and then disappears, Kyrien becomes director of MSF. He must manage its government contracts, divided loyalties, ordinary intelligence work, and response to the Spill without her magical authority. He does not know that Lynleit bore their son during her disappearance. She continues to keep the child hidden from him and the wider world. During Arc 2 they restore intimacy and eventually conceive a daughter, who is born later. They have two children by the end of their story. Works for years to support his mother and finance lawyers. After institutional refusal and her later humiliation, he attempts to kill the newly appointed Prosecutor General. Accepts paid confidential work and support for release, with his lawyer negotiating terms and care for his mother. Tells Lynleit that a battle is reason enough to fight. Protects Myka until Natalia can intervene. Survives the curse but does not learn why Lynleit attempted intimacy. Takes over MSF while Lynleit is absent. Remains unaware that Lynleit bore his son. Tentative prequel: family life before recruitment; the age and Arc of his father's death remain undecided. Shares a private encounter with Lynleit months after Doom, then gives her his flask without pressing for an explanation. Kyrien

entries.title: Kyrien: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Conflicts Independent operator and later MSF director Concealed recruit Felix distrusts him, and his position initially depends on Lynleit's protection. Command without a Magiarch He later runs MSF's ordinary and supernatural work while Lynleit is absent. Kyrien

entries.title: Kyrien: Connections
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Connections Independent operator and later MSF director Their son First child Born during Lynleit's disappearance and kept hidden from Kyrien and the wider world afterward. Their daughter Second child Conceived after intimacy is restored during Arc 2 and born later. Lynleit Handler and eventual partner She questions him knowing that his failed attack nearly harmed her, a fact he never learns. Their repeated card games create a voluntary contest inside the coerced arrangement. He later protects her water-walking secret, gives her refuge, and chooses to remain once her authority can no longer compel him. In the later part of Arc 1's second half, one curse binds their identities after they destroy a Holumn together. Lynleit attempts intimacy without revealing the proposed treatment. The incomplete attempt is followed by recovery, leaving Kyrien with questions she will not answer. Their closeness also requires him to accept being recognized and challenged. His reserve does not always protect him from her attention, and remaining beside her gradually permits responses he would otherwise conceal. Kyrien's father Formative authority A military-police commander who introduces Kyrien to weapons, protocol, and officer morality. His correction of Kyrien's first reckless act with a Sparrow becomes the foundation of his son's belief that using force also means accepting reciprocal danger. Kyrien's mother Continuing family responsibility His father's death and disgrace leave her increasingly unable to manage ordinary life. Kyrien cares for her while working to fund legal representation. Her tastes, habits and attempts at independence persist; her care and his income remain obligations after recruitment. Myka Undercover charge Kyrien keeps Myka safe inside the Magi Academy through conventional field skills and contact with Felix and Reiner until Natalia reaches them. Lynleit Lynleit recruits him while he faces continued detention, with his lawyer negotiating pay and provision for his mother. He later chooses to stay, keeps her forbidden ability secret, and gives her refuge. After their shared curse ends, she refuses to explain why she tried to sleep with him. He suspects a connection between the attempt and their recovery. Tien Tien serves Helena as a concealed assassin. Kyrien must contend with an opponent who also relies on deception and surprise. Potential sexual tension Lynleit Established arc Mutual, slow to surface Kyrien wants to beat Lynleit at cards and dislikes finding that she can read him. Her elegance and nerve also attract him. He stays because he wants the battle, then finds himself facing private questions that her orders cannot answer. After the attempted intimacy, she will not tell him why their curse disappeared. He notices her pleasure in success and answers with a joke rather than a declaration. When she later asks for his flask, he does not force an explanation. The author also intends him to notice how being able to affect him changes her confidence. This reciprocal observation is not a shift into generic dominance. Quiet companionship and private tells matter alongside practical dependence and protected secrets. Her initiative, pride, and curiosity can reach him, but both must gradually allow themselves to be affected rather than continually managing what the other notices. Their intimacy includes being quietly recognized, accompanied, and challenged without their usual defenses; restraint can become unnecessary without making them talkative. Recruitment remains antagonistic: Kyrien's legal campaign and care obligations make paid work and release support materially important. Lynleit's concern for his mother coexists with leverage and concealed anger. Neither his agreement nor her guilt establishes attraction. The interrogation, card games, protected secret, and voluntary decision to stay give this pairing different kinds of familiarity. In Doom Has an Address, an incomplete attempt at intimacy breaks the shared curse. Lynleit loses the excuse of treatment without losing her interest in Kyrien; he is left trying to understand what happened. Their sexual relationship begins later in Arc 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge precede Doom. Months afterward, a spontaneous park encounter lets Lynleit's curiosity and wounded pride become a successful private milestone. Oral intimacy, reciprocal exploration, first intercourse, and pregnancy remain separate. The family theme does not turn ancestry into an instruction or make grief itself attraction. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from both Kyrien and the wider world. They restore intimacy during Arc 2 and eventually conceive a second child, a daughter, who is born later. The daughter's conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2, not within it. The author has confirmed this direction, not the scenes that restore intimacy or the timing of Kyrien's discovery of their son. Duty remains primary; a second child does not substitute for the work of reconnection. Their connected dream in The Shared Night remains unspecified. Develop a nonsexual, painful or emotionally exposing experience that draws them closer unintentionally; childhood disclosures are a possibility, not established history. Preserve the later physical milestones. Potential sexual tension Sherie Strong potential Situational and confrontational Sherie's charm is too deliberate to disarm him, but the precision behind it earns his attention. He is more likely to watch for the moment her performance fails than reward the performance itself. Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit. Kyrien

entries.title: Kyrien: Motivations
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Motivations Independent operator and later MSF director Survive Lynleit's control, master the intelligence side of MSF, pursue the Prosecutor General responsible for his family's destruction without abandoning his mother, and eventually make choices inside the hidden world on terms that are genuinely his own. Kyrien

entries.title: Kyrien: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Strengths and weaknesses Independent operator and later MSF director Kyrien speaks little, rarely smiles, and wants to win. Cards, chess, and a gunfight can all provoke the same stubbornness. Cheating can make him abandon the safer objective. He notices things others miss in his surroundings and in unfolding events, looking first for danger in unfamiliar behavior. An explanation that seems faulty bothers him even when the method works. He keeps thinking about it in the background, sometimes reaching an answer and acting before he can explain how he got there. If he is wrong, he wants to find the assumption that misled him and avoid repeating the mistake. The Shared Night He notices the exchanged looks before Sherie and Felix admit their shared dreams. He and Lynleit acknowledge their own experience without discussing its particulars in front of the group. Intelligence tradecraft 97 He observes details in the environment and in unfolding situations that others overlook. Those observations let him prepare for dangers that are not yet apparent to the people around him. Strategic adaptation 94 He turns preparation into immediate tactical action when a threat develops. This makes him a concealed resource for Lynleit when isolation or conspiracy leaves her without her usual support. Survival discipline 92 He does not try to overpower Magi. He stays difficult to locate, corner, deceive, or kill. ISTP Ti-Se-Ni working model; INTJ alternative Suspected Kyrien

entries.title: Kyrien: Tradecraft
entries.subtitle: Independent operator and later MSF director
entries.text: Kyrien: Tradecraft Independent operator and later MSF director Concealment Subterfuge Controls what others can infer about his intent, identity, loyalties, and next movement. He survives by giving opponents a convincing answer that is not the true one. Escape discipline Evasion Studies surveillance and plans exits before entry. He looks for ways to change the terms of a confrontation, though his urge to win can draw him into one he would otherwise avoid. Misdirection Trickery Uses false patterns, staged weaknesses, timing, and selective truth to make stronger opponents commit to the wrong interpretation. Physical execution Endurance and precision Kyrien combines endurance with precision in his movements and actions. Relative strength Obstacle movement His strength is most effective against his own body weight. He may not strike with the greatest force, but he moves quickly through difficult ground, pulls himself over obstacles, and can climb fences or walls when an escape route demands it. Preparedness Redundant options Kyrien usually keeps at least two objects available that are weapons or can become weapons. The pair changes with circumstance and may include a knife, keys, a pen, or a pocket pistol. The habit keeps options within reach rather than imposing a fixed loadout. Experience with lawyers Caution under questioning Years financing his father's case teach him to follow legal advice and recognize invitations to incriminate himself. Lawyers do the legal research and procedural work. His own contribution is persistence, family records, recollection, and practical observation. Reciprocal force Firearms His father taught him that pointing a weapon creates an obligation. Kyrien keeps the lesson as a personal rule: "You cannot do much in this world without life or death stakes. But if you dare to point a gun at someone, you should be prepared to be shot yourself." He uses firearms to create distance, interrupt an attack, or open an escape route. Mobility Motorcycle The only driving licence he ever wanted was for a motorcycle. He values the machine as a narrow, responsive escape tool that is harder to trap than a car, not as a leisure accessory. Last resort Survival combat Uses practical close combat and terrain awareness to remain mobile, evade a stronger opponent, or reach an escape route. Leadership Intelligence operations His unofficial MSF association gives him experience in surveillance, counterintelligence, and field planning. By Lynleit's disappearance, he can direct the agency's ordinary intelligence work while relying on Magi for its supernatural operations. Kyrien

entries.title: Lester: Biography
entries.subtitle: Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally
entries.text: Lester: Biography Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally Lester is a demiholumn, half human and half Holumn. Neither he nor Natalia knows how he became one. Chronological factors in his biography contradict continuity itself; his history cannot be reconciled into a conventional causal timeline. Understanding how he came into existence lies beyond the horizon of human singularity and normal human comprehension. He becomes Natalia's ally without becoming her employee. When one of her cases reaches an impossible barrier, his unusual nature can provide an answer that neither ordinary investigation nor conventional magecraft could reach. Lester's unusual abilities help Natalia with otherwise impossible cases. He also pushes back against her habit of examining him and notices when her attention becomes personal. His working relationship with Natalia develops sexual tension. Natalia comes to recognize contradiction as an intrinsic feature of nature, rather than treating his existence as an error in reality. His origin is not reducible to a discoverable transformation, experiment, infection, or ordinary supernatural mechanism. The limits of his abilities remain unknown. Lives as a demiholumn whose biography cannot form a continuous causal chronology. Helps Natalia without joining her business. Uses his unusual nature when her casework meets an impossible obstacle. Natalia recognizes his contradiction as intrinsic to nature, without explaining his origin. Lester

entries.title: Lester: Connections
entries.subtitle: Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally
entries.text: Lester: Connections Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally Natalia Natalia is his trusted investigator ally, not his employer. She calls on him when a case crosses the boundary between difficult and impossible. Their attraction grows through his refusal to remain only an object of her analysis and her increasing ability to see the man without ignoring the demiholumn condition. Classification Any institution that reduces him to either a human witness or a Holumn threat will misunderstand what he is and may decide that he cannot be allowed to remain free. Potential sexual tension Natalia Established tension Mutual, differently expressed Natalia's analytical distance gives Lester something unusually difficult to provoke. He enjoys forcing the reserved researcher into immediate experience, but the tension changes when he wants her attention to recognize the man rather than examine the demiholumn condition. Repeated cases bring Natalia's examination of Lester into conflict with his insistence on being treated as more than a case. He provokes her to act; she notices more than he expected. Their attraction does not answer her questions about his demiholumn nature. Neither knows how he came into existence. His chronology is intrinsically contradictory, not a solvable transformation history. Natalia's recognition that contradiction belongs to nature does not mean she can explain him completely or that attraction answers the contradiction. Lester

entries.title: Lester: Motivations
entries.subtitle: Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally
entries.text: Lester: Motivations Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally Help Natalia when ordinary methods fail while preserving the autonomy and secrecy of a life the hidden authorities may refuse to recognize. Lester

entries.title: Lester: Nature
entries.subtitle: Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally
entries.text: Lester: Nature Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally Classification Demiholumn Lester is half human and half Holumn. This is an inherent condition, not magecraft, a profession, or membership in Natalia's business. Known consequence The impossible becomes possible His part-Holumn nature sometimes allows him to accomplish things Natalia could not obtain through ordinary investigation or Magus practice. Unresolved boundary Human agency inside a Holumn nature Neither Lester nor Natalia knows the full extent or cost of his demiholumn nature. Lester

entries.title: Lester: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally
entries.text: Lester: Strengths and weaknesses Demiholumn and Natalia's outside ally Lester likes novelty, conflict, and finding out what happens when he gets involved. That appetite takes him into situations Natalia cannot reach through scholarship alone. His own history defeats both of them: its events cannot fit into one continuous chronology. Impossible intervention His part-Holumn nature can make an otherwise impossible task achievable for Natalia, although the mechanism and limits remain unknown. Outside ally He assists Natalia without joining her business. Natalia remains the sole employee of her office. Unclassified existence Neither the human nor Holumn half currently explains the whole person, leaving his place in the hidden world uncertain. ESTP strong Se Confirmed Lester

entries.title: Lynleit: Appearance
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Appearance Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Hair Very long, wavy ash-black hair with a side-parted fringe, most often worn loose. Eyes Bright cyan-blue. Height and build 169 cm, the same height as Helena; only Natalia is taller among the women. A longer, leaner silhouette with very attractive legs, elegant shins and ankles, stronger, well-shaped thighs, and a firm, rounded bottom she takes pride in. Her slender build retains these curves. Distinguishing features Pale complexion, refined angular features, expressive eyes, and a composed, quietly sensual gaze. A long tailored blue coat over a pale high-collared blouse with a narrow black ribbon, fitted high-waisted black shorts, dark tights, and black over-the-knee lace-up boots. Her wardrobe is formal and fashion-conscious. Midnight blue, black, white, cold cyan Belt equipment A special pair of black leather gloves is draped over her belt, usually concealed by the coat unless someone looks closely. Hair variation She occasionally wears her hair in a ponytail or bun. The bun becomes her usual working hairstyle in Arc 2 and is also worn during long report sessions and before sleep. Arc 2 elusive appearance In Arc 2, Lynleit wears her ash-black hair in a compact bun. She wears a high-necked black top beneath a short cape-like mantle, fitted black shorts, dark tights, gloves, over-the-knee lace-up boots, and a vivid blue sash at the waist. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Biography
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Biography Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Lynleit is associated with the Cult of Inanna through Fionn's lineage, without directly participating in it. She grew up close to MSF leadership. Felix and Reiner became her friends and the bodyguards Fionn trusted with her safety. At the Magi Academy, Natalia was her favourite teacher. She distrusted Helena before any open conspiracy, noticing her stepmother's questions about Fionn's schedules, visitors, trusted officers, and Lynleit's travel. At the Prosecutor General's appointment dinner, Kyrien's failed attack nearly harms her. She never tells him she attended. His represented interrogation reveals years of work paying lawyers and caring for his mother. She recognizes suppression behind his father's persecution and keeps that knowledge from him. Guilt, admiration of his competence, and her warning of approaching danger lead her to offer paid confidential service and limited help obtaining release. She tells only Felix and Reiner in her circle. After her mother's death, Lynleit resisted the family's move from Turon to Vilen and accepted it only on the condition that her study-bedroom occupy the third floor. The hillside site places thick trees close to the house and overlooks a river flowing toward the city center. Rustling leaves inspire her. She regards flowing water as life energy and seeks its emotional grounding despite her childhood fear of drowning. Days before Fionn's death, the Nameless Street leaves Lynleit with the memory of a dead boy below a broken fence. Seeing her father's body below the hill at the family house brings the memory back. Helena uses her stunned reaction to support the accusation that Lynleit killed him. Hunted and out of resources, Lynleit reaches Kyrien's hotel-room hideout. He helps her reconnect with Felix and Reiner. Fionn's old officers begin questioning Helena when Lynleit can answer his private recognition challenge and Helena cannot. During the river operation, the Drowned Choir drags Lynleit underwater and tears away her blue suede jacket. She burns the hands with blue flame, breaks the surface, and stands on the water. Kyrien sees her from the park bank. It is his first unmistakable exposure to magic; he tells nobody, and she initially only suspects what he saw. Father Mikhail later discovers that Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner know about magic. Lynleit insists on handling the breach herself. When the Church and Magiarchy send her to assist Mikhail in Cardiff, she sends Kyrien to help Myka at the Academy. She underestimates the danger there. In Cardiff, she and Mikhail protect one another despite their incompatible methods. Midway through Arc 1, after Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he replaced her coat with a leviathan-hide garment. Later in the second half of Arc 1, she and Kyrien survive a shared curse after an incomplete attempt at intimacy. She refuses to discuss it with him even after the curse is gone. Their sexual relationship begins later. Near the Arc 2 transition she disappears. She bears their son during her absence and keeps him hidden from Kyrien and the wider world while raising him, recovering, and seeking answers about the Spill. Years later she begins appearing around MSF missions without explaining her return. During Arc 2 they restore intimacy; this eventually leads to the conception and later birth of their daughter, their second child. Grows up as Fionn's daughter and studies magecraft under Natalia. Survives the Drowned Choir; Kyrien witnesses her walking on water. Assists Mikhail abroad without MSF's conventional resources. Sends Kyrien to help Myka while she is away. Helena blames her for Fionn's death. Escapes to Kyrien and reconnects with Felix and Reiner. Asks Kyrien why he keeps accepting danger without a promised reward. Survives a shared curse in the later part of Arc 1’s second half, after the hotel refuge. Exact placement remains open. Leaves near the Arc 2 transition to raise her son and investigate the Spill. Reappears around MSF operations without announcing her return. Development outline: continuing grief, a changing household, and school years before the main story. Months after Doom, private research and spontaneous closeness lead to a successful encounter in the park, before later intercourse. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Conflicts Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Helena's accusation She must recover allies inside the agency now hunting her. Forbidden witnesses Mikhail knows she disclosed magic to Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner. She insists on handling the breach herself. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Connections
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Connections Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Felix Long-standing friend and bodyguard Their friendship allows teasing, blunt correction, and easy physical familiarity. He and Reiner accompany her and Fionn on church visits. Felix repeatedly flirts with nuns while Reiner behaves, eventually exhausting her patience. When she catches him by his tie, he answers with a declaration of attention to her. She rejects his reading of the reprimand. Their son First child Born during Lynleit's disappearance and kept hidden from Kyrien and the wider world afterward. Their daughter Second child Conceived after intimacy is restored during Arc 2 and born later. Kyrien Strategic recruit and eventual partner She recruits him deliberately for strategic reasons, without anticipating their eventual closeness. Card games, shared work, and his protection of her water-walking secret bring private familiarity. He shelters her after Fionn's death and chooses to remain when she can no longer compel him. Her initiative, pride, and curiosity meet his reserve and close observation. Gradually each allows the other to notice what they would usually conceal, and quiet companionship becomes important without displacing her duties. Natalia Favourite teacher and friend Lynleit jokes with Natalia, challenges her conclusions, and readily returns to her for help. She follows her explanations with a student's curiosity rather than a subordinate's deference. Natalia taught her at the Magi Academy, later asks her to help Myka, and identifies ego transformation as a possible way to survive the shared curse. Father Mikhail Cardiff counterpart and theological adviser The Magiarchy and Church send Lynleit to assist Mikhail abroad. They protect one another despite a moral rift, and he later finds related cases in Church records and proposes reciprocal identity change as a possible way out of the shared curse. His mock blessing names her lineage's association with the Cult of Inanna. She objects to his use of family history as a personal obligation and threatens a reprisal if he repeats the address publicly. Kyrien Kyrien's failed attack nearly harms her, but she never tells him. Their coerced alliance acquires a private familiarity through card games and shared work. He keeps her water-walking secret, shelters her after Fionn's murder, and chooses to stay when he could leave. An incomplete attempt at intimacy ends their shared curse; her embarrassment and his unanswered questions outlast it. Helena Lynleit distrusts her stepmother before the takeover, then learns Helena played a major role in Fionn's assassination even though the full conspiracy remains unclear. Potential sexual tension Kyrien Established arc Mutual, slow to surface Lynleit studies Kyrien first as a recruit whose failed attack nearly harmed her. Their card games make that scrutiny personal: she learns his tells and begins noticing his hands and breath. Later she attempts intimacy as a possible treatment for their shared curse, but remains interested after they survive without completing it. Mikhail's mock blessing exposes her family association with the Cult of Inanna. She counters with abstract principles and increasingly personal objections. His teasing does not create her attraction to Kyrien or make ancestry a reason for it. In the park, she wants to correct her private sense of failure, then finds satisfaction in knowing Kyrien as a particular person. Her theory follows an impulse already present. The preparation remains theoretical. Her attention shifts from proving competence toward learning his individual responses; the current park draft leaves that passage for the author rather than depicting it. Recruitment remains antagonistic: Kyrien's legal campaign and care obligations make paid work and release support materially important. Lynleit's concern for his mother coexists with leverage and concealed anger. Neither his agreement nor her guilt establishes attraction. The interrogation, card games, protected secret, and voluntary decision to stay give this pairing different kinds of familiarity. In Doom Has an Address, an incomplete attempt at intimacy breaks the shared curse. Lynleit loses the excuse of treatment without losing her interest in Kyrien; he is left trying to understand what happened. Their sexual relationship begins later in Arc 1. Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge precede Doom. Months afterward, a spontaneous park encounter lets Lynleit's curiosity and wounded pride become a successful private milestone. Oral intimacy, reciprocal exploration, first intercourse, and pregnancy remain separate. The family theme does not turn ancestry into an instruction or make grief itself attraction. Lynleit bears their son during her disappearance and later keeps him hidden from both Kyrien and the wider world. They restore intimacy during Arc 2 and eventually conceive a second child, a daughter, who is born later. The daughter's conception becomes apparent only after Arc 2, not within it. The author has confirmed this direction, not the scenes that restore intimacy or the timing of Kyrien's discovery of their son. Duty remains primary; a second child does not substitute for the work of reconnection. Their connected dream in The Shared Night remains unspecified. Develop a nonsexual, painful or emotionally exposing experience that draws them closer unintentionally; childhood disclosures are a possibility, not established history. Preserve the later physical milestones. Potential sexual tension Felix Established asymmetry Felix overt, Lynleit deflecting Felix's flirting belongs to a long friendship she refuses to reorganize around his advances. Her ease with him, combined with the repeated refusal, creates visible chemistry without requiring matching sexual intent. Only Eyes for You develops a recurring problem during Lynleit and Fionn's church visits, with Felix and Reiner accompanying them. Reiner behaves, while Felix repeatedly flirts with nuns until Lynleit loses patience. He answers her eventual reprimand with 'I only have eyes for you.' The author identifies accumulated irritation as the comic cause, not jealousy. His reply redirects an objection he does not want to answer; it does not make her objection romantic. His wider flirting coexists with his persistent fixation on Lynleit and does not establish an attachment to any particular nun. The visits precede Fionn's death, but their exact placement and relation to his growing closeness with Sherie remain open. Sherie's 'Looks like you two have unresolved tension' in the card-game interlude is her teasing interpretation, not confirmation that Lynleit reciprocates. Felix's distraction by Sherie coexists with the same unresolved attachment. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Equipment
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Equipment Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Magecraft protection Black leather gloves Belt-carried Blue-flame protection A special pair of black leather gloves hangs over Lynleit's belt, usually concealed by her coat. She relies on them during blue-flame outbursts: exposed skin can be damaged or scarred. When putting on one glove for blue flame, she rolls up the corresponding sleeve to keep her clothes from catching fire; with both gloves, she rolls up both sleeves. She covers a nearby victim separately, first using their jacket and, if necessary, her own coat. items.html?item=lynleits-protective-gloves Issued sidearm Ren L17 "Sparrow" 9×17 mm Leather OWB holster Right-handed draw Lynleit carries the compact Sparrow in a snug leather outside-the-waistband holster centered just above her tailbone. A rightward cant lets her draw with her right hand. The pistol's small proportions and the long jackets or coats central to her wardrobe keep it concealed without disturbing her usual silhouette. weapons.html#ren-l17-sparrow Later loan Ren L21 "Rook" 9×19 mm Borrowed from Felix Micro-compact Felix later lends Lynleit his personal L21 after her continued preference for the weaker 9×17 Sparrow becomes a cause of concern for him. The Rook gives her a lighter polymer-frame pistol in the more common 9×19 mm cartridge. weapons.html#ren-l21-rook Inherited protection Leviathan-hide coat Autonomous form Minor magical protection Active coverage required Midway through Arc 1, after Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he had discreetly replaced her blue coat with a garment sewn from material called the hide of leviathan. The coat chooses whether to appear as a coat, scarf, an imitation of her lost suede jacket, or another piece of clothing. Its protection does not activate merely because she wears it. She must cover the threatened part of her body or place the garment over someone else. items.html?item=leviathan-hide-coat Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Magecraft
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Magecraft Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Hereditary magecraft Blue flame Lynleit inherited her family's ability to manifest blue flame. It can be directed into many applications, but her control is less subtle than Fionn's. Her protective gloves prevent routine burns; careless exposure risks skin damage and scarring. The office-building rescue leaves her hands unburned but costs her a nosebleed, a split lip and tremors, with recovery expected within days. Natural tendency Unsafe volume Where Fionn relies on virtuosity and precision, Lynleit has the nerve to call forth far more flame than is safe. Force comes more readily to her than finesse. Irreplaceable force Beyond ordinary weapons Blue flame becomes indispensable when normal firearms cannot finish the threat: an immortal or rapidly regenerating Holumn, a body that moves without being alive, or a barrier that conventional force cannot breach. Accidental miracle-making Walking on water This ability appeared independently of her inherited magecraft. It manifested from her childhood fear of drowning and allows her to cross the surface of water on foot. Its resemblance to a sacred miracle places it outside tolerated magecraft. Strictly concealed Night practice Lynleit keeps the talent secret from everyone because the Church strongly punishes miracle-making that imitates acts associated with Jesus, saints, saviours, and other sacred figures, even when the effect seems harmless. She practices alone at night on secluded stretches of local lakes and rivers. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Motivations
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Motivations Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Reclaim MSF from Helena, protect the people in her care, and investigate the Spill. During her later absence, she also keeps her son outside the conflict. Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Strengths and weaknesses Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir Lynleit puts MSF and her own missions first. She shares her thinking with the people she leads. When uncertain, she feels there is an answer even though she cannot yet explain it. Talking to someone she trusts helps bring it into focus; she tries not to show how much the uncertainty troubles her. In private she is reserved and reflective. Personal embarrassment makes her evasive or irritable, especially when Kyrien notices it. Mikhail gets formal objections, sharp retorts, and eventually a carefully worded threat. The Shared Night She and Kyrien share a dream whose particulars they do not recount in the briefing. Natalia catches her repeating a lesson as an independent conclusion. Relational leadership 95 She treats candid communication as a source of trust and coordinated action. A trusted objection can unsettle her even when a plan is working, making her question whether she pushed for something others were uncomfortable with. Strategic foresight 92 An unresolved sense that something is wrong can prevent her from fully committing to a plan. Trusted reassurance sometimes helps her proceed, but does not settle the unease; she may postpone without being able to explain why. Private introspection 86 In private she is comfortable disappearing into solitude, following symbolic threads, and processing difficult emotion internally. INFJ Ni-led reading; strong Fe Suspected Lynleit

entries.title: Lynleit: Tradecraft
entries.subtitle: Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir
entries.text: Lynleit: Tradecraft Fionn's biological daughter and displaced heir The office-building rescue Test what remains usable She tests a coin, painted edges, door fittings and moving air instead of trusting floor numbers. Her small silver Sparrow and spare magazine buy time but do not finish the pursuer. Once empty, the pistol becomes a thrown distraction. She brings the witness out and gives the Church as little to discuss openly in his presence as possible. Physical aptitude Agility Lynleit is somewhat more agile and nimble than the average woman. Immediate danger Physical survival She is generally competent at keeping herself alive under imminent physical threat. Lynleit

entries.title: Myka: Biography
entries.subtitle: Magi Academy student
entries.text: Myka: Biography Magi Academy student Myka studies at the Magi Academy and keeps in regular contact with her aunt Natalia, a former professor. She asks her for help with studies and personal problems; Natalia checks on her and sometimes treats her like a daughter. Myka encounters terrors inside the Academy and must rely on Natalia for rescue and support. Natalia asks Lynleit for help, but Lynleit is being sent to Cardiff and dispatches Kyrien as her substitute. The threat turns formal study into a struggle for survival inside an institution meant to train and protect young Magi. Kyrien enters the Academy as a non-Magus undercover helper and keeps Myka safe through conventional field skills and communications with Felix and Reiner. The danger exceeds Lynleit's estimate and forces Natalia to intervene personally. This becomes Myka's first direct experience with Kyrien and MSF. Myka survives the Academy crisis and graduates at the top of her class. Her experience with Kyrien contributes to her later decision to join MSF as a Magus. Studies at the Academy and seeks advice from Natalia. Faces dangers she cannot resolve within the institution. Receives help from Kyrien and later Natalia. Survives and graduates at the top of her class. Joins the agency after her experience with Kyrien. Myka

entries.title: Natalia: Biography
entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Biography Independent magical examiner and private investigator Natalia earned a professorship at the Magi Academy as a talented Magus and serious researcher. Lynleit studied under her during those years and remembers Natalia as her favourite teacher. Natalia eventually found academic life too constraining: the institution could support scholarship, but it also defined which questions were respectable and how far an inquiry was permitted to go. She resigned to continue her work independently. Natalia opens a private-investigation business to pay for her independent research. Her knowledge of Magi and magecraft attracts clients whose problems ordinary investigators cannot handle. Her one-woman office now sits between a detective agency, consultation room, and private laboratory. Clients bring suspected crimes, unstable talents, personal deviations, and magical problems they cannot safely expose. Natalia examines the person and phenomenon before deciding whether a crime has occurred at all. Lester repeatedly forces her to distinguish professional fascination with his demiholumn condition from personal attention to him. When Myka encounters terrors inside the Academy, Natalia becomes her principal source of advice, rescue, and support beyond the institution. She asks her former student Lynleit for help, then intervenes personally when the danger exceeds the protection Kyrien can provide. Natalia's work repeatedly brings her into contact with Lester. Her interest in him becomes personal as well as professional. Helping Myka renews her work with Lynleit and introduces her niece to Kyrien and MSF. Neither Natalia nor Lester knows how he became a demiholumn. She comes to recognize his contradictory chronology as an intrinsic feature of nature, without reconciling it into an ordinary causal history. Teaches Lynleit at the Magi Academy. Resigns to pursue research independently. Takes investigative and examination work to fund it. Intervenes when Kyrien can no longer contain the danger to Myka. Identifies transformation as an alternative to the shared curse's fatal solution. Works with Lester as an independent ally. Natalia

entries.title: Natalia: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Conflicts Independent magical examiner and private investigator Institutional interference The Academy, Magiarchy, and Church can restrict her inquiries or claim her cases. Natalia

entries.title: Natalia: Connections
entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Connections Independent magical examiner and private investigator Lester Outside ally and source of tension Lester remains outside the business, but his demiholumn nature sometimes carries Natalia past barriers that scholarship and ordinary investigation cannot cross. Their attraction develops along the boundary between examination and being personally seen. Myka Niece, student, and friend Natalia keeps constant contact with her niece at the Magi Academy. Myka asks for advice on her studies, Natalia checks on her life, and their bond often resembles mother and daughter as much as aunt and niece. Lynleit Former student and friend Natalia teaches through examples Lynleit can work through, including her own failed approaches. Lynleit teases her, offers playful objections, and trusts her enough to keep asking difficult questions. Their friendship is informal; Natalia's greater experience remains evident in the corrections and connections Lynleit learns from her. They work together over Myka's danger and the curse Lynleit shares with Kyrien. Lester Lester is not her employee. He is an outside ally and a demiholumn whose part-Holumn nature sometimes allows him to accomplish what should be impossible for an ordinary investigator. Their repeated work carries sexual tension because her effort to understand him cannot remain entirely separate from personal attention. Institutional capture The Academy, Magiarchy, and Church can each narrow an inquiry by deciding which questions are permissible, which cases belong to them, and which answers must remain hidden. Potential sexual tension Lester Established tension Mutual, differently expressed Lester is the living exception that Natalia cannot finish classifying. Her professional attention can become personal before she recognizes the change, especially when he interrupts an examination by noticing that she is watching him rather than the phenomenon around him. Repeated cases bring Natalia's examination of Lester into conflict with his insistence on being treated as more than a case. He provokes her to act; she notices more than he expected. Their attraction does not answer her questions about his demiholumn nature. Neither knows how he came into existence. His chronology is intrinsically contradictory, not a solvable transformation history. Natalia's recognition that contradiction belongs to nature does not mean she can explain him completely or that attraction answers the contradiction. Natalia

entries.title: Natalia: Motivations
entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Motivations Independent magical examiner and private investigator Fund and protect an independent life of magical research while giving clients an answer before hidden authorities reduce their problem to jurisdiction, secrecy, or punishment. Natalia

entries.title: Natalia: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Independent magical examiner and private investigator
entries.text: Natalia: Strengths and weaknesses Independent magical examiner and private investigator Natalia investigates private cases to pay for the research she wants to do. She left the Academy rather than keep asking permission to pursue it. When explaining a difficult idea, she reaches for an example or something she tried herself, including the attempts that failed. She asks her listener to try the next step and enjoys a good objection. Lynleit gets the lesson and the teasing of a former student who is still her friend. Natalia admits where her evidence runs out. The Shared Night In The Shared Night she compares independent reports and resists treating dream acts as confessions. Her work on complexes, dreams and magical pathology leads her to consider weakened inhibition, a shared imaginal field and the Holumn's selective pressure as competing explanations. Independent scholarship She resigned from the Academy when its environment became too restrictive for the questions and methods she wanted to pursue. Magical examination She examines unusual magecraft and personal deviations closely, studying the affected person as well as the circumstances of the incident. Selective casework The business has one employee: Natalia. Paid cases finance her research and let her choose which clients, risks, and secrets enter her office. Identity analysis When Lynleit and Kyrien inherit a shared curse, Natalia introduces the ego hypothesis and quotes Jung. A two-name diagram helps Lynleit follow its paired attachment; Natalia's own research mistakes distinguish a changed self-description from a change in decisions. She cannot measure the degree of transformation the curse requires. INTP strong Ti Confirmed Natalia

entries.title: Reiner: Biography
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Reiner: Biography MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Reiner is Lynleit's long-standing friend and one of the MSF officers Fionn trusts as her personal bodyguards. They also spend time together outside assignments. Lynleit reveals her secret recruitment of Kyrien only to Reiner and Felix, withholding it even from Fionn. Reiner sees the same danger Felix sees, particularly whenever neither bodyguard is near her, but recognizes that rejecting the plan would also mean rejecting Lynleit's judgment. Reiner accepts Lynleit's decision to recruit Kyrien despite the breach of protocol. His vote leaves Felix in the minority. He continues watching Kyrien. Reiner's trust does not eliminate scrutiny. After Fionn's murder and the hunt for Lynleit's arrest, Kyrien helps her contact Reiner and Felix from hiding. Reiner must protect her, preserve the covert link inside Helena's MSF, and decide how far disciplined loyalty can support the effort to reclaim the agency. Serves alongside Lynleit as a friend and trusted bodyguard. Learns she recruited Kyrien without Fionn's knowledge. Supports her decision despite his reservations. Keeps Kyrien under scrutiny while helping Lynleit. Reiner

entries.title: Reiner: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Reiner: Conflicts MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Trust and protocol Supporting Lynleit's secret recruitment means accepting a breach he would ordinarily oppose. Reiner

entries.title: Reiner: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Reiner: Strengths and weaknesses MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Reiner is stern and rarely smiles. He follows procedure, respects the chain of command, and takes duty and legitimate authority seriously. A small break in his composure is conspicuous beside Felix's constant play. In the field he commits to the direct line: the rook that holds a position or breaks through it. The Shared Night He questions how closely the dream accounts agree and watches the increasingly embarrassing briefing. Protocol-focused He treats procedure as accumulated operational knowledge and notices quickly when others disregard it. Severe composure Reiner is restrained, difficult to fluster, and rarely seen smiling even among people he trusts. When he and Felix accompany Lynleit and Fionn to churches, Reiner behaves appropriately while Felix keeps flirting with the nuns. Reliable protection He expresses friendship through preparation, consistency, and remaining exactly where Lynleit needs him to be. ISTJ strong Si-Te Confirmed Reiner

entries.title: Reiner: Tradecraft
entries.subtitle: MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard
entries.text: Reiner: Tradecraft MSF officer, friend, and personal bodyguard Direct action Brute-force intervention Reiner specializes in situations where an obstacle must be confronted directly, relying on physical power, discipline, and decisive commitment. Physical security Close protection His build and composure make him the stable physical barrier in Lynleit's security detail, able to hold position when an operation becomes chaotic. Operational geometry Rook pattern He controls clear lines, anchors a position, and applies force without unnecessary movement. Reiner is most effective when the threat has nowhere left to hide.
