entries.title: Sherie: Biography
entries.subtitle: Diplomat in training and covert negotiator
entries.text: Sherie: Biography Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Sherie studies diplomacy under her uncle Drake. She is quicker at reading a room and drawing people into conversation than he is. She is not a Magus and begins without knowledge of magic. Drake's peers ridicule his warning and the Duke remains skeptical. Sherie believes her uncle, but rejects his decision to remain inside official limits and begins designing her own approach to Lynleit. Sherie develops the unauthorized approach to Lynleit against Drake's wishes, persuades him to attend, and leads the negotiations herself. After it succeeds, she asks him to praise and pamper her. Sherie and Drake use the private agreement to ask Lynleit for a loyal team capable of covertly inspecting apparently unmanned night shipments on the Vilen river. She seeks evidence about the suspected coup; what the officers discover does not yet become her knowledge. Trains under her uncle Drake. Proposes approaching Lynleit outside official channels. Conducts the hilltop negotiation despite Drake's reluctance. Requests the river inspection with Drake. Sherie

entries.title: Sherie: Conflicts
entries.subtitle: Diplomat in training and covert negotiator
entries.text: Sherie: Conflicts Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Unauthorized agreement Her private approach to MSF would be stopped if the Court or government discovered it. The cost of persuasion She enjoys making attraction useful and can keep playing while consequences grow beyond what she understands. Reading a response well does not tell her what the other person will do afterward. Uneven attachment Felix becomes increasingly important to her while remaining fixated on Lynleit. Sherie has limits to what attention she will accept; she wants to be seen clearly, not simply enjoyed as a diversion. Sherie

entries.title: Sherie: Connections
entries.subtitle: Diplomat in training and covert negotiator
entries.text: Sherie: Connections Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Felix Growing familiarity They have no meaningful personal relationship at the story's opening. Her diplomatic work increasingly overlaps with his duties around Lynleit and MSF. Repeated encounters bring respect, private jokes, and affection. Sherie enjoys directing their exchanges; Felix teases back and complicates her control. His continued fixation on Lynleit can hurt, even as he seeks Sherie's company. Her confidence does not spare her disappointment or doubts about whether he sees her clearly. During a card game she catches him looking at her while he complains about Lynleit. She leaves her legs stretched along the sofa and begins enjoying his distraction. At first she enjoys catching his attention; later she wants him to seek her out without an invitation. She can hear his distraction without knowing its cause, while he sometimes catches what she hides inside an amusing account. Eventually she refuses to spend their private time accommodating his hopes about Lynleit. She does not seek a formal partnership. Their intimacy stays private, with cards and rematches acquiring meanings only they share. She trusts his discretion and enjoys his particular humor and resistance; afterward she can return to tea and tomorrow's work without a solemn declaration. Drake Her uncle, mentor, and strategic counterpart. He trains her for diplomacy, while her charm and quick mind carry them through situations his social skills cannot. Official oversight The government and Ducal Court would end the partnership if either discovered it. Potential sexual tension Kyrien Strong potential Situational and confrontational Kyrien's refusal to be steered threatens a skill she has internalized as part of her identity. Each failed attempt to produce a reaction can make his eventual attention feel more valuable and personally dangerous. Sherie uses language and calibrated flirtation to control the rhythm of an exchange. Kyrien answers with silence, literalism, or no usable reaction at all. Repeated negotiation could turn her professional frustration into sexual tension without making them compatible or displacing Kyrien's eventual relationship with Lynleit. Potential sexual tension Felix Author-confirmed direction Private games, mutual trust and uneven attachment Sherie enjoys directing an exchange, while Felix teases back and complicates her control. As their work repeatedly overlaps, she finds room to become theatrical, petty, ridiculous, or openly delighted without losing his respect. She may recognize their intimate potential before he does. His fixation on Lynleit can hurt despite his responsive attention; her confidence does not remove disappointment, boundaries, or doubt about whether he sees her clearly. She gradually recognizes the seriousness beneath his jokes and becomes someone around whom he need not always entertain. Social play is something she enjoys off duty too. An unexpected response makes her attend to the emotional change in Felix and in the exchange, without guaranteeing that she understands its cause. In Unresolved Tension, the author favors comfort preceding calculated display: reclining is initially ordinary to Sherie. She notices Felix's pause and glance, then chooses not to change her position. Enjoying his response can come before understanding her own interest. Her enjoyment of catching his attention acquires a new concern: whether he seeks her out unprompted. She can hear his distraction without understanding it, and he can surprise her by noticing what she has concealed in an amusing account. Eventually she refuses to spend their private time accommodating his hopes about Lynleit; the timing and his response still need scenes. She does not seek a formal relationship. Reputation, diplomatic work and divided loyalties make discretion valuable, but she chooses Felix for his humor, resistance and familiarity, not merely his availability. Her confidence comes from observation and quick adaptation; limited prior experience remains possible. Learning his particular responses gives her private pride, while practical mistakes still give her something to learn. She can return to cards, tea and tomorrow's work almost immediately afterward. In The Shared Night, her anger includes being witnessed and discovering that Felix suspected their shared experience before telling her. When the pressure eases, she steps away and keeps the no-kissing boundary. She enjoys him but tries to minimize emotional entanglement, protect professional stability and keep their gradually sexual connection plausibly deniable. His dependency on her would be dangerous; her dependency on him would alarm her still more. They have no meaningful personal relationship at the story's opening. Sherie's diplomatic responsibilities increasingly overlap with Felix's work around Lynleit and MSF, bringing repeated encounters before either chooses closeness. Familiarity, respect, private jokes, and a compatible rhythm develop gradually. Her confident, playful dominance meets his expressiveness, improvisation, and willingness to challenge her. Humor, visible enjoyment, mutual provocation, and occasional reversals carry into affection and eventual adult intimacy. Care becomes particularly revealing when one stops performing and the other remains attentive. Readers can notice Felix building intimacy's foundations with Sherie while still imagining it with Lynleit; narration need not explain that contradiction. The later teasing challenge to Lynleit remains, but it neither starts their familiarity nor reduces Sherie's interest to winning him. This differs from Lynleit's strategic recruitment of Kyrien and their quieter recognition through restrained attention, protected secrets, and gradually accepted vulnerability. Both couples remain subplots beneath the political and supernatural story. Unresolved Tension supplies an early card-game scene draft and a linked panel sequence. Her observation about Felix and Lynleit, his denial, her 'Mm,' and the final unanswered 'Like what?' let a second, less acknowledged attraction enter the conversation. The cards give them an ordinary shared activity; no game, stakes, winner, room owner, or numbered phase is established. The Shared Night now preserves their no-kissing boundary after recovered choice; precise chronology remains unplaced. Their diplomatic and MSF obligations can produce substantive disagreements that attraction cannot settle. Establish ordinary company, especially her voice in his communications work, before a separation or dangerous assignment makes a delayed reply frightening. A failed familiar joke, reciprocal care, or a voluntary decision to stay can convey the later weight without extinguishing their pleasure. The particular disputes, danger, and separation remain unwritten; tragedy is not required. A restrained early musical motif may return with more space and unresolved harmony as a composition direction, not an assigned recording. Their later intimacy is a private, deniable game rather than a conventional formal romance. Cards, rematches and tactics acquire meanings only they share; "nothing happened" accumulates trust, embarrassment, tenderness and private history. Her rapid return to ordinary conversation can surprise him. "You're safe" names the freedom she finds with him, not a guarantee against disappointment. The early discovery encounter is author-directed but not drafted or dated. Its mechanics remain off-page. This later code must not be read back into the early card-game scene as an established habit. Sherie's Kyrie Eleison direction places a serious eventual reckoning beyond her enjoyment of manipulative social games. The particular catastrophe is undecided, and Felix is not assigned as its victim, cause or savior. Their genuine affection and trust remain; her wider mistakes must not turn every private exchange into a calculated exploitation. She starts without knowledge of magic, and her personal theme is not automatically their shared relationship motif. The Shared Night is a canonical encounter with draft dialogue and unassigned placement. Compelled dream activity cannot establish a preference or desire. Their familiar provocations persist, but acknowledging their enjoyment of one another helps restore a gap between impulse and action. Sherie steps away when she can. She does not kiss Felix in or outside dreams. Her intention is a stable, professional, plausibly deniable connection with minimized emotional dependency, not a formal romance. This contrasts with the unintended emotional closeness proposed for Lynleit and Kyrien's nonsexual dream. Sherie

entries.title: Sherie: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Diplomat in training and covert negotiator
entries.text: Sherie: Strengths and weaknesses Diplomat in training and covert negotiator Sherie teases and provokes mischief even off duty. She is quick to read someone's mood, relationships, and standing in a group; an unexpected reply makes her reconsider the exchange she thought she understood. She can draw out information without making a person feel interrogated and keep a difficult conversation going. She also enjoys using beauty, attraction and psychological pressure to influence people, sometimes trusting her ability to manage the consequences too far. With Felix she can be theatrical, petty, ridiculous, or openly delighted without losing his respect. As she gets to know him, she also learns when his jokes conceal something serious. The Shared Night She discovers that Felix remembers the intimate dreams she thought private. When choice returns, she steps away and keeps their no-kissing agreement. They arrange coffee afterward. She enjoys his company while trying to keep their gradually sexual connection stable, professional and plausibly deniable; she fears dependency in either direction. By the briefing she knows about Holumns, though her first discovery is not recorded. Social play She enjoys teasing and provoking mischief even when nobody needs to be persuaded or impressed. Quietness usually means she feels unwell or uncomfortable. Emotional attention An unexpected response draws her attention to what changed in the person and in the atmosphere of the whole exchange. Persuasive judgment A useful agreement reached for the wrong reason feels like a success she cannot safely repeat. She may joke that she failed successfully while reconsidering her understanding of the other person. ENFJ strong Fe Confirmed Sherie

entries.text: Tien: Biography Mercenary assassin and secret bodyguard Helena secretly hires Tien, a professional mercenary and assassin, as her bodyguard and to remove her enemies. Helena deploys Tien against Lynleit and Kyrien as MSF's internal conflict leaves official channels behind. Tien and Kyrien become direct operational rivals because both begin as concealed assets serving handlers with opposing interests. Their functions overlap, but Tien exists primarily to remove Helena's enemies quietly and cleanly. His covert work for Helena puts him in repeated opposition to Kyrien. Works as a mercenary and assassin. Becomes Helena's concealed bodyguard. Opposes Kyrien during the struggle over MSF. Continues removing threats to Helena. Tien

entries.title: Yulia: Biography
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Biography Criminology student and procedural investigator Yulia and Hiyu study criminology at the same university. She stands at the top of the class through discipline, detail, and command of established method, while Hiyu makes his reputation through personal investigations that ignore the path everyone else was taught to follow. Their interaction is often painful to observe: he chases another possibility, she develops another headache, and neither notices how accustomed they are becoming to the other's company. Hiyu concludes that magic may be involved in the park disappearances despite not knowing that magic actually exists. Yulia considers the theory absurd, but joins his attempt to enter the quarantine partly to prove him wrong and partly because she does not trust him to remain safe alone. Inside the park, Yulia's meticulous observation remains valuable, but ordinary criminological protocol cannot tell her what rules the environment follows. Her attachment to Hiyu becomes a second vulnerability because protecting him can pull her deeper into a danger neither of them understands. Their original aversion gradually becomes dependence and then unacknowledged romantic tension. Yulia refuses to name it, while Hiyu remains so absorbed in ideas that he does not understand why her company has become necessary to him. Excels at criminology through careful method. Accompanies Hiyu to challenge his theory and keep him safe. Encounters events her training cannot explain. Becomes increasingly attached to Hiyu despite their disagreements. Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Connections
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Connections Criminology student and procedural investigator Hiyu Her opposite in method and temperament. He generates possibilities she would never entertain, while she gives his ideas evidentiary discipline. Over time, irritation becomes an attachment neither understands clearly. An investigation without rules Yulia can master a known procedure, but the park confronts her with evidence whose governing categories have not yet been admitted to exist. Potential sexual tension Hiyu Emerging arc Mutual, unequally conscious Hiyu irritates her into sustained attention. She keeps arguing, correcting, and following because his ideas have already occupied more of her mind than she wants to admit. Suppressed attraction can sharpen both her impatience and her awareness of his physical presence. A possible scene has them lean over the same evidence or reach for the same document while arguing. Yulia notices their proximity first; Hiyu continues the theory. Another possible beat has him keep turning toward her usual place while investigating alone. These are staging suggestions for their established attraction arc, not completed encounters or an established sexual relationship. Her objections must remain genuine, and the investigation must still matter. Yulia

entries.text: Yulia: Motivations Criminology student and procedural investigator Keep Hiyu alive, test his impossible theory honestly, and preserve enough reliable evidence to understand what ordinary criminology cannot explain. Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Strengths and weaknesses
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Strengths and weaknesses Criminology student and procedural investigator Yulia is reliable, meticulous, and most comfortable with evidence she can test against an established procedure. Hiyu's eureka moments give her a headache. She follows him anyway, checking his leaps and having to consider possibilities her usual methods would exclude. Procedural rigor She is at the top of her criminology class because she applies method consistently, respects chains of evidence, and notices when a required step has been skipped. Detail verification Yulia is strongest when a theory must be tested against the record, an observation must be preserved accurately, or an exciting conclusion must survive patient scrutiny. Reluctant loyalty She complains, resists, and wishes she were elsewhere, yet still goes with Hiyu when leaving him alone would place him in greater danger. ISTJ strong Si Confirmed Yulia

entries.title: Yulia: Tradecraft
entries.subtitle: Criminology student and procedural investigator
entries.text: Yulia: Tradecraft Criminology student and procedural investigator Academic strength Classical criminological method Yulia follows evidence handling, observation, reconstruction, and procedural discipline with a consistency Hiyu does not naturally possess. Team function Verification and correction She tests Hiyu's intuitive threads, separates useful anomalies from noise, and gives their investigations a record another person could actually follow. Failure condition Procedure without precedent The quarantined park is especially dangerous because its supernatural conditions do not respect the categories or safety assumptions on which her strongest methods depend. Yulia

entries.title: Arc 0: Households and the Becoming of MSF · v1
entries.subtitle: Prequel Development
entries.text: Arc 0: Households and the Becoming of MSF · v1 Prequel Development A tentative, Fionn-centered prequel outline: changing households, school years, MSF, and the younger cast’s unfinished habits. Arc 0: Households and the Becoming of MSF Status and scope This is a tentative prequel direction, not a fixed chronology or a completed account of MSF's founding. Arc 0 is a separate life period centered on Fionn, his household, and the development of MSF. The younger cast's high-school years provide parallel formation stories beneath that adult narrative. Exact dates, ages, institutional milestones, and school arrangements remain undecided. The Arc 0 outline collects its sparse scene anchor. No separate prequel Chapter is established yet. Fionn's story Fionn needs objectives, friendships, political obligations, weaknesses, and decisions that do not exist solely to explain his daughter. Follow him as a widower, father, professional, political actor, and man able to love again. His remarriage and his work should affect each other through concrete pressures rather than parallel exposition. MSF should become recognizable through people solving immediate problems. Temporary arrangements, practical necessity, threats, institutional failures, loyalties, and compromises may harden into lasting practices. Do not assign a founding date, invent a precursor organization, or assume that nothing called MSF existed before these years. The distinction between founding and later restructuring needs an author decision. Two households Lynleit, Fionn, and Helena Lynleit's mother died while she was still a junior schooler. The move from Turon to Vilen and her third-floor condition retain that existing chronology. Arc 0 can explore the continuing grief during her teenage years without moving the death or relocation into high school. The proposed domestic arc follows a household rebuilding after loss. Helena's arrival changes meals, seating, schedules, private conversations, rooms, and who can interrupt Fionn. Lynleit may understand that Helena cannot replace her mother while reacting as though a familiar gesture has erased something. Her fear concerns memory as much as possession of her father's attention. Let Helena genuinely give Fionn companionship. Lynleit then has to recognize a legitimate place for someone she resents. An apology, accepting help, or admitting Helena was right are possible scenes, not established events. Do not rewrite Helena's later actions as inevitable from her first entrance. Ordinary father-daughter familiarity matters: a late meal, an argument about school, waiting while he works, a manipulation he recognizes immediately, or discovering that he does not know an answer. Not every conversation needs a lesson or a later callback. Kyrien and his family The proposed teenage arc gives Kyrien a mother and sister whom he tries to protect after his father's death. Their names, ages, circumstances, and present-day status remain open. Show their ordinary life before the loss: meals, arguments, unwanted chores, jokes, and someone expecting him home. His father's death makes lineage a practical burden before he has the resources or authority to carry it. Money, legal standing, inherited danger, dismissive officials, and relatives are candidate pressures, not confirmed incidents. His mother and sister must retain their own judgment and sometimes reject his interference. The useful conflict is between responsibility and actual capacity. Accepting help, listening, or standing down can cost him more pride than a fight. Institutions may include people acting reasonably who still cannot help his family. Avoid making either solitary defiance or official procedure a universal answer. Adolescence and developing habits Young Lynleit should make mistakes her adult self has learned to hide. Curiosity, political awareness, competitiveness, family privilege, immature manipulation, and visible grief may coexist. Young Kyrien can be easier to read, angrier, more trusting, and quicker to mistake determination for resources. Neither is the finished adult in school clothes. The proposed contrast is specific: Lynleit learns to keep important people near after loss; Kyrien learns to function when alone. Proximity can support loyalty or become possessiveness. Independence can support survival or make help difficult to accept. These are development directions to test in scenes, not explanations for every adult action. Kyrien's whiskey flask is established adult equipment. Arc 0 may explore its beginnings through his father, an older relative, imitation, inheritance, or a difficult night. None of these origins is selected. The habit may begin awkwardly and become a measured private ritual. Do not depict alcohol as medical treatment or as the source of his competence. School and the ensemble Use classmates, family backgrounds, examinations, rivalries, meals, clubs, and ordinary boredom to make the younger ensemble socially alive. Do not assign all current characters to the same school or generation. Kyrien's later introduction to the Magi world remains intact: magical schooling and doctrine belong to characters who already have access to them, not automatically to him. For young Magi, lessons, exercises, history, doctrine, and unequal access to training can show how their institutions describe themselves. Teachers may be sincere yet transmit omissions or mistaken assumptions. A lesson is evidence of what students were taught, not automatic confirmation of the world's underlying truth. Talent should create expectations and mistakes as well as prestige. Friendships and rivalries may change without every classmate becoming an important enemy. Warmth, adolescent certainty, humor, family affection, and small victories should coexist with class, political pressure, magical privilege, and threats the adults cannot always contain. Optional forgotten encounter A brief teenage encounter between Lynleit and Kyrien remains optional. A waiting room, station, shop, school event, or corridor could let two exhausted adolescents irritate each other and inadvertently challenge a defensive assumption. No venue, dialogue, or meeting is confirmed. If used, keep it non-romantic. No secret relationship, destiny framing, promise, or compulsory later recognition follows. It must not give Fionn a meaningful relationship with adult Kyrien or give Kyrien early knowledge of magic. The adult interrogation remains their first proper meeting. Ending and retrospective effect Arc 0 need not run directly into Arc 1. A household equilibrium, departure, graduation, meal, or early MSF assignment could close the formative period. These are alternatives, not an ending montage. Let later knowledge change the reader's experience of ordinary places and habits. Avoid announcing which object or conversation will matter. Fionn never properly knows the adult Kyrien who becomes important to Lynleit; do not manufacture that missing relationship to comfort the reader. The prequel must not reveal the future child. Questions before Chapters Which MSF changes occur in these years, and what already exists beforehand? When does Fionn remarry relative to the move and Lynleit's school years? How old is Kyrien when his father dies, and what happens to his mother and sister? Which younger characters overlap in age and schooling? Which origin, if any, belongs to the flask? Does the forgotten encounter happen at all? The Nasu audit favors the conflict between useful institutions and the households affected by their decisions. Its restraint here is to keep the candidate incidents optional rather than turn a development discussion into a finished history. Author's Desk

Curiosity, political awareness, competitiveness, family privilege, immature manipulation, and visible grief may coexist. Young Kyrien can be easier to read, angrier, more trusting, and quicker to mistake determination for resources. Neither is the finished adult in school clothes. The proposed contrast is specific: Lynleit learns to keep important people near after loss; Kyrien learns to function when alone. Proximity can support loyalty or become possessiveness. Independence can support survival or make help difficult to accept. These are development directions to test in scenes, not explanations for every adult action. Kyrien's whiskey flask is established adult equipment. Arc 0 may explore its beginnings through his father, an older relative, imitation, inheritance, or a difficult night. None of these origins is selected. The habit may begin awkwardly and become a measured private ritual. Do not depict alcohol as medical treatment or as the source of his competence. School and the ensemble Use classmates, family backgrounds, examinations, rivalries, meals, clubs, and ordinary boredom to make the younger ensemble socially alive. Do not assign all current characters to the same school or generation. Kyrien's later introduction to the Magi world remains intact: magical schooling and doctrine belong to characters who already have access to them, not automatically to him. For young Magi, lessons, exercises, history, doctrine, and unequal access to training can show how their institutions describe themselves. Teachers may be sincere yet transmit omissions or mistaken assumptions. A lesson is evidence of what students were taught, not automatic confirmation of the world's underlying truth. Talent should create expectations and mistakes as well as prestige. Friendships and rivalries may change without every classmate becoming an important enemy. Warmth, adolescent certainty, humor, family affection, and small victories should coexist with class, political pressure, magical privilege, and threats the adults cannot always contain. Optional forgotten encounter A brief teenage encounter between Lynleit and Kyrien remains optional. A waiting room, station, shop, school event, or corridor could let two exhausted adolescents irritate each other and inadvertently challenge a defensive assumption. No venue, dialogue, or meeting is confirmed. If used, keep it non-romantic. No secret relationship, destiny framing, promise, or compulsory later recognition follows. It must not give Fionn a meaningful relationship with adult Kyrien or give Kyrien early knowledge of magic. The adult interrogation remains their first proper meeting. Ending and retrospective effect Arc 0 need not run directly into Arc 1. A household equilibrium, departure, graduation, meal, or early MSF assignment could close the formative period. These are alternatives, not an ending montage. Let later knowledge change the reader's experience of ordinary places and habits. Avoid announcing which object or conversation will matter. Fionn never properly knows the adult Kyrien who becomes important to Lynleit; do not manufacture that missing relationship to comfort the reader. The prequel must not reveal the future child. Questions before Chapters Which MSF changes occur in these years, and what already exists beforehand? When does Fionn remarry relative to the move and Lynleit's school years? How old is Kyrien when his father dies, where does that history fall relative to Arc 0, and what are his sister's circumstances and his mother's later fate? Which younger characters overlap in age and schooling? Which origin, if any, belongs to the flask? Does the forgotten encounter happen at all? The Nasu audit favors the conflict between useful institutions and the households affected by their decisions. Its restraint here is to keep the candidate incidents optional rather than turn a development discussion into a finished history. Author's Desk

entries.text: Archive Audit: 12 September 2026 · v1 Editorial Audit Approval-pending findings on canon consistency, chronology, prose, character development, reader knowledge, and responsive design. No audit actions have been implemented. Archive Audit: 12 September 2026 Status and scope Findings and proposals only. The author has not approved implementation of the actions below. Today's character clarifications have been integrated separately in the Cognition and Physical Competence reference. That integration does not authorize the revisions proposed here. Jump to consistency and chronology, story and writing, UI and reading, writer workflow, or recommended order. The review covered the current public pages, 18 profiles, 8 default Chapters, 24 current Moments, 14 registered documents, World records, shared registries, editorial ledgers, search, navigation, and version handling. Current narrative text received the closest editorial review. Historical revisions were checked for separation and sampled for context, not treated as current canon or exhaustively line-edited. Original artwork and audio were not altered. Automated browser checks exercised 80 routes at 390, 1024, and 1440 pixels in Chromium and WebKit: 480 views. They found no broken displayed images, page-wide horizontal overflow, or browser script errors. They did find two local text-overflow problems at 1024 pixels. Existing regression checks also covered navigation, search history, portrait thumbnails, relationship selection, and masonry hover stability. These are useful checks, not proof of complete accessibility or of behavior on a physical iPhone. Native Safari, VoiceOver, and live authenticated Page notes were not exercised by the local sweep. The Nasu audit was applied as the project's advisory framework, not as participation by Kinoko Nasu. Its principal influence is to require observable preparation, consequential limits, and earned exceptions without explaining away the mysteries. The author's established outcomes remain controlling. What is already working Natalia's worked examples give complex material a human scale. Her familiar teacher-student rhythm with Lynleit is worth preserving. The river's empty boats, submerged hands, lost jacket, and divided banks provide specific action and imagery rather than interchangeable supernatural danger. The Nameless Street has a strong sequence of objects and actions: balloon, crying, fence, body, smile, fall. Its uncertainty is productive. Mikhail and Lynleit's prolonged exchange has recognizable comic business and escalation. Length alone is not a reason to dismantle it. Sherie and Felix now have a relationship direction distinct from Lynleit and Kyrien. The difference should survive scene drafting. Shared registries, version snapshots, ordinary-looking entity links, flat styling, and the mobile archive toolbars provide a sound base. A wholesale site redesign is not justified by this audit. First priority: factual consistency and chronology R01. Lester's foundation entry has not caught up with his ontology Evidence: Hidden World Foundation still leaves open whether Lester was born a demiholumn or became one. His profile and the Holumn archive expressly reject an ordinary discoverable transformation as the explanation. The older wording reopens a route the author closed. Proposed action: Version and update the foundation document to preserve intrinsic contradiction, the limits of human comprehension, and Natalia's recognition. Keep questions about his capabilities and observable biography open. Do not invent an origin event. Decision needed: Implementation approval only; the governing author decision already exists. R02. The Drowned Choir's stated boundary is broader than the scene supports Evidence: HI-003's countermeasure summary says the hands cannot reach through the river surface. Maren appears to be pulled from the boat before she is in the water, but the blocking does not explain the first grip under that broad restriction. The incident's fuller description instead locates the impassable boundary beneath water-walking Lynleit. HI-003 also says the dead speak through the girl, although the encounter presents her as silent. Proposed action: Distinguish the observed boundary under Lynleit from a universal restriction on the hands. Check the source of the claim about speaking before retaining it as fact. Preserve the Choir and leviathan as separate Holumns. Decision needed: Approval to reconcile the wording; author confirmation if the boundary is meant to have a broader mechanism or the Choir has an established voice outside this encounter. R03. The interrogation outline contains stale exposition and repeated entry Evidence: After the Failed Attempt introduces Lynleit's entrance twice in successive paragraphs and says her authority has not been explained. Her profile already names the MSF transfer clause. An explanation deliberately withheld from Kyrien is different from an unresolved explanation in the archive. Proposed action: Remove the repeated entrance and align the outline's account of what is known with the owning records. Preserve the protected politician, the danger to Lynleit, her concealed knowledge, and the coercive initial arrangement. Do not invent interrogation dialogue merely to fill the gap. Decision needed: Implementation approval only for the consistency edit; drafting the full encounter is a separate action. R04. Some reciprocal or absolute claims need a source decision Evidence: The World index says Natalia was Lynleit's favourite teacher. Natalia's profile and the Academy Moment additionally call Lynleit Natalia's favourite student. Those are separate claims. Kyrien's later intelligence work is described as mastered completely, which exceeds a bounded account of competence. Proposed action: Confirm whether the favourite-student relationship is reciprocal. Replace unsupported absolutes with the specific work a character can accomplish, without reducing established competence. Apply the same source check to current records rather than treating every old sentence as an author decision. Decision needed: Confirm Natalia's preference if it is not already in an authoritative source. No new weaknesses should be invented to balance the wording. R05. Approximate chronology still looks more fixed than it is Evidence: Doom's approximate phase appears in the single ordered timeline after the political settlement. The text says its relation to surrounding phases is unfixed, but the visual order suggests otherwise. The flask's unknown origin receives an Arc 0 chronology entry labelled Family history even though its source and beginning remain open. The Nameless Street shares the Cardiff/Academy phase without establishing its exact relation to the journeys. Proposed action: Display approximate ranges, concurrent strands, and genuinely unplaced entries without forcing a single exact sequence. Keep the confirmed order of the hotel refuge, Doom, park encounter, later intimacy, pregnancy, and Arc 2. Remove an unearned period assignment from unknown item history; preserve stable links and flexible numbering. Decision needed: Approval for the presentation and metadata work. Exact dates, durations, and the relationship of Doom to political milestones remain author decisions. R06. Reveal order needs its own record, distinct from event order Evidence: Profiles, timelines, incident explanations, and Chapter tables contain different levels of knowledge about the first missing person, Fionn's death, the coat, the Cult connection, and Lynleit's children. The reader understanding the son is not the same event as Kyrien finding out. The current Cult naming follows the approved later Doom revisions and should not be silently returned to the earlier implied-only treatment. Proposed action: Track when an event occurs, when the reader can infer or learn it, and when each relevant character knows it. Begin with the small set of major secrets already established. Preserve the author's current revision decisions and leave undetermined revelations blank. Decision needed: Approve the model; choose any still-undecided revelation dates or audiences only when the story supplies them. Story, prose, and reader comprehension R07. Decide how much the archive should spoil for a first-time reader Evidence: The Story timeline exposes the first missing person's causal role before the Chapters. Preface tables reveal outcomes before the prose, and profiles span later life periods. These are useful writer references but can remove discovery from the reading experience. Proposed action: Keep the required preface tables, but offer a clear reading mode or a collapsed spoiler summary. Keep the complete writer view available. Separate intended chronology from recommended reading order rather than pretending the archive is already a finished novel. Decision needed: Whether this site should support spoiler-conscious reading at all, and whether that or the writer view should be the default. No spoilers have been hidden during this audit. R08. Draft status and Chapter coverage need clearer presentation Evidence: The catalog places 141-word and 225-word placeholders beside developed scenes of roughly 1,400 to 3,600 words. The status badges exist, but all entries share sequential Chapter labels and the same reader architecture. The Name Left Behind introduces a future-dated record about Fionn and self-altering archives without a matching Moment. Before the First Bell also lacks a linked Moment. Proposed action: Make outlines, drafted scenes, canon drafts, and writer gaps distinguishable in catalog filtering and reader headers. Add missing Moment links where the material is accepted. Keep the invented archive incident outside shared canon until accepted or explicitly retired; do not delete its historical source. Decision needed: Whether to keep and develop The Name Left Behind, or retain it only as an unused outline. Creating a Moment must not automatically ratify its inventions. R09. The main political and supernatural plot needs more scene work Evidence: The central recruitment remains an outline. Fionn's murder, the refuge, reclamation of MSF, the Cardiff moral conflict, and the Academy rescue mostly exist as planning records rather than Chapters. Doom has received substantially more dialogue and revision work than those turning points. Proposed action: Prioritize a small sequence of main-plot scenes before adding further intimate milestones: the interrogation, a professional encounter showing Sherie and Felix, an operational consequence of Kyrien's preparation, and a scene exposing the pressure around Fionn. Draft only where facts are sufficient; request focused decisions for missing causes. Decision needed: Which scene to develop first. This is a proposal for writing work, not permission to manufacture the missing conspiracy or chronology. R10. Doom's recovery needs more visible support in the characters Evidence: Doom v7 carefully presents the proposed cure as uncertain, then explains categorically that the incomplete attempt and aftermath changed both identities enough. The particular change in Kyrien is less visible than the explanation of the mechanism. The final assurance risks doing work the preceding behavior should carry. Proposed action: Develop observable, non-graphic changes in attention, choice, or expectation on both sides, and review the transition in narrative viewpoint around the recovery. Preserve the incomplete attempt, the successful recovery, Kyrien's incomplete knowledge, Natalia's practical teaching, and Mikhail's comic exchange. Do not introduce a new ritual, completed sexual encounter, or guaranteed cure formula. Decision needed: Approval for a new revision and, if necessary, agreement on the particular changes each character undergoes. The outcome itself is not being reopened. R11. Recheck shown and inferred labels against specific evidence Evidence: The river preface interprets physical tells as attraction and the empty boats as evidence of the crews' fate. These may be intentional readings, but they are not equally certain deductions. Elsewhere explanatory narration makes material explicit that an older outline may have left inferred. The park contains a visible writer gap, which is a different status again. Proposed action: Attach each current table claim to the passage that supports it, soften claims where the evidence supports only a possibility, and distinguish facts supplied by the author from conclusions available inside the scene. Preserve the blue/purple reader key and neutral outline facts. An undrafted passage must not be presented as delivered evidence. Decision needed: Approval for the label and wording audit. Any change to a intended reveal itself needs the author's agreement. R12. Revise explanatory habits without flattening the voices Evidence: The interrogation repeats an entrance. Institutional headings repeatedly announce abstractions such as two purposes or three degrees of distance before explaining the actual subject. Some profile claims are broad verdicts. Several scenes use the same short denial, correction, and counter-correction rhythm, which can make different speakers converge. Proposed action: Perform a passage-level edit for repetition, focalization, abstract summary, and unnecessary justification. Keep productive comic repetition, prop business, domestic detail, and the author's approved extended banter. Distinguish Felix's generated alternatives from Hiyu's investigative hypotheses, Kyrien's observation from Reiner's procedural speech, and Lynleit's familiar irreverence from Sherie's social play. Use today's behavior as attention, not dialogue explaining a type. Decision needed: Approval for selected current documents and Chapters, preserving old published revisions. No imitation of another writer's prose is required. R13. The capability graphs still imply false precision and comparison Evidence: The Capability ledger already records Lester's Magecraft score despite his inherent demiholumn nature, Mikhail's missing counter-Magus distinction, and the mixing of Kyrien's later mastery with earlier competence. Exact numbers suggest calibrated comparisons that the canon does not yet support. Proposed action: First distinguish story period and type of capability. Separate trained magecraft, Church countermeasures, and inherent anomalous ability where comparison would otherwise mislead. Use a supported descriptive scale or an explicitly bounded graph model. Keep today's agility, endurance, precision, and trained competence independent of MBTI. Do not simply reduce high scores until shapes look balanced. Decision needed: Agreement on what the graph should compare. Specific training histories, failure limits, and supernatural costs remain open. R14. Supporting characters need decisions that belong to them Evidence: Tien is strongly defined by serving Helena and opposing Kyrien; Myka's danger and eventual success have more definition than her own decisions; the Cardiff disagreement identifies moral incompatibility without establishing the act that makes it unavoidable. Broad statements about competence or morality cannot yet carry those scenes. Proposed action: Develop one consequential choice, one dependency, and one credible limit for each character when their next scene is written. For Cardiff, identify the specific solution Mikhail accepts that Lynleit cannot accept. For Myka, establish something she does that affects her survival and later recruitment. Preserve specialist distinctions rather than giving every supporting character the protagonists' skills. Decision needed: Concrete author choices. The audit should not invent Mikhail's ethics, Myka's curriculum, or Tien's private loyalties. R15. Relationship direction needs evidence across ordinary work Evidence: Sherie and Felix's confirmed gradual direction is richer than the professional encounters currently drafted. Much intimacy guidance describes anticipated behavior. A hypothetical response to Sherie's hurt is not yet a scene. Lynleit and Kyrien's rescue and secrecy milestones are better documented than their mundane repeated contact. Proposed action: Give future main-plot scenes space for small, specific interactions that accumulate. Track established encounters separately from intended development. Preserve Felix's attachment to Lynleit while Sherie acquires significance of her own, and keep Lynleit's duty primary. Do not add a confession simply to complete an audit checklist. Decision needed: Approval to develop particular encounters, with chronology kept open where it is not fixed. R16. Foundational terms need a shorter route into the setting Evidence: Definitions of magic, magecraft, miracles, Holumns, identity, and suppression are distributed across World and Docs. Human singularity appears in Lester's account without a short local explanation of what the phrase permits the reader to understand. Institutional interpretations can sound like universal physical laws when read in isolation. Proposed action: Provide a concise entry point with links to owning definitions. Distinguish observed effects, institutional doctrine, and unanswered ontology. Cross-link existing explanations before adding another large foundational essay. Move public development prompts such as the Magiarchy page's Awaiting definition section into the editorial ledgers, while retaining honest statements about unknown phenomena. Preserve unknown mechanisms rather than filling them with invented technical language. Decision needed: Approval for organization and clearer wording; any new metaphysical definition requires author confirmation. UI and reading experience R17. Fix the two confirmed intermediate-width overflows Evidence: At 1024 pixels in both engines, the Director's House heading has about 199 pixels of content in a 162-pixel column. The Holumn definition's first explanation exceeds its local column as well. The house keeps a three-column hero until a 950-pixel breakpoint; its fixed side columns and padding leave the title too narrow. The Holumn layout nests another two-column grid inside an already constrained panel. Proposed action: Collapse these compositions according to available content width, reduce unsuitable fixed minimums, and allow long text to wrap. Test the full interval around the breakpoints and browser zoom. Preserve the distinct page designs and flat palette. Decision needed: Implementation approval only. Neither issue was fixed in this audit. R18. Restore visible life-period context to profile artwork Evidence: The portrait carousel updates Arc information in image alt text, thumbnail titles, and a screen-reader-only status. A sighted touch user cannot reliably identify the displayed Arc 2 artwork from those labels. Catalog cards do display an Arc label. Proposed action: Add a small visible era label only when relevant, without restoring arrow buttons, image counters, a large overlay background, or obstructed artwork. Keep image-half taps, dragging, swiping, and thumbnails. Decision needed: Implementation approval and placement preference only if the author wants to choose it. R19. Remove misleading empty choices and distinguish music concepts Evidence: All 33 current Gallery records use unspecified location, while the location selector still offers several named places with no matching images. Music has one playable recording and four concepts; the category architecture now matches Characters, but concepts still occupy the same prominent browsing space as playable work. Proposed action: Derive available filter choices and counts from records, without inventing locations. Keep future metadata support. Offer a straightforward playable-only option or separate concepts from recordings, retaining the custom banner player and both downloads. Do not relabel a concept as available. Decision needed: Approval for filtering improvements; keeping concepts visible by default is a design choice, not a canon question. R20. Reduce navigation work in long readers Evidence: A Chapter reader places the full horizontal story timeline before the actual chapter. Long documents and profiles require substantial scrolling; the desktop layout also has an independently scrolling content pane and a Page notes column. These structures work, but they compete with sustained reading. Proposed action: Offer a compact or collapsible timeline in reader views, retain the full timeline in catalogs, add useful section navigation, and preserve back navigation and scroll position. Improve the use of the right column without adding a permanent left sidebar. Do not remove the timeline or breadcrumbs. Decision needed: Approval for reader-focused design work. A default reading mode should be chosen together with R07. R21. Finish accessibility testing beyond visual correctness Evidence: Existing tests cover menu focus and several interactions, but do not establish complete screen-reader behavior, contrast, every tooltip dismissal route, map rearrangement without a pointer, or physical iPhone gesture behavior. The local WebKit run is not native Safari certification. Proposed action: Test F/M/S notes with keyboard and assistive technology, verify text contrast and touch targets, test map and portrait interaction under zoom and reduced motion, and confirm that drag gestures do not trap vertical scrolling. Add only the controls required to make the existing interactions usable. Decision needed: Approval for the accessibility pass. A physical Safari check requires access to the target environment; until then, report that limit explicitly. Writer workflow and cohesion R22. Make the ledgers reflect evidence and actual unresolved decisions Evidence: The contradictions ledger records no unresolved contradiction despite the source drift in R01 and the boundary problem requiring review in R02. The capability ledger already holds several concerns that have not changed the graph. Confidence percentages help scan the questions but do not explain what evidence would close them. Proposed action: Register verified conflicts after approval, link them to their owning sources and required follow-up surfaces, and group questions by the decision that would answer them. Retain the required confidence and resolution bars. Separate ordinary missing information, deliberate mysteries, and genuinely incompatible statements. Do not resolve a deliberate contradiction in Lester's existence as though it were a continuity error. Decision needed: Approval for ledger maintenance. Answers remain the author's unless already established. R23. Reduce duplicated explanations and conflicting maintenance guidance Evidence: Suppression doctrine and basic ontology are explained in several World and Docs records. They serve different readers, but repeated full explanations increase drift risk. The maintenance charter still describes entity links as ordinary prose until hover, while the recorded design preference is that they remain ordinary-looking in every state, with usable keyboard focus. Large shared style sections and repeated navigation markup also make local adjustments hard to reason about. Proposed action: Keep one owning definition and concise contextual explanations elsewhere. Reconcile guidance wording, document the owner of each recurring component, and refactor only where tests demonstrate equivalent behavior. Do not force the individually designed World pages into one template or undertake a framework migration. Decision needed: Approval for focused maintenance and source consolidation, not a site rebuild. R24. Extend regression checks to the failures this audit found Evidence: Existing checks passed while the 1024-pixel text overflows and Lester's foundation drift remained. A single explicitly registered v1 document also exposed a mismatch between search URL generation and the expected version URL during today's integration; the new reference follows the existing implicit-v1 convention instead. Proposed action: Add tests for internal text overflow at intermediate widths, explicit single-version documents, visible artwork era labels, and selected cross-record canon invariants. Retain current checks for snapshots, search history, links, gradients, masonry, and mobile navigation. Keep prose judgment and unresolved canon out of false pass/fail assertions. Decision needed: Implementation approval only for tests and demonstrated defects; do not turn a hypothesis into a test that forces it to become canon. Recommended order after approval 1. Consistency and verified defects: R01-R05, R17-R19, R22-R24, excluding questions that need an author decision. 2. Reading and knowledge structure: R06-R08, R11, R16, R20-R21. 3. Prose, capability, and scene development: R09-R10, R12-R15, with a bounded plan for each revision. The decisions most likely to need the author directly are the archive's spoiler policy, the future of The Name Left Behind, reciprocal favourite-student status, exact chronology still left open, capability limits, the concrete Cardiff moral conflict, and any new scene proposed to demonstrate a relationship or a talent. Approval of cleanup alone must not be interpreted as permission to decide those facts. Archive Review

Approximate chronology still looks more fixed than it is Evidence: Doom's approximate phase appears in the single ordered timeline after the political settlement. The text says its relation to surrounding phases is unfixed, but the visual order suggests otherwise. The flask's unknown origin receives an Arc 0 chronology entry labelled Family history even though its source and beginning remain open. The Nameless Street shares the Cardiff/Academy phase without establishing its exact relation to the journeys. Proposed action: Display approximate ranges, concurrent strands, and genuinely unplaced entries without forcing a single exact sequence. Keep the confirmed order of the hotel refuge, Doom, park encounter, later intimacy, pregnancy, and Arc 2. Remove an unearned period assignment from unknown item history; preserve stable links and flexible numbering. Decision needed: Approval for the presentation and metadata work. Exact dates, durations, and the relationship of Doom to political milestones remain author decisions. R06. Reveal order needs its own record, distinct from event order Evidence: Profiles, timelines, incident explanations, and Chapter tables contain different levels of knowledge about the first missing person, Fionn's death, the coat, the Cult connection, and Lynleit's children. The reader understanding the son is not the same event as Kyrien finding out. The current Cult naming follows the approved later Doom revisions and should not be silently returned to the earlier implied-only treatment. Proposed action: Track when an event occurs, when the reader can infer or learn it, and when each relevant character knows it. Begin with the small set of major secrets already established. Preserve the author's current revision decisions and leave undetermined revelations blank. Decision needed: Approve the model; choose any still-undecided revelation dates or audiences only when the story supplies them. Story, prose, and reader comprehension R07. Decide how much the archive should spoil for a first-time reader Evidence: The Story timeline exposes the first missing person's causal role before the Chapters. Preface tables reveal outcomes before the prose, and profiles span later life periods. These are useful writer references but can remove discovery from the reading experience. Proposed action: Keep the required preface tables, but offer a clear reading mode or a collapsed spoiler summary. Keep the complete writer view available. Separate intended chronology from recommended reading order rather than pretending the archive is already a finished novel. Decision needed: Whether this site should support spoiler-conscious reading at all, and whether that or the writer view should be the default. No spoilers have been hidden during this audit. R08. Draft status and Chapter coverage need clearer presentation Evidence: The catalog places 141-word and 225-word placeholders beside developed scenes of roughly 1,400 to 3,600 words. The status badges exist, but all entries share sequential Chapter labels and the same reader architecture. The Name Left Behind introduces a future-dated record about Fionn and self-altering archives without a matching Moment. Before the First Bell also lacks a linked Moment. Proposed action: Make outlines, drafted scenes, canon drafts, and writer gaps distinguishable in catalog filtering and reader headers. Add missing Moment links where the material is accepted. Keep the invented archive incident outside shared canon until accepted or explicitly retired; do not delete its historical source. Decision needed: Whether to keep and develop The Name Left Behind, or retain it only as an unused outline. Creating a Moment must not automatically ratify its inventions. R09. The main political and supernatural plot needs more scene work Evidence: The central recruitment remains an outline. Fionn's murder, the refuge, reclamation of MSF, the Cardiff moral conflict, and the Academy rescue mostly exist as planning records rather than Chapters. Doom has received substantially more dialogue and revision work than those turning points. Proposed action: Prioritize a small sequence of main-plot scenes before adding further intimate milestones: the interrogation, a professional encounter showing Sherie and Felix, an operational consequence of Kyrien's preparation, and a scene exposing the pressure around Fionn. Draft only where facts are sufficient; request focused decisions for missing causes. Decision needed: Which scene to develop first. This is a proposal for writing work, not permission to manufacture the missing conspiracy or chronology. R10. Doom's recovery needs more visible support in the characters Evidence: Doom v7 carefully presents the proposed cure as uncertain, then explains categorically that the incomplete attempt and aftermath changed both identities enough. The particular change in Kyrien is less visible than the explanation of the mechanism. The final assurance risks doing work the preceding behavior should carry. Proposed action: Develop observable, non-graphic changes in attention, choice, or expectation on both sides, and review the transition in narrative viewpoint around the recovery. Preserve the incomplete attempt, the successful recovery, Kyrien's incomplete knowledge, Natalia's practical teaching, and Mikhail's comic exchange. Do not introduce a new ritual, completed sexual encounter, or guaranteed cure formula. Decision needed: Approval for a new revision and, if necessary, agreement on the particular changes each character undergoes. The outcome itself is not being reopened. R11. Recheck shown and inferred labels against specific evidence Evidence: The river preface interprets physical tells as attraction and the empty boats as evidence of the crews' fate. These may be intentional readings, but they are not equally certain deductions. Elsewhere explanatory narration makes material explicit that an older outline may have left inferred. The park contains a visible writer gap, which is a different status again. Proposed action: Attach each current table claim to the passage that supports it, soften claims where the evidence supports only a possibility, and distinguish facts supplied by the author from conclusions available inside the scene. Preserve the blue/purple reader key and neutral outline facts. An undrafted passage must not be presented as delivered evidence. Decision needed: Approval for the label and wording audit. Any change to a intended reveal itself needs the author's agreement. R12. Revise explanatory habits without flattening the voices Evidence: The interrogation repeats an entrance. Institutional headings repeatedly announce abstractions such as two purposes or three degrees of distance before explaining the actual subject. Some profile claims are broad verdicts. Several scenes use the same short denial, correction, and counter-correction rhythm, which can make different speakers converge. Proposed action: Perform a passage-level edit for repetition, focalization, abstract summary, and unnecessary justification. Keep productive comic repetition, prop business, domestic detail, and the author's approved extended banter. Distinguish Felix's generated alternatives from Hiyu's investigative hypotheses, Kyrien's observation from Reiner's procedural speech, and Lynleit's familiar irreverence from Sherie's social play. Use today's behavior as attention, not dialogue explaining a type. Decision needed: Approval for selected current documents and Chapters, preserving old published revisions. No imitation of another writer's prose is required. R13. The capability graphs still imply false precision and comparison Evidence: The Capability ledger already records Lester's Magecraft score despite his inherent demiholumn nature, Mikhail's missing counter-Magus distinction, and the mixing of Kyrien's later mastery with earlier competence. Exact numbers suggest calibrated comparisons that the canon does not yet support. Proposed action: First distinguish story period and type of capability. Separate trained magecraft, Church countermeasures, and inherent anomalous ability where comparison would otherwise mislead. Use a supported descriptive scale or an explicitly bounded graph model. Keep today's agility, endurance, precision, and trained competence independent of MBTI. Do not simply reduce high scores until shapes look balanced. Decision needed: Agreement on what the graph should compare. Specific training histories, failure limits, and supernatural costs remain open. R14. Supporting characters need decisions that belong to them Evidence: Tien is strongly defined by serving Helena and opposing Kyrien; Myka's danger and eventual success have more definition than her own decisions; the Cardiff disagreement identifies moral incompatibility without establishing the act that makes it unavoidable. Broad statements about competence or morality cannot yet carry those scenes. Proposed action: Develop one consequential choice, one dependency, and one credible limit for each character when their next scene is written. For Cardiff, identify the specific solution Mikhail accepts that Lynleit cannot accept. For Myka, establish something she does that affects her survival and later recruitment. Preserve specialist distinctions rather than giving every supporting character the protagonists' skills. Decision needed: Concrete author choices. The audit should not invent Mikhail's ethics, Myka's curriculum, or Tien's private loyalties. R15. Relationship direction needs evidence across ordinary work Evidence: Sherie and Felix's confirmed gradual direction is richer than the professional encounters currently drafted. Much intimacy guidance describes anticipated behavior. A hypothetical response to Sherie's hurt is not yet a scene. Lynleit and Kyrien's rescue and secrecy milestones are better documented than their mundane repeated contact. Proposed action: Give future main-plot scenes space for small, specific interactions that accumulate. Track established encounters separately from intended development. Preserve Felix's attachment to Lynleit while Sherie acquires significance of her own, and keep Lynleit's duty primary. Do not add a confession simply to complete an audit checklist. Decision needed: Approval to develop particular encounters, with chronology kept open where it is not fixed. R16. Foundational terms need a shorter route into the setting Evidence: Definitions of magic, magecraft, miracles, Holumns, identity, and suppression are distributed across World and Docs. Human singularity appears in Lester's account without a short local explanation of what the phrase permits the reader to understand. Institutional interpretations can sound like universal physical laws when read in isolation. Proposed action: Provide a concise entry point with links to owning definitions. Distinguish observed effects, institutional doctrine, and unanswered ontology. Cross-link existing explanations before adding another large foundational essay. Move public development prompts such as the Magiarchy page's Awaiting definition section into the editorial ledgers, while retaining honest statements about unknown phenomena. Preserve unknown mechanisms rather than filling them with invented technical language. Decision needed: Approval for organization and clearer wording; any new metaphysical definition requires author confirmation. UI and reading experience R17. Fix the two confirmed intermediate-width overflows Evidence: At 1024 pixels in both engines, the Director's House heading has about 199 pixels of content in a 162-pixel column. The Holumn definition's first explanation exceeds its local column as well. The house keeps a three-column hero until a 950-pixel breakpoint; its fixed side columns and padding leave the title too narrow. The Holumn layout nests another two-column grid inside an already constrained panel. Proposed action: Collapse these compositions according to available content width, reduce unsuitable fixed minimums, and allow long text to wrap. Test the full interval around the breakpoints and browser zoom. Preserve the distinct page designs and flat palette. Decision needed: Implementation approval only. Neither issue was fixed in this audit. R18. Restore visible life-period context to profile artwork Evidence: The portrait carousel updates Arc information in image alt text, thumbnail titles, and a screen-reader-only status. A sighted touch user cannot reliably identify the displayed Arc 2 artwork from those labels. Catalog cards do display an Arc label. Proposed action: Add a small visible era label only when relevant, without restoring arrow buttons, image counters, a large overlay background, or obstructed artwork. Keep image-half taps, dragging, swiping, and thumbnails. Decision needed: Implementation approval and placement preference only if the author wants to choose it. R19. Remove misleading empty choices and distinguish music concepts Evidence: All 33 current Gallery records use unspecified location, while the location selector still offers several named places with no matching images. Music has one playable recording and four concepts; the category architecture now matches Characters, but concepts still occupy the same prominent browsing space as playable work. Proposed action: Derive available filter choices and counts from records, without inventing locations. Keep future metadata support. Offer a straightforward playable-only option or separate concepts from recordings, retaining the custom banner player and both downloads. Do not relabel a concept as available. Decision needed: Approval for filtering improvements; keeping concepts visible by default is a design choice, not a canon question. R20. Reduce navigation work in long readers Evidence: A Chapter reader places the full horizontal story timeline before the actual chapter. Long documents and profiles require substantial scrolling; the desktop layout also has an independently scrolling content pane and a Page notes column. These structures work, but they compete with sustained reading. Proposed action: Offer a compact or collapsible timeline in reader views, retain the full timeline in catalogs, add useful section navigation, and preserve back navigation and scroll position. Improve the use of the right column without adding a permanent left sidebar. Do not remove the timeline or breadcrumbs. Decision needed: Approval for reader-focused design work. A default reading mode should be chosen together with R07. R21. Finish accessibility testing beyond visual correctness Evidence: Existing tests cover menu focus and several interactions, but do not establish complete screen-reader behavior, contrast, every tooltip dismissal route, map rearrangement without a pointer, or physical iPhone gesture behavior. The local WebKit run is not native Safari certification. Proposed action: Test F/M/S notes with keyboard and assistive technology, verify text contrast and touch targets, test map and portrait interaction under zoom and reduced motion, and confirm that drag gestures do not trap vertical scrolling. Add only the controls required to make the existing interactions usable. Decision needed: Approval for the accessibility pass. A physical Safari check requires access to the target environment; until then, report that limit explicitly. Writer workflow and cohesion R22. Make the ledgers reflect evidence and actual unresolved decisions Evidence: The contradictions ledger records no unresolved contradiction despite the source drift in R01 and the boundary problem requiring review in R02. The capability ledger already holds several concerns that have not changed the graph. Confidence percentages help scan the questions but do not explain what evidence would close them. Proposed action: Register verified conflicts after approval, link them to their owning sources and required follow-up surfaces, and group questions by the decision that would answer them. Retain the required confidence and resolution bars. Separate ordinary missing information, deliberate mysteries, and genuinely incompatible statements. Do not resolve a deliberate contradiction in Lester's existence as though it were a continuity error. Decision needed: Approval for ledger maintenance. Answers remain the author's unless already established. R23. Reduce duplicated explanations and conflicting maintenance guidance Evidence: Suppression doctrine and basic ontology are explained in several World and Docs records. They serve different readers, but repeated full explanations increase drift risk. The maintenance charter still describes entity links as ordinary prose until hover, while the recorded design preference is that they remain ordinary-looking in every state, with usable keyboard focus. Large shared style sections and repeated navigation markup also make local adjustments hard to reason about. Proposed action: Keep one owning definition and concise contextual explanations elsewhere. Reconcile guidance wording, document the owner of each recurring component, and refactor only where tests demonstrate equivalent behavior. Do not force the individually designed World pages into one template or undertake a framework migration. Decision needed: Approval for focused maintenance and source consolidation, not a site rebuild. R24. Extend regression checks to the failures this audit found Evidence: Existing checks passed while the 1024-pixel text overflows and Lester's foundation drift remained. A single explicitly registered v1 document also exposed a mismatch between search URL generation and the expected version URL during today's integration; the new reference follows the existing implicit-v1 convention instead. Proposed action: Add tests for internal text overflow at intermediate widths, explicit single-version documents, visible artwork era labels, and selected cross-record canon invariants. Retain current checks for snapshots, search history, links, gradients, masonry, and mobile navigation. Keep prose judgment and unresolved canon out of false pass/fail assertions. Decision needed: Implementation approval only for tests and demonstrated defects; do not turn a hypothesis into a test that forces it to become canon. Recommended order after approval 1. Consistency and verified defects: R01-R05, R17-R19, R22-R24, excluding questions that need an author decision. 2. Reading and knowledge structure: R06-R08, R11, R16, R20-R21. 3. Prose, capability, and scene development: R09-R10, R12-R15, with a bounded plan for each revision. The decisions most likely to need the author directly are the archive's spoiler policy, the future of The Name Left Behind, reciprocal favourite-student status, exact chronology still left open, capability limits, the concrete Cardiff moral conflict, and any new scene proposed to demonstrate a relationship or a talent. Approval of cleanup alone must not be interpreted as permission to decide those facts. Archive Review

entries.title: Bone Archive: Development and Source
entries.subtitle: World Development
entries.text: Bone Archive: Development and Source World Development The song-inspired Holumn direction, recovery costs, surviving bargains, and limits of the comparison with Lester. Bone Archive: Development and Source Approved world direction The author approved integrating the Bone Archive concept into MAGIARCHY on 14 September 2026. HI-008 owns the Holumn record. It preserves experiences without a continuous place for them in a person's surviving history. Their traces can be bodily as well as remembered. The opening incident is an officer stepping aside before a shot, then finding a scar where the bullet would have entered. It has no assigned character, institution, location, Arc, or Chapter. Begin with this person's evidence rather than a comprehensive explanation of the Archive. Recovery and attachment Recovered experience can supply a response or knowledge, accompanied by the suffering through which it was acquired. Remembering how to escape a burning room may include remembering death there. This is a cost-bearing phenomenon, not a dependable way to undo a mistake or acquire any desired skill. Preserve the possibility that an affected person wants to keep the experience. A remembered loved one may be a stranger in the present; real relationships can become less familiar. The person can be proud, complicit, angry, or protective of the life others want them to relinquish. No particular victim or relationship has yet been chosen for those developments. Records and responsibility The devil's receipts inspire surviving records of bargains whose making cannot be recovered. An authentic agreement and authentic evidence of wrongdoing can coexist. The agreement does not automatically establish that its promised alternative was true, or absolve someone for fulfilling it. A Church investigation is a possible way to stage this conflict. No trial, doctrine, verdict, victim, or investigator has been assigned. Keep devil and angel as the source speaker's terms until the author establishes an in-world referent. Natalia and Lester Natalia could investigate the Archive, recognize a resemblance to Lester's contradiction, and discover the limits of the comparison. This remains a development route. It does not establish an encounter, experiment, new expertise, or personal memory for her. Lester is not explained by discarded timelines or recovered memories. His origin remains beyond a conventional causal account. The Archive must not become a mechanism for repairing his biography. Musical source Title: Bone Archive (Rewind) Author-described sound: Cellos, fast church organs, deep EDM bass, minor chords, and a fast tempo. The author wrote intuitively for atmosphere, without a predetermined story or explanation. No audio file was supplied for this integration. The recurring bodily and archival imagery suggests experience recorded in the person rather than a readable supernatural library. The refrain's possessiveness suggests someone defending their attachment to the condition. These readings inspired the approved direction; the lyrics do not independently establish facts about MAGIARCHY. The song's speaker remains unidentified. A repeated future, debt measured in hours, and divine figures belong to the lyric voice, not to a settled cosmology or a guaranteed prediction mechanism. Atmospheric options The contrast between ceremony and speed can guide a later scene: testimony recited too quickly, a ritual continuing after its purpose has been forgotten, or a remembered event arriving before the present seems ready for it. These remain optional scene approaches. The music's rhythm is not an activation condition, and a sung rewind is not proof that time reverses. Audit and limits The Nasu-inspired advisory audit favors physical evidence before explanation, useful recovery coupled to cost, personal attachment that complicates rescue, and records that deepen moral disagreement rather than resolve it. This is the project's framework, not participation or endorsement by Kinoko Nasu. Do not invent a keeper, storage building, bone relic, access rite, guaranteed countermeasure, unlimited forecasts, or a causal tie to the Spill. The Questions ledger owns the unresolved choices. Character capability, behavior, and relationship records should change only when a particular character's involvement is established. Author's Desk
