entries.subtitle: Holumn Archive
entries.text: Holumn Incidents and Victim Testimonies · v9 Holumn Archive HI-009, the Oneiric Confluence: shared dreams, weakened volition and competing explanations. Holumn Incidents and Victim Testimonies These accounts describe Holumn encounters, what victims remember, and how institutions have interpreted them. Police, government, Magi, and Church envoys may not know about every encounter listed here. Forms and countermeasures are collected in Holumns. The institutional readings below compare plausible interpretations of the same evidence. They are not transcripts of completed investigations unless a source explicitly establishes one. A stated Holumn property belongs to the archive; it is not automatically known to a witness or institution. The Oneiric Confluence HI-009 · Event-bound · Common name: The Shared Night. Affected sleepers independently remember the same environments, conversations and emotionally important actions, with smaller discrepancies in details and sequence. Early reports include a customs officer shot by his supervisor in a nonexistent station, an impossible library, an accountant and secretary whose shared memories damage their working relationship, and neighbours meeting over tea and grief. These reports produce no corresponding bodily injuries. The absence of injury does not make the experience psychologically harmless. During Natalia's briefing, Sherie discovers that Felix remembers their recurring intimate dreams. Yulia reports Hiyu's dream attack with a filing cabinet. Lynleit and Kyrien describe a quiet house beside water. The variety prevents intimacy, aggression or domestic imagery from becoming a universal explanation. Personality persists while ordinary inhibition and the ability to refuse weaken. The dreamer may recognize an unwanted impulse and still enact it. Natalia considers weakened censorship, a shared imaginal field and the Holumn's selective intensification as competing explanations. Overlapping sleep does not establish a shared clock. No common vector, location, object or deliberate targeting has been found in the initial reports. Sherie and Felix later find that naming a pressure can restore a gap between impulse and action. The pressure returns before easing again. They can step away before choosing a kiss. Their experience supports a limited recognition response, not a reliable cure; Natalia has not received that final account within the chapter. Dream behaviour does not prove fixed preferences or waking intentions. An echo continuing after one participant wakes is a research possibility, not observed testimony. The full research record preserves the competing hypotheses, Natalia's teaching, cast accounts and unresolved limits. Chronology remains unplaced; see the Moment. What an incident can establish Being taken describes a Holumn-specific state, not travel to one common destination. Death is one possibility. Other effects can involve madness, contradiction, disrupted time, altered reality, compromised physicality, damaged or transformed memory, and changes to identity or causality. Location, chronology, life, death, and physical continuity may cease to behave as ordinary categories. A victim can return, but each Holumn determines what makes return possible and whether the returned person is continuous with the person taken. Phenomena resembling life after death and reanimated corpses are also possible. Neither establishes ordinary resurrection or restoration of the original person. These are author-confirmed boundaries of the category, not testimony attributed to the witnesses below. No universal mechanism or destination should be inferred from one record. See the Holumns World archive for the shared principles. A conceptual analogy, not a recorded incident Jungian synchronicity offers an analogy for the possible range. A Holumn could make a synchronicity-like condition inhabitable or imprisoning: meaningful coincidence would become the condition of the victim's existence, rather than something they observe. No such specific Holumn or victim is established here. The relevant inquiry would be what state the Holumn imposed, not where the victim travelled. Lester and continuity Lester's biography contains chronological factors that cannot be reconciled into a continuous causal history. Neither Lester nor Natalia knows how he became a demiholumn. Understanding his coming into existence lies beyond the horizon of human singularity and normal human comprehension. His condition is not a missing transformation event, experiment, infection, or ordinary supernatural mechanism waiting to be found. Natalia comes to recognize contradiction as an intrinsic feature of nature. Lester's apparent violation of continuity can belong to reality at a deeper level, rather than merely being an error in it. This does not establish that he was taken by another Holumn, returned from one, or possesses unlimited abilities. See Lester and Natalia. Bone Archive Record: HI-008 Known forms: Event-bound and curse-bound effects Primary medium: Embodied experience, discontinuous memory, and surviving records An officer steps aside before a shot is fired. He cannot explain the movement. Later, while changing his shirt, he finds a scar where the bullet would have entered. His name, affiliation, location, and the date of the incident are not recorded here. The Bone Archive preserves experiences that no longer have a place in the surviving history of a life. A person may remember a conversation nobody else recalls, mourn a child absent from their biography, or recognize someone as their killer while still alive. An unexplained limp, pain, or practiced movement can carry the experience into the body. No physical library or collection of bones has been identified. Recovery is costly. Knowledge of how to survive a burning room may arrive with the memory of dying in it. A useful response and the suffering through which it was acquired need not be separable. This does not establish controllable time travel, an interchangeable supply of skills, or a reliable forecast. A person may become attached to the remembered life. Someone who loved them there is a stranger here; actual friends can feel less familiar. Loyalty to those experiences can give an affected person reasons to resist losing them, even when they suffer from their return. Surviving bargains The associated records include bargains whose consequences remain although their making cannot be recovered. An authentic record may demand an act as the price of preventing something worse. Authentic evidence against the person who committed it can coexist with that record. Neither proves that the promised alternative would have occurred, or settles whether the act was justified. The source song calls the parties a devil and an angel. These are not confirmed species, divine offices, or identified custodians of the Archive. Interpretive limits An old scar, anticipation, and mistaken recollection are ordinary explanations for individual details of the officer's account. The available incident does not itself establish a discarded timeline. The broader Archive phenomenon preserves experiences without a reconciled causal history; whether those experiences were erased, imposed, or displaced remains unresolved. No access condition, keeper, transferable ownership, reliable selection procedure, or means of release is known. No Church ruling on the records is established. The officer's incident has no assigned Arc, Story phase, or Chapter. No connection to the Spill is confirmed. Development and source The author approved this Holumn direction from their song Bone Archive (Rewind) . The preferred introduction follows one person's bodily evidence before revealing the wider Archive. Natalia is a possible investigator, not an established witness. A comparison with Lester must preserve his distinct ontological contradiction: this Holumn does not explain his origin, turn him into a returned victim, or make his biography a solvable missing-history problem. See Bone Archive: Development and Source for the approved direction, song imagery, and unresolved implementation choices. Sleepers Record: HI-007 Witness: Kyrien Location: Vilen river Account: Sleepers above the River Kyrien encounters human figures hanging roughly twenty to fifty metres above the water and embankment. Most resemble men wearing trench coats and hats. Their heads are lowered and their limbs hang loosely, as if from invisible puppet strings. Clothing moves in the wind; the figures otherwise remain still. They do not attack, pursue, communicate, or visibly respond to his presence. Their faces are difficult to see. He finds no visible supports. After privately calling them Sleepers, he takes a boat downstream to observe more of them. The available account ends while he is still on the river. No quoted testimony, additional witness, institutional investigation, or later outcome is recorded. No countermeasure is known. It is not established whether the figures are people, whether other observers can see them, or whether the river is necessary to their appearance. No connection to the Drowned Choir, river leviathan, or Spill is established. Institutional readings No police, government, Magus, or Church reading has been established for this encounter. Editorial status The manifestation and encounter are author-established; the scene is intentionally incomplete and unplaced. The intended omen concerns approaching circumstances beyond a person's meaningful control, despite preparation or ability. It need not mean death or failure, and choices may still affect details. This is development direction, not an explanation known to Kyrien or a demonstrated predictive rule. Its referent, scope, cause, and reliability remain undecided. See the Questions ledger. The Voice on the Line Record: HI-001 Known form: Disembodied will Primary medium: Telephone call and borrowed voice Have you heard of a telephone call that answers to you in your own voice? At first I thought whoever was on the phone was repeating me. But it was my own voice. At first it felt like an echo, because all it did was repeat my words. Then it started calling me incessantly, and it was talking to me in bizarre ways. In my own voice. Institutional readings Police and government Harassment, a compromised line, manipulated audio, or a distressed witness. Magi and special envoys A reflection that has crossed into agency. The voice no longer requires the witness to speak first. The Last Piece Record: HI-002 Known form: Attached curse Primary medium: A puzzle sold at a market The purchaser becomes increasingly compelled to solve the puzzle. Once the final piece is placed, the purchaser disappears and is entered into the missing-person system. No surviving victim testimony is known. Institutional readings Police and government A missing-person case with a market purchase among the owner's possessions. Whether investigators connect the puzzle to the disappearance is unknown. Magi and special envoys The object carries a condition. The disappearance occurs when the puzzle is completed. Fog during the Spill Narvea already has areas where ordinary fog repeatedly disrupts travel and observation. Certain Holumn incidents during the Spill produce unusually large amounts of fog or mist. The quarantined park in Vilen and the river encounters are especially affected. This is a confirmed setting condition, not a quotation attributed to a witness. Its mechanism must be established incident by incident. Poor visibility alone does not identify a manifestation, prove a disappearance, or establish altered space. The force responsible for the loss of Heyk's unit remains unexplained; no separate fog entity has been identified there. See Narvean fog for the country record and Dread and Action Direction for scene guidance. The Drowned Choir The Drowned Choir and the river leviathan are separate Holumns, not two manifestations of one river-bound intelligence. Record: HI-003 Known forms: Embodied and environmental manifestation Primary medium: The city river, drowned souls, and a humanlike body A pale girl emerges from the water. Her eyes are sewn shut with fishing line, and her dress is made from dead fish. The souls of people drowned in the river across generations are bound to her. Their submerged hands seize swimmers and pull them downward. The girl does not speak during this encounter. It felt as though my legs were being grabbed and pulled by someone's hands. Source: MSF Officer Maren after reaching shore The encounter occurs during a covert MSF operation requested by Sherie and Drake. Small wooden boats owned by contraband gangs move on the darkest nights without visible operators. Dark tarps cover their shallow holds, fixed rudders hold their heading, and the current provides most of their movement. Felix freezes the bridge cameras and remains on the city side as communications fallback while Lynleit, Reiner, Kyrien, Maren, and Ivo descend. When they pull back the tarps, the holds are empty. The Drowned Choir has already taken every crew before the boats reach the interception point. The officers are trained swimmers, but unseen hands make the short escape to shore nearly impossible. Reiner, Maren, and Ivo reach the street-facing city bank with Felix's fallback line. Kyrien is driven toward the quarantined park bank instead and observes the river from inside the trees. Only Lynleit sees the hands clearly after she is pulled underwater. They tear away the fitted blue suede jacket she chose for the operation. Fear and fury release her blue flame at full force. It burns the drowned hands beneath the water until their grip opens. Unusually heavy mist restricts sight across the river during the encounter. Visibility remains uneven: the near water can be seen from the park bank, and Felix can distinguish the swimmers approaching the city steps. The surviving accounts do not establish which manifestation produces the mist or how it does so. When Lynleit breaks the surface, her palm meets resistance. She brings one knee and then both boots onto the same yielding layer. The river bows beneath her weight without admitting her body. Once she stands, the hands cannot cross the surface beneath her feet. The girl then rises before Lynleit. She remains silent and tilts her head. The gesture suggests bewilderment at Lynleit standing on the water, but does not explain the girl's rule or why she does not pursue her. Only Kyrien witnesses Lynleit standing on the river and keeps the ability secret afterward. Lynleit later reaches him on the park side, where they recover among the trees. Their return to the others is not yet recorded. Institutional readings Police and government Darkness, panic, current, exhaustion, and shared misperception can be used to separate the officers' accounts from the empty boats and missing smugglers. No ordinary report can explain why several trained swimmers independently describe hands pulling at their legs. Magi and special envoys An embodied Holumn has enslaved the river's drowned souls and uses their hands to seize victims. Lynleit's blue flame burns the submerged hands. Once the surface supports her, the hands below her cannot reach through it. This encounter does not establish that the hands are unable to cross any part of the river surface, or explain what holds them below her. Neither observation establishes a means of destroying the girl or releasing the dead. The River That Is Too Deep This river leviathan is distinct from the Drowned Choir. Their shared river does not make them one entity. Record: HI-004 Known forms: Environmental and possibly embodied Primary medium: The city river The river produces waves its width and depth should not permit. Boats and kayaks suffer damage without a sufficient material cause. Bodies recovered from the water carry missing sections larger than the bite of any animal expected in the river. The available evidence does not yet establish whether a creature occupies the river, whether the river itself has become the manifestation, or whether both readings describe different layers of the same Holumn. Institutional readings Police and government Hidden debris, dangerous currents, criminal interference, and postmortem animal damage remain the available categories. Magi and special envoys The damage may come from a Holumn whose movement does not fit the river's measured depth. Whether this is a creature, a change in the river, or both remains disputed. Under unknown conditions, a person who becomes lost may enter a deserted network of steep lanes, stairs, courtyards, balconies, retaining walls, and sudden drops that cannot be reconciled with the surrounding city. entries.title: Kyrien: Family, Justice, and Recruitment
entries.subtitle: Character Continuity
entries.text: Kyrien: Family, Justice, and Recruitment Character Continuity The father's persecution, years spent financing justice, the shop humiliation, represented recruitment, and the unresolved conditions for later revenge. Kyrien: Family, Justice, and Recruitment The author-confirmed origin behind After the Failed Attempt v3. This record separates the full history from what Kyrien and the reader know in the Chapter. The origin precedes his recruitment in early Arc 1 by years; its beginning has no assigned date or Arc. His father's persecution Kyrien's father is a military-police commander. During the arrest and attempted escape of a fugitive, he intervenes to protect his officers. The fugitive assaults him. He survives and kills the fugitive in self-defence, unmistakably witnessing magic during the confrontation. He tells nobody, including his son. Existing government officials linked directly or indirectly to the Magiarchy learn what happened. His competence, professional credibility, and independence make them doubt that his continued silence can be guaranteed. A senior prosecutor helps initiate a fabricated case to discredit him and force his submission. Each successful rebuttal brings another allegation; the pressure eventually reaches his family. He will not accept a false account of his conduct, but continues to keep the magical encounter private. When the prosecution fails to make him controllable, the officials directing it obtain the necessary sanction to escalate. He is murdered. His death is presented as suicide, with public suggestions of shame, instability, and fear of further revelations. The suppression doctrine supplies the magical justification: the Church holds final sanction, and Magiarchal resources act within that framework. No named individual has yet been assigned the sanction or killing; do not assume Fionn or Mikhail ordered either. Responsibility belongs to officials making particular decisions, not a new faction called hidden authorities. Some know the magical purpose. Others accept confidential national-security instructions, protect colleagues, or lack the access to question what they are told. Ordinary investigators and administrative staff need not know magic exists. The years he pays for justice His father's death and disgrace devastate his mother. She increasingly struggles with ordinary life, and Kyrien takes on much of her care. She retains preferences, habits, judgment, and occasional attempts at independence. Her dependence is not her entire personality. Kyrien initially believes capable professionals can prove the wrong and persuade the wider system to act. He works extra shifts and additional jobs, postpones ambitions, and repeatedly sacrifices money to support his mother and pay for representation. Work, consultations, invoices, and responsibilities at home leave him exhausted. He has no professional legal expertise. Lawyers research the law, examine evidence, pursue remedies, identify patterns across manipulated proceedings, and coordinate the case. He pays, supplies family papers, remembers events, answers questions, and follows up. Recognizing a discrepancy about his own family does not make him an investigator who independently reconstructs a prosecutorial network. At least one lawyer is both competent and honest. Their work helps trigger an independent inquiry into the senior prosecutor. A preliminary review confirms that important evidence against the commander was knowingly distorted. Kyrien permits himself to hope that the years of work have purchased a real chance of justice. A closed review then accepts the prosecutor's conduct under a confidential national-security mandate. Officials with Magiarchy connections protect the underlying reason; others accept the restricted explanation without learning it. The prosecutor is publicly vindicated. The family's inquiry is recast as a malicious campaign against an honourable public servant. The lawyers can explain what they proved and why the available routes are blocked. They cannot make the state enforce consequences it has chosen to prevent. Someone Kyrien respects privately admits his father was wronged, then insists the country cannot afford the consequences of pursuing responsibility. Their identity is not fixed. There is an interval after this defeat. Kyrien keeps working and caring for his mother. His faith in obtaining justice has collapsed, but he has not yet decided on murder. The shop and the decision His mother has begun trying small errands again. Kyrien accompanies her to a neighbourhood shop. A customer recognizes her and repeats the public claim that the family tried to ruin an honourable prosecutor for compensation or personal advantage. The casual accusation is especially bitter after years spent paying legal fees. She struggles to defend her husband. The shopkeeper asks her to stop making a scene. One person watches; another looks away. Nobody has been sent to intimidate her. The official vindication has made the accusation ordinary enough for strangers to repeat. Kyrien intervenes and takes her outside without attacking anyone or announcing his intentions. Afterward she says: "I'm sorry. I thought I could manage the shopping." She treats the humiliation as her own failure. Only after getting her home and attending to her needs does he decide to kill the prosecutor. He knows that his mother needs him and that the decision risks taking away the person still supporting her. He continues his outward routine while preparing deliberately. Her care during his absences must be credible, and work and exhaustion must remain in his life. The Prosecutor General The senior prosecutor is promoted to Prosecutor General. A formal dinner celebrates the appointment and presents his survival of the supposed smear campaign as evidence of integrity. MSF assists with security through its existing government contracts. Lynleit attends and remains professionally civil despite privately disliking him. Kyrien's attempt fails partly because of the target's concealed connection to the magical world. Kyrien sees nothing that reveals magic. He escapes immediate capture and leaves insufficient evidence for a conclusive case; police detain him later because of his history, motive, and possible involvement. His practical resourcefulness has roots in his father's military contacts and instruction. It does not make him a flawless professional assassin. Lynleit is nearly harmed without his knowing she attended. She never tells him. The prosecutor's connection to the Magiarchy is confirmed; whether he is himself a Magus is not. Do not restore the older description of him as a confirmed Magus politician. The interrogation and terms Kyrien is exhausted, guarded, and worried about his mother. Years of legal consultations have taught him to follow advice, withhold damaging information, and notice questions that invite an admission. He does not conduct his own defence as an expert. MSF's participation in the security investigation gives Lynleit access to questioning, not unlimited police or judicial authority. Legal representation remains active. Her certainty that Kyrien carried out the attempt exceeds what the available evidence conclusively establishes; he refuses to close that gap with a confession. Employment records and payment histories show her what his legal campaign cost. She asks why he crossed the line after, rather than immediately upon, the inquiry's defeat. The author's dialogue anchor survives in v3: "You were still paying your lawyers after the review." / "They were still answering." / "Then something changed." / "They started on my mother." He can acknowledge the family's treatment without admitting the attempt. She asks whether someone is with his mother and arranges confirmation of her welfare. She never threatens her. Continued detention already risks separating Kyrien from someone who depends on him. Lynleit recognizes the suppression operation through information she can access. She conceals that recognition, the existence of magic, her attendance at the dinner, and her full recruitment motives. Admiration of his competence, guilt about the injustice of the magical order, and her intuition of approaching danger all contribute. Her suspicion of Helena remains grounded in existing questions about Fionn's movements and household, not foreknowledge of his assassination. She offers help obtaining release from immediate custody, protection against continued scrutiny, and a possible cleaner future in exchange for confidential service. She cannot promise unconditional immunity. Income, care for his mother, and the possibility of leaving must be discussed. His family responsibilities survive recruitment. He agrees reluctantly, recognizing her leverage and self-interest; she gains cooperation without trust. She subsequently tells only Felix and Reiner inside her established circle. Fionn remains uninformed. Reiner trusts her judgment. Felix accepts her decision without trusting Kyrien. Reader and character knowledge Kyrien knows nothing unmistakably magical through the persecution, assassination attempt, questioning, or initial service. His father told him nothing. His first undeniable exposure is seeing Lynleit walk on water during the river incident. He tells nobody; she initially has reason to suspect rather than certain knowledge of what he saw. Both father and son encounter magic and remain silent. The father's independence and capacity to threaten Magi contributed to his elimination; similar qualities make the son indispensable to Lynleit. Let the parallel emerge from their circumstances rather than turning it into a supernatural inheritance. V3 shows the legal success and institutional refusal, the shop, and the interview. A separate Lynleit viewpoint recognizes suppression; it does not pass that knowledge to Kyrien. The father's actual magical encounter remains in the full reference history, not an event witnessed in this Chapter. See Events, Witnesses, and Reveals. Later revenge: confirmed direction and open rule The unplaced Moment The Prosecutor's Return carries this direction into Story and character scene listings without assigning it a phase. The Prosecutor General remains a recurring figure. Lynleit continues to deal civilly with him in professional settings despite her dislike and knowledge of what happened to Kyrien's family. Much later, after Kyrien openly knows about Magi and Lynleit knows he possesses that knowledge, the prosecutor commits a fresh transgression serious enough for the Magi framework's punitive jurisdiction. Lynleit deliberately offers Kyrien a possibility of revenge as an incentive. He sees the manipulation. Her condition is genuine proof of an offence serious enough for the contemplated punishment. Their hatred, dislike, and the family's suffering cannot stand in for that proof. The offence and its prohibition are not yet selected. One development route is misuse of Magiarchy connections or suppression powers to control state leadership or remove officials obstructing his ambitions. Ordinary political involvement is insufficient: Magiarchs already have political interests, and Church envoys political functions. Define an actual abuse, establish the rule before the accusation becomes central, and make its jurisdiction apply regardless of the prosecutor's still-undecided magical status. This later offence is separate from the protected persecution of Kyrien's father. Revenge may become possible without any institution withdrawing that earlier protection or admitting responsibility. Punishment is a possibility, not a completed event. No execution, new power, exact law, or timeline slot is established here. Draft choices and audit boundary V3's unnamed lawyer, neighbour, tea, bread, payment details, interview blocking, and written employment terms provide concrete scene staging. They do not establish a named cast member, an exact salary, the date of the father's death, a new Narvean statute, or the identity of the official who sanctioned the murder. The neighbour is a familiar paid caregiver in this draft, not a resolution of the sister's circumstances or a permanent family arrangement. The Nasu advisory audit focuses on the competent legal work achieving truth but not accountability, the mother's ordinary attempted independence, and the difference between later punishment and institutional redress. It preserves mixed motives and uneven knowledge without proposing another faction or treating coercive recruitment as attraction. Kyrien's legal and magical knowledge stay bounded. No physical capability score changes. The exact attack choreography, people who authorized the original operation, later prohibition and jurisdiction, mother's continuing care arrangements, and later revenge timing belong in Questions. The author's new facts supersede the older all-powerful transfer-clause interpretation; they are not an unresolved contradiction requiring another decision. Author's Desk

entries.title: Magecraft: Structure, Leverage, and Cost
entries.subtitle: Magecraft Doctrine
entries.text: Magecraft: Structure, Leverage, and Cost Magecraft Doctrine A practical guide to magecraft mechanics, internal and external practice, limitations, Holumn manifestations, and the need for control. Magecraft: Structure, Leverage, and Cost Magecraft and miracle-making Magecraft uses conditions already present in reality. A Magus perceives a point of strain or weakness and deliberately alters it. Fire can be encouraged to start, matter weakened, attention sharpened, or perception redirected. The effect requires something to act upon. Miracle-making is a separate, forbidden category. The Church condemns acts that imitate sacred deeds associated with Jesus, saints, saviours, and other religious figures, even when the immediate effect is harmless. Lynleit's water walking falls within this prohibition. Two directions of practice Thaumaturgy Thaumaturgy acts outward upon the surrounding world. Its effects can usually be observed or measured. Igniting or suppressing fire Reinforcing or weakening material Changing concentration or distribution Altering physical sensation Redirecting an environmental process Theurgy Theurgy acts upon the operator's perception, thought, identity, or relationship to the world. Expanding awareness Altering perception Recalibrating thought and emotion Integrating spiritual experience Changing the way identity is understood An inward change can carry risks as serious as a visible physical intervention. The continuum Thaumaturgy and theurgy are categories within one connected reality. An outward spell requires an adjustment in its operator. A change in perception or identity changes how that person acts upon the world. Matter, perception, emotion, probability, agency, and cognition belong to the same natural structure. The distinction between inward and outward practice describes the principal direction of an act, not a complete separation. Magi Magi are human. Their unusual perception lets them identify conditions that other people cannot detect, and their training lets them intervene deliberately. Talent is rare and unevenly distributed. Training alone does not guarantee it. Power depends on both perception and control. Fionn's precise blue flame and Lynleit's dangerous volume illustrate different uses of the same inherited ability. Holumn manifestations Fear, memory, fixation, and psychic strain can produce Holumns. The source may be an individual or a population, and its manifestation need not be a creature. Weather, events, disembodied wills, and curses also belong to the category. A visible body may be only one part of a manifestation. Containment therefore requires evidence about its circumstances, repeated conditions, people, and objects as well as its physical form. Incident records and known countermeasures are collected in Holumns. Limits and cost Magecraft cannot create something from nothing or erase the foundational conditions upon which it works. Every intervention changes an existing balance and can meet resistance. Overuse can destabilize the affected system. Poor judgment can direct force into the wrong place. Greater force increases exposure to backlash. A successful effect can cause harmful secondary consequences. Precision can achieve what a larger display cannot. Its value depends on the operator understanding the conditions well enough to avoid unwanted effects. Authority and secrecy The Magiarchy regulates sanctioned practice and cooperates with the Church in containment. The Church needs Magi to suppress threats ordinary institutions cannot handle, but watches for uncontrolled practice and forbidden miracles. Renegade Magi reject the arrangement. Both the Church and the Magiarchates pursue them. Most people do not know magic exists. Some clergy, officials, and advisers receive limited knowledge. The Church holds final sanction over suppression; Magiarchal resources may investigate, contain, coerce, recruit, or remove witnesses under that authority. Exposure can provoke Church retaliation, public panic, or conflict inside Magi institutions. Disagreement over what to conceal and how to conceal it persists within the sanctioned order. entries.text: MAGIARCHY Prose Style · v1 Writer's Style Reference The working house style: narrative voice, focalization, comic timing, dialogue, rhythm, imagery, and reader inference, developed through the Chapters. MAGIARCHY Prose Style This is the working house style for Chapters. Its starting point is the author's preference for concrete scenes, unruly conversation, unsettling supernatural rules, and intimacy that intrudes on a story concerned with other things. It develops through actual Chapters rather than through imitation of another writer. Use this document alongside Prose and Scene Guidance, which owns revision boundaries and development approaches. This document owns narrative voice and craft choices. Narrative voice and focalization Default: third-person past tense with a clearly established focal character. Let the narration borrow that person's vocabulary and immediate concerns through free indirect discourse, without turning every thought into an italicized monologue. Stay close during fear, embarrassment, discovery, and difficult decisions. A character can notice a wet cuff before understanding a curse. Widen the psychic distance for travel, repeated failed attempts, elapsed time, or a rule already established in the scene. Change focalization at a section or scene break. In Doom Has an Address, Lynleit's research and Kyrien's incomplete account require separate access to their thoughts. Neither should know what the other has concealed simply because the narrator does. The narrator may be dry, observant, and briefly amused. Comic commentary is welcome when it sharpens a particular absurdity. Avoid an omniscient verdict that explains what every gesture proves about the cast. Tonal register and counterpoint The principal register combines precise observation with conversational ease. Technical language belongs to a character solving a technical problem; it should not become everyone's inner voice. Let terror, ordinary inconvenience, and embarrassment occupy the same scene without cancelling one another. The fatal curse remains fatal while Lynleit objects to the proposed solution. A lost jacket can matter to her without being the emotional thesis of the river chapter. Humor often comes from unequal seriousness: the answer is technically useful, socially unbearable, and delivered by someone enjoying that discrepancy. Do not make every character equally witty. Reiner need not return Felix's joke; Kyrien's plain question can cause more trouble than a clever retort. The Nasu advisory framework may help test a rule, exception, or dramatic consequence. It does not supply a borrowed voice, stock catchphrase, or permission to imitate a particular author's prose. Scene, summary, and exposition Dramatize the point where someone must answer, act, refuse, or reconsider. Summarize the travel and repeated research that bring them there. A supernatural explanation earns space when it changes the available choices. Natalia's explanation of the ego is a discovery in this scene, not background terminology the narrator should give Lynleit beforehand. Mikhail contributes a different body of evidence before giving an embarrassingly practical answer. Preserve the discovery sequence : observation, interpretation, objection, revised possibility. Let an explanation meet resistance. The listener may interrupt for the wrong reason, misunderstand a word, or resent a perfectly accurate answer. “Show, don't tell” is a preference for dramatizing important experience, not a ban on exposition. State a mechanism plainly when withholding it would confuse the scene. Do not then explain its emotional meaning after the reader has already watched the reaction. Dialogue, idiolect, and subtext Speech should carry at least one immediate purpose: obtain an answer, evade it, test a premise, provoke, reassure, delay, or end the conversation. The purpose need not match what the speaker admits. Lynleit Idiolect: specific questions, impatient objections, attempts to return a discussion to its useful conclusion. She can handle professional disclosure yet become evasive when the subject is personally embarrassing. Repeated denials may expose what she intends to close. Natalia Idiolect: precise definitions, associative examples, a former teacher's questions, and dry corrections. She enjoys making Lynleit follow a sound argument to an unwelcome conclusion. Do not remove her playfulness in order to make her seem intelligent. Father Mikhail Idiolect: patient doctrinal explanation followed by unexpectedly blunt ordinary language. He continues giving useful advice while Lynleit is trying to escape the conversation. His irreverence does not erase his conviction or severity elsewhere. Kyrien Idiolect: short questions, literal observation, suspicion when someone's behavior changes. He can recognize that something happened without possessing the missing explanation. Frustration does not require a confession or an eloquent speech. These are observations from the current Chapters, not scripts for every future line. MBTI and function emphasis support a characterization check; they do not dictate syntax or replace personal history. Prefer unobtrusive dialogue tags. Use action beats when they locate a speaker, change the timing, or reveal divided attention. A page turned without being read does more here than several descriptions of hidden desire. Comic timing and repetition Distinguish redundant exposition from comic repetition . Repeated information can be cut; a repeated denial may be the action of the scene. Preserve the setup, escalation, pause, reversal, and closing beat when revising a comic exchange. Read it aloud before removing a line. In Doom Version 3: The examination routine restores the old teacher-student relationship before Natalia supplies the ego hypothesis. The academically respectable answer sets up the instruction to consult a priest. Mikhail's apparent consideration of centuries of theology delays an exceptionally blunt answer. His repeated use of Lynleit's name accompanies successive stages of her exit. “It worked” and “By failing” make the same recovery mean different things to the speakers. The later “I haven't asked anything” exchange recalls the earlier call. The repetition now exposes Lynleit's anticipation. Natalia's final question works because the preceding silence has made Lynleit keep talking. Do not compress this into a summary that says Natalia teased her. Do not explain the punchline afterward. A joke may need several apparently unnecessary lines to establish its timing. Syntax, rhythm, and paragraphing Use complete, varied sentences for the narrative baseline. Alternate longer sentences that follow observation or reasoning with shorter sentences at a decision or interruption. Short paragraphs and fragments are emphasis tools. A whole chapter of isolated declarations gives every detail the same weight. Dialogue can remain one utterance per paragraph because the white space controls turn-taking and pace. Use a deliberately repeated structure for a specific effect, then leave it. Avoid habitual three-part lists, mirrored reversals, and final sentences that restate the paragraph in grander language. Keep tense consistent unless a quoted document or deliberate temporal shift requires otherwise. No em dashes. Diction and imagery Prefer concrete verbs, recognizable materials, and specific physical relationships. Fishing line, a soaked sleeve, an unread page, and a notebook are useful because someone can touch or act on them. Choose imagery through focalization. Lynleit may notice dress and composure; Kyrien may notice a change in someone's movements. Neither should become an all-purpose sensor reporting every detail. Use an extended metaphor only while it helps the reader reason. Natalia's address metaphor makes the curse's recognition understandable; it should not spread into every description of affection, leadership, or domestic life. Do not justify an appearance or defend a character after every flawed response. Do not label an ordinary feeling as profound. Leave room for awkwardness that remains awkward. Subtext, ellipsis, and reader knowledge Subtext is what a reader can infer from speech, behavior, juxtaposition, or omission. It is not a fact the author has not decided yet. Ellipsis may omit an encounter while showing its consequences. Doom Version 3 does not narrate the incomplete attempt itself. The next call and Kyrien's account establish what they can establish; exact choreography remains unresolved. Mark Chapter preface and Moment conclusions as inferred only when the scene supplies evidence without stating the conclusion. If a revision makes the explanation explicit, change the label. Do not explain a purple inference in narration merely to make it easier to validate. Keep later consequences out of an earlier scene's closing summary unless a flash-forward is a deliberate narrative choice. Terminology and researched allusion Physicians are ordinary medical professionals without knowledge of magic unless the author explicitly establishes an exception. Do not invent a class of physicians treating thaumaturgy. A medical examination, if used, must preserve that ignorance and show or account for concealment. Doom Version 3 uses Magi's examination of the curse and does not add an off-page physician visit. Natalia introduces the ego hypothesis and attributes the psychological definition to Jung. Her application of it to the curse belongs to fictional magecraft, not to Jung's claim. Brief quotations must be verified; store their source here rather than interrupting dialogue with research apparatus. The short definition quoted in Version 3 is reproduced in the C. G. Jung Society of Sydney's account of ego, shame, and embodiment. Only that definition is quoted. The curse mechanism and Natalia's proposed use of reciprocal change are fictional. Revision protocol Before drafting or editing a Chapter or Moment, read this document, the chosen source version, and the relevant character records. Identify the focal character, discovery sequence, emotional pressure, and any dialogue whose timing must survive. During revision, keep two separate passes: 1. Dramatic pass: continuity, knowledge, choices, voice, discovery, and the function of each exchange. 2. Line-edit pass: cadence, diction, repetition, dialogue tags, paragraphing, and unnecessary explanation. Compare the result against the source. Restore any lost joke, disagreement, or character-specific awkwardness that was removed merely for concision. Recheck the preface, Moment, and F/M/S anchors against the actual revised paragraphs. Afterward, add a concise entry below only when the Chapter teaches us a reusable style choice. Give its source, craft term, example or location, and limit. Separate author decisions from editorial working choices. Do not accumulate a new absolute rule for every attractive sentence. Style decisions in use Author direction: 5 September 2026 Preserve original banter and comic repetition. Natalia originates the ego idea and quotes Jung. Do not introduce magic-aware physicians. Limit: a joke's timing does not excuse duplicate explanations elsewhere. Working implementation: Doom Has an Address, Version 3 Past-tense narration, sectioned focalization, exposition through adversarial dialogue, callbacks, exit beats, and an elliptical encounter. Limit: these devices do not require every Chapter to be comic or withhold its central action. Under review: later Chapters Refine the house style from what the author accepts in finished scenes. Limit: no new event or character trait becomes canon through this document. Version 3 is based on the earlier Version 2 text preserved in commit 868fc31 , before the prose rewrite in b06c821 . It restores that dialogue-led treatment, applies the author's corrections, and is now the canonical version. Versions 1 and 2 remain accessible alternates. Author's Desk

Author direction and implementation: Doom Has an Address, v4 Natalia teaches complex topics through practical examples and personal attempts, failures, and discoveries. Lynleit remains a whimsical, loyal student and friend; intellectual asymmetry is visible without a superior-subordinate social rhythm. The worked diagram, decision diary, resignation anecdote, and Myka call implement that direction in v4. Preserve the curse outcome and the earlier comic callbacks. Limit: an anecdote must earn its place by changing the listener's understanding. Do not manufacture a major invention, past relationship, or magical success merely to supply an example. Version 3 derives from the earlier Version 2 text in commit 868fc31 , before the rewrite in b06c821 . Version 4 builds on v3 and revises Natalia's teaching and the teacher-student dialogue. Version 5 retains that text and adds Mikhail's mock blessing. Version 6 adapts the author's Russian exchange. Version 7 restores nine author-approved performance beats and supplies shared canon. Versions 1 through 6 remain accessible alternates. Historical implementation: Doom Has an Address, v5 Mock encomium and bathos: Mikhail gives each phrase of an exaggerated honorific the cadence of a blessing. Lynleit's stopped pen interrupts the register. She asks him to speak normally; the unchanged mundane insult answers that request. Keep the declaration short enough that the listener's confusion remains the turning point. His seated patience, her successive attempts to leave, and the later notebook joke retain their original timing. Delayed recognition: the address to her father's household lets a first-time reader detect private knowledge without yet identifying its source. The author has confirmed Fionn's Magi-lineage association with the Cult of Inanna and Lynleit's indirect association without direct participation. That withholding governed v5. The author's v6 exchange replaces it by naming Inanna and discussing the lineage openly. Jungian editorial lens: inherited identity, conscious self-description, desire, and embarrassment can pull in different directions. Here the imposed honorific makes an expectation personal before Lynleit can dismiss it as theory. This is a craft reading of the scene, not a diagnosis, a new Jung quotation, or a rule that shame causes transformation. Natalia's existing attributed definition remains the Chapter's psychological reference; see the Jung Society source above. Limit: Mikhail's phrase "divine whore" is his mocking allusion. It establishes neither an authentic liturgical quotation nor compulsory cult practice. His insult is not the narrator's judgment about sexual inexperience. No borrowed character name, catchphrase, or imported fictional theology belongs in the scene. Author direction and working implementation: Doom Has an Address, v6 Author direction: sexual subjects involving the main cast should be psychologically revealing, funny, raw, and memorable where the scene supports comedy. Adapt the supplied exchange, preserving its useful lore and slapstick rather than merely making the language respectable. This does not require erotic comedy in every intimate or frightening scene. Register clash and mock encomium: Mikhail rises to deliver an ornate invocation, then sits, drinks, and speaks crudely. The register changes are deliberate acts by the speaker. His knowledge supplies the material; his timing makes it embarrassing. Keep his practical answer and its uncertainty intact so the scene remains a consultation. Prop business and status negotiation: Lynleit's cup repeatedly gives her hands somewhere to go. Mikhail notices and names it; she answers with the porcelain retort. Preserve her capacity to resist. Her increasingly abstract principles defend a private discomfort, while her ordinary professional openness remains unchanged. Escalation and selective compression: keep repetitions that change the stakes: inappropriate wording, rejected objection, personal genealogy, an attempted exit, and the final threat. Cut acknowledgments or objections that only confirm the previous line. The authorial source's elaborate pauses become selected action beats rather than a fragment after every movement. Subtext and explicit exposition: v6 names Inanna and states the lineage's long association. Do not label that information inferred. The cup, formal defence, and threat carry the private embarrassment without a narrator explaining the double insult. Mikhail's monastic composure and Lynleit's defensive formality are character-specific, not universal male or female behavior. Scene breaks and closing tag: a break isolates Mikhail's private last joke from Lynleit's corridor reaction. The notebook callback preserves the earlier Chapter, while the priest's coda belongs to the author's new exchange. Limit: the priest's accusation is personal mockery, not an objective finding that Lynleit has failed a religious duty. The ancestry is not the source of her desire for Kyrien. A Jungian reading may attend to the difference between her declared indifference and her behavior, but it does not establish a clinical diagnosis or give Mikhail access to her unspoken thoughts. Author-approved restoration: Doom Has an Address, v7 Performance beats and comic delay: the author approved the priestly calm, Lynleit's hope for discretion, finger-counting assessment, delayed reply to the insult, accidental defence, porcelain setup, withheld joke, ancient-versus-present problem, and farewell/coda pacing. Preserve these as turns in the exchange rather than compressing them into a description of teasing. Blocking and prop continuity: a restored gesture must fit the actions around it. Lynleit returns the cup during the porcelain setup; later she leaves it alone rather than setting it down again. The prop reveals divided attention without narration explaining that her hands need occupation. Withheld response: after repeatedly exploiting her hesitation, Mikhail lets one averted glance pass. The reader can notice this change without a verdict announcing tenderness. A character's restraint can be visible through an expected action they do not perform. Reaction and reply: Lynleit's denial of agreement, correction from defence to principle, and porcelain retort keep her an active participant. Allow the silence after an insult to land before either speaker resumes. Limit: these are approved choices for this exchange, not instructions to give every joke a long pause or every provocative character a reassuring moment. Natalia's explanation, Mikhail's uncertain treatment, and the later outcome remain unchanged. Author direction: 8 September 2026 Subplot hierarchy: intimacy develops inside the ongoing political, magical, and institutional story. It must not reorganize every character's priorities around romance. The hotel refuge is grief and nonsexual comfort; do not eroticize it or use it as a shortcut to the later sexual milestones. Embodied motive and rationalization: Lynleit's curiosity and attachment precede the research she uses to manage embarrassment. Distinguish general knowledge from skill adapted to one person. Reuse an established tell sparingly rather than narrating a lesson about the callback. Ellipsis and unfinished prose: The Bench under the Lamp v2 leaves a marked writer gap between the supplied approach and aftermath. Do not disguise an undrafted passage as a deliberate finished ellipsis, or replace the omitted action with an invented kiss. Its preface describes only what the prose shows or supports; the Moment's continuity keeps the author's separate milestones explicit. Delayed comic consequence: let the bench seem finished, let Lynleit enjoy her success, and move the pair down the path before the whiskey request. Kyrien's decision not to demand an explanation preserves the last exchange. The flask should already have an ordinary use, not appear solely to serve this joke. Prequel restraint: Arc 0 develops unfinished habits through candidate experiences rather than repeating adult personalities in younger bodies. Keep its unselected scenes in development records. Fionn's own work and household remain its center. Limit: these directions do not make grief a prescription for sex, ancestry an obligation, alcohol a treatment, or every private gesture an interpretable symbol. Author correction: source fidelity and character blocking Blocking: retain the supplied approach, setting, and sequence where drafted. A substitute romantic gesture changes the scene even if the emotional destination seems similar. The park revision removes the unrequested kiss and preserves the original research-success line. Character exposition: preparation need not equal experience. Lynleit brings theoretical knowledge, learns that a particular person does not behave exactly like an account on paper, and becomes interested in his responses beyond her initial wish to prove herself. Kyrien also observes her. Keep that reciprocal observation distinct from a one-sided demonstration of mastery. The complete intimate passage remains for the author, not concealed inside instructional prose. Editorial lacuna: use > [WRITER: concise non-graphic completion notice] for an undrafted passage. The amber callout is an editorial marker, not a fictional event. Preserve the source in the timestamped backlog archive and retain the surrounding dialogue and aftermath. Do not count the gap as shown or inferred evidence in the preface. Character attention: author answers from 12 September 2026 Use the Cognition and Physical Competence reference for the full facts and uncertain type readings. Focalization and divided attention: Lynleit can seek help articulating an internal answer while concealing distress. Trusted reassurance need not remove her unease. Narrative voice and focalization The default is third-person past tense, close to a clearly established character. Let their vocabulary and immediate concerns enter the narration. Widen the view for travel, elapsed time, and repeated attempts. Change the focal character at a scene or section break; concealed knowledge does not pass between minds through the narrator. Keep the narrator observant and dry. A brief amused remark can belong, especially beside an absurdly serious action. Avoid a verdict about everybody's motives. The Nasu advisory framework can test rules and consequences; it is not permission to borrow another writer's voice. Dialogue and explanation Speakers want different things from the same conversation. One needs an answer, another wants the premise corrected, and a third has noticed an opportunity for a joke. Allow a question to go unanswered when that is what the character would do. Not every conversation needs an interruption. Lynleit asks specific questions and wants a useful conclusion. She values professional openness but grows evasive about personal embarrassment. With Natalia she is a whimsical, loyal former student and friend. Keep her objections intelligent even when her professor knows much more. Natalia starts from an example her listener can follow. Her own failed attempts can be as useful as her successes. Show what she tried, what happened, and what she changed. Let Lynleit misunderstand or object without turning every reply into the next step of a flawless lesson. Mikhail can explain doctrine patiently and then say something appallingly ordinary. His advice can still be useful. His comedy does not erase his convictions or severity. Kyrien notices, asks short questions, and can arrive at an answer before he can explain his reasoning. He does not automatically know what somebody has hidden. Felix offers jokes and possibilities, including reassurance he is still privately testing. Reiner need not join in. Sherie enjoys teasing even off duty. An unexpected response can change her understanding of the whole exchange. These are tendencies, not quotas. Use unobtrusive dialogue tags. A gesture should locate the person, affect timing, or show what their attention is doing. Explain a mechanism when the reader needs it to follow a choice. Keep the limit of an analogy clear: names crossed out on paper are not a spell. Natalia introduces the ego hypothesis in Doom and attributes its psychological definition to Jung. The proposed curse treatment is fictional magecraft. Research sources are in Style History. Comic timing Preserve setup, delay, repetition, and the reply that makes the delay worthwhile. A repeated denial may be the action of the scene. Check the whole exchange before cutting an apparently unnecessary line. “The organ had fallen silent. Felix had not.” belongs to that church and that nuisance. Keep such specific short declarations. Do not replace them with a general claim about silence or human nature. Lynleit can be embarrassed and still answer sharply. Let a joke stop where it lands. Do not explain afterward why it was endearing, revealing, or ironic. Repetition is useful when deliberate, not when every paragraph ends in the same contrast or three-part list. Keep objects available for ordinary use. A cup occupies hands, a jacket can be lost, a notebook can contain a question someone would rather not ask aloud. They need not become symbols every time. Preserve awkwardness, uneven attention, and occasional bluntness. Do not roughen clean prose with artificial mistakes, and do not polish every section into equal length. Appearance states observable facts without defending the outfit. Dread and action Use Dread and Action Direction when a scene involves frightening exploration, a Holumn, or physical danger. Keep the reader close to what the focal character can perceive and attempt. Establish the useful geography before speed matters. Let a sound, distance, bodily limitation, or altered familiar detail change a decision instead of repeatedly naming the atmosphere as sinister. Give survival, quiet, and existing character-specific humor room to register. Do not explain away the remaining horror after a temporary success. Intimacy and changes of register Sex occupies little space in the larger story but can change much. A joke, glance, memory, or sensual detail should earn its place through this character's attention or a specific consequence. Established intimacy does not displace work and ordinary life. Do not append a sentence certifying it. An undecided fact is not subtext; an undrafted passage is not a finished ellipsis. Use blue for what a scene shows or states, purple for a conclusion its evidence leaves the reader to infer. Outline records stay neutral. An amber > [WRITER: ...] notice identifies a genuine omission. Preserve the surrounding action without inventing a substitute. State uncertainty precisely and once where possible. Keep consequential limits, not a defensive list of every conclusion a reader must avoid. Public records describe the world; editorial work belongs in Docs. Revision practice Read the chosen current text and relevant character facts before editing. First check what happens, who knows it, and what each speaker wants. Then edit cadence and unnecessary explanation. Compare against the source for lost jokes, recurring gestures, tactical reasoning, and deliberate repetition. Recheck prefaces, Moment facts, and paragraph-note anchors if prose changes. Canon synchronization does not require identical wording in every record. Do not add another permanent style rule just because one revision worked. A rule needs the author's reusable approval or a preference demonstrated across accepted passages. Keep specific Chapter findings in Style History. Use npm run prose:audit as a prompt for rereading, never as a demand to replace a word. No em dashes. Use magecraft for trained practice and magic for the underlying phenomenon. Physicians are ordinary professionals without magical knowledge unless the author establishes otherwise. Author's Desk

entries.title: MAGIARCHY Prose Style · v2
entries.subtitle: Writer's Style Reference
entries.text: MAGIARCHY Prose Style · v2 Writer's Style Reference House style for narrative voice, dialogue, comic timing, and practical exposition, including Natalia's worked examples and her friendship with Lynleit. MAGIARCHY Prose Style This is the working house style for Chapters. Its starting point is the author's preference for concrete scenes, unruly conversation, unsettling supernatural rules, and intimacy that intrudes on a story concerned with other things. It develops through actual Chapters rather than through imitation of another writer. Use this document alongside Prose and Scene Guidance, which owns revision boundaries and development approaches. This document owns narrative voice and craft choices. Narrative voice and focalization Default: third-person past tense with a clearly established focal character. Let the narration borrow that person's vocabulary and immediate concerns through free indirect discourse, without turning every thought into an italicized monologue. Stay close during fear, embarrassment, discovery, and difficult decisions. A character can notice a wet cuff before understanding a curse. Widen the psychic distance for travel, repeated failed attempts, elapsed time, or a rule already established in the scene. Change focalization at a section or scene break. In Doom Has an Address, Lynleit's research and Kyrien's incomplete account require separate access to their thoughts. Neither should know what the other has concealed simply because the narrator does. The narrator may be dry, observant, and briefly amused. Comic commentary is welcome when it sharpens a particular absurdity. Avoid an omniscient verdict that explains what every gesture proves about the cast. Tonal register and counterpoint The principal register combines precise observation with conversational ease. Technical language belongs to a character solving a technical problem; it should not become everyone's inner voice. Let terror, ordinary inconvenience, and embarrassment occupy the same scene without cancelling one another. The fatal curse remains fatal while Lynleit objects to the proposed solution. A lost jacket can matter to her without being the emotional thesis of the river chapter. Humor often comes from unequal seriousness: the answer is technically useful, socially unbearable, and delivered by someone enjoying that discrepancy. Do not make every character equally witty. Reiner need not return Felix's joke; Kyrien's plain question can cause more trouble than a clever retort. The Nasu advisory framework may help test a rule, exception, or dramatic consequence. It does not supply a borrowed voice, stock catchphrase, or permission to imitate a particular author's prose. Scene, summary, and exposition Dramatize the point where someone must answer, act, refuse, or reconsider. Summarize the travel and repeated research that bring them there. A supernatural explanation earns space when it changes the available choices. Natalia's explanation of the ego is a discovery in this scene, not background terminology the narrator should give Lynleit beforehand. Mikhail contributes a different body of evidence before giving an embarrassingly practical answer. Preserve the discovery sequence : observation, interpretation, objection, revised possibility. Let an explanation meet resistance. The listener may interrupt for the wrong reason, misunderstand a word, or resent a perfectly accurate answer. “Show, don't tell” is a preference for dramatizing important experience, not a ban on exposition. State a mechanism plainly when withholding it would confuse the scene. Do not then explain its emotional meaning after the reader has already watched the reaction. Dialogue, idiolect, and subtext Speech should carry at least one immediate purpose: obtain an answer, evade it, test a premise, provoke, reassure, delay, or end the conversation. The purpose need not match what the speaker admits. Lynleit Idiolect: specific questions, impatient objections, attempts to return a discussion to its useful conclusion. She can handle professional disclosure yet become evasive when the subject is personally embarrassing. Repeated denials may expose what she intends to close. With Natalia, keep the whimsy and loyalty of a favourite student who has become a friend. Lynleit may joke about marks, challenge a conclusion, or offer her professor an absurd favour. She also listens, tries the example, and asks the next useful question. Show the difference in expertise through what Natalia notices or corrects, not through formal submission or a loss of Lynleit's intelligence. Natalia Idiolect: concrete demonstrations, personal research anecdotes, precise definitions, a former teacher's questions, and dry corrections. She enjoys making Lynleit follow a sound argument to an unwelcome conclusion. Do not remove her playfulness in order to make her seem intelligent. Use worked examples and instructional scaffolding : begin with an object, action, or familiar problem; let the listener make a prediction; introduce the difficult term after its purpose is apparent. Have the listener apply the idea to a new case rather than merely say that it makes sense. These are craft tools, not a compulsory sequence for every conversation. Her personal examples should include an attempted approach, an observable result, and what she changed afterward. Failure can be useful teaching material without secretly making every failed experiment a triumph. In Doom v4, the decision diary exposes her habit of inventing reasonable explanations after choosing; comparing predictions with actions gives her a better question, not a universal answer. Her resignation and a missed call from Myka provide different examples of habits and attachment. Limit analogical transfer explicitly where it matters. Names on paper illustrate the shared attachment; crossing them out is not a spell. Concern for a niece illustrates attention reorganized around another person; it does not prove romantic desire or guarantee the cure. Keep Natalia's practical warmth distinct from certainty about an untested hypothesis. Use personal stories where they clarify this problem, not as decorative memoirs between lectures. Father Mikhail Idiolect: patient doctrinal explanation followed by unexpectedly blunt ordinary language. He continues giving useful advice while Lynleit is trying to escape the conversation. His irreverence does not erase his conviction or severity elsewhere. Kyrien Idiolect: short questions, literal observation, suspicion when someone's behavior changes. He can recognize that something happened without possessing the missing explanation. Frustration does not require a confession or an eloquent speech. These are observations from the current Chapters, not scripts for every future line. MBTI and function emphasis support a characterization check; they do not dictate syntax or replace personal history. Prefer unobtrusive dialogue tags. Use action beats when they locate a speaker, change the timing, or reveal divided attention. A page turned without being read does more here than several descriptions of hidden desire. Comic timing and repetition Distinguish redundant exposition from comic repetition . Repeated information can be cut; a repeated denial may be the action of the scene. Preserve the setup, escalation, pause, reversal, and closing beat when revising a comic exchange. Read it aloud before removing a line. In Doom Version 3: The examination routine restores the old teacher-student relationship before Natalia supplies the ego hypothesis. The academically respectable answer sets up the instruction to consult a priest. Mikhail's apparent consideration of centuries of theology delays an exceptionally blunt answer. His repeated use of Lynleit's name accompanies successive stages of her exit. “It worked” and “By failing” make the same recovery mean different things to the speakers. The later “I haven't asked anything” exchange recalls the earlier call. The repetition now exposes Lynleit's anticipation. Natalia's final question works because the preceding silence has made Lynleit keep talking. Do not compress this into a summary that says Natalia teased her. Do not explain the punchline afterward. A joke may need several apparently unnecessary lines to establish its timing. Syntax, rhythm, and paragraphing Use complete, varied sentences for the narrative baseline. Alternate longer sentences that follow observation or reasoning with shorter sentences at a decision or interruption. Short paragraphs and fragments are emphasis tools. A whole chapter of isolated declarations gives every detail the same weight. Dialogue can remain one utterance per paragraph because the white space controls turn-taking and pace. Use a deliberately repeated structure for a specific effect, then leave it. Avoid habitual three-part lists, mirrored reversals, and final sentences that restate the paragraph in grander language. Keep tense consistent unless a quoted document or deliberate temporal shift requires otherwise. No em dashes. Diction and imagery Prefer concrete verbs, recognizable materials, and specific physical relationships. Fishing line, a soaked sleeve, an unread page, and a notebook are useful because someone can touch or act on them. Choose imagery through focalization. Lynleit may notice dress and composure; Kyrien may notice a change in someone's movements. Neither should become an all-purpose sensor reporting every detail. Use an extended metaphor only while it helps the reader reason. Natalia's address metaphor makes the curse's recognition understandable; it should not spread into every description of affection, leadership, or domestic life. Do not justify an appearance or defend a character after every flawed response. Do not label an ordinary feeling as profound. Leave room for awkwardness that remains awkward. Subtext, ellipsis, and reader knowledge Subtext is what a reader can infer from speech, behavior, juxtaposition, or omission. It is not a fact the author has not decided yet. Ellipsis may omit an encounter while showing its consequences. Doom Version 3 does not narrate the incomplete attempt itself. The next call and Kyrien's account establish what they can establish; exact choreography remains unresolved. Mark Chapter preface and Moment conclusions as inferred only when the scene supplies evidence without stating the conclusion. If a revision makes the explanation explicit, change the label. Do not explain a purple inference in narration merely to make it easier to validate. Keep later consequences out of an earlier scene's closing summary unless a flash-forward is a deliberate narrative choice. Terminology and researched allusion Physicians are ordinary medical professionals without knowledge of magic unless the author explicitly establishes an exception. Do not invent a class of physicians treating thaumaturgy. A medical examination, if used, must preserve that ignorance and show or account for concealment. Doom Version 3 uses Magi's examination of the curse and does not add an off-page physician visit. Natalia introduces the ego hypothesis and attributes the psychological definition to Jung. Her application of it to the curse belongs to fictional magecraft, not to Jung's claim. Brief quotations must be verified; store their source here rather than interrupting dialogue with research apparatus. The short definition retained in v3 and v4 is reproduced in the C. G. Jung Society of Sydney's account of ego, shame, and embodiment. Only that definition is quoted. The curse mechanism and Natalia's proposed use of reciprocal change are fictional. The substitute-king example has a historical basis in the Assyrian report of a substitute assuming the omens; Natalia's explanation of supernatural recognition is an in-world interpretation, not a verified historical effect. Revision protocol Before drafting or editing a Chapter or Moment, read this document, the chosen source version, and the relevant character records. Identify the focal character, discovery sequence, emotional pressure, and any dialogue whose timing must survive. This reference is versioned in Docs. Use its current revision for new work. Before changing it or another prose reference, preserve the previous published revision and register the new one; a historical version records past decisions without directing current canon. During revision, keep two separate passes: 1. Dramatic pass: continuity, knowledge, choices, voice, discovery, and the function of each exchange. 2. Line-edit pass: cadence, diction, repetition, dialogue tags, paragraphing, and unnecessary explanation. Compare the result against the source. Restore any lost joke, disagreement, or character-specific awkwardness that was removed merely for concision. Recheck the preface, Moment, and F/M/S anchors against the actual revised paragraphs. Afterward, add a concise entry below only when the Chapter teaches us a reusable style choice. Give its source, craft term, example or location, and limit. Separate author decisions from editorial working choices. Do not accumulate a new absolute rule for every attractive sentence. Style decisions in use Author direction: 5 September 2026 Preserve original banter and comic repetition. Natalia originates the ego idea and quotes Jung. Do not introduce magic-aware physicians. Limit: a joke's timing does not excuse duplicate explanations elsewhere. Working implementation: Doom Has an Address, Version 3 Past-tense narration, sectioned focalization, exposition through adversarial dialogue, callbacks, exit beats, and an elliptical encounter. Limit: these devices do not require every Chapter to be comic or withhold its central action. Under review: later Chapters Refine the house style from what the author accepts in finished scenes. Limit: no new event or character trait becomes canon through this document. Author direction and implementation: Doom Has an Address, v4 Natalia teaches complex topics through practical examples and personal attempts, failures, and discoveries. Lynleit remains a whimsical, loyal student and friend; intellectual asymmetry is visible without a superior-subordinate social rhythm. The worked diagram, decision diary, resignation anecdote, and Myka call implement that direction in v4. Preserve the curse outcome and the earlier comic callbacks. Limit: an anecdote must earn its place by changing the listener's understanding. Do not manufacture a major invention, past relationship, or magical success merely to supply an example. Version 3 derives from the earlier Version 2 text in commit 868fc31 , before the rewrite in b06c821 . Version 4 builds on v3, revises Natalia's teaching and the teacher-student dialogue, and is now canonical. Versions 1 through 3 remain accessible alternates. Author's Desk
