entries.title: Prose Style History · v1
entries.subtitle: Historical Writing Reference
entries.text: Prose Style History · v1 Historical Writing Reference Earlier Chapter decisions, approved examples, research sources, and revision provenance. Use the current house style for new prose. Prose Style History Historical notes relocated from Prose Style v10 on 19 September 2026. These record how particular revisions were made, including superseded choices. They are not a style corpus for new prose. Use the current house style; consult this history for provenance, continuity, comparison, and explicitly approved passages. The complete earlier reference remains available as v10. Earlier Chapter examples In Doom Version 3: The examination routine restores the old teacher-student relationship before Natalia supplies the ego hypothesis. The academically respectable answer sets up the instruction to consult a priest. Mikhail's apparent consideration of centuries of theology delays an exceptionally blunt answer. His repeated use of Lynleit's name accompanies successive stages of her exit. “It worked” and “By failing” make the same recovery mean different things to the speakers. The later “I haven't asked anything” exchange recalls the earlier call. The repetition now exposes Lynleit's anticipation. Natalia's final question works because the preceding silence has made Lynleit keep talking. Do not compress this into a summary that says Natalia teased her. Do not explain the punchline afterward. A joke may need several apparently unnecessary lines to establish its timing. Teaching examples retained from v10 Use worked examples and instructional scaffolding : begin with an object, action, or familiar problem; let the listener make a prediction; introduce the difficult term after its purpose is apparent. Have the listener apply the idea to a new case rather than merely say that it makes sense. These are craft tools, not a compulsory sequence for every conversation. Her personal examples should include an attempted approach, an observable result, and what she changed afterward. Failure can be useful teaching material without secretly making every failed experiment a triumph. In Doom v4, the decision diary exposes her habit of inventing reasonable explanations after choosing; comparing predictions with actions gives her a better question, not a universal answer. Her resignation and a missed call from Myka provide different examples of habits and attachment. Limit analogical transfer explicitly where it matters. Names on paper illustrate the shared attachment; crossing them out is not a spell. Concern for a niece illustrates attention reorganized around another person; it does not prove romantic desire or guarantee the cure. Keep Natalia's practical warmth distinct from certainty about an untested hypothesis. Use personal stories where they clarify this problem, not as decorative memoirs between lectures. Research sources and allusion Physicians are ordinary medical professionals without knowledge of magic unless the author explicitly establishes an exception. Do not invent a class of physicians treating thaumaturgy. A medical examination, if used, must preserve that ignorance and show or account for concealment. Doom Version 3 uses Magi's examination of the curse and does not add an off-page physician visit. Natalia introduces the ego hypothesis and attributes the psychological definition to Jung. Her application of it to the curse belongs to fictional magecraft, not to Jung's claim. Brief quotations must be verified; store their source here rather than interrupting dialogue with research apparatus. The short definition retained in v3 and v4 is reproduced in the C. G. Jung Society of Sydney's account of ego, shame, and embodiment. Only that definition is quoted. The curse mechanism and Natalia's proposed use of reciprocal change are fictional. The substitute-king example has a historical basis in the Assyrian report of a substitute assuming the omens; Natalia's explanation of supernatural recognition is an in-world interpretation, not a verified historical effect. Style decisions in use Author direction: 5 September 2026 Preserve original banter and comic repetition. Natalia originates the ego idea and quotes Jung. Do not introduce magic-aware physicians. Limit: a joke's timing does not excuse duplicate explanations elsewhere. Working implementation: Doom Has an Address, Version 3 Past-tense narration, sectioned focalization, exposition through adversarial dialogue, callbacks, exit beats, and an elliptical encounter. Limit: these devices do not require every Chapter to be comic or withhold its central action. Under review: later Chapters Refine the house style from what the author accepts in finished scenes. Limit: no new event or character trait becomes canon through this document. Author direction and implementation: Doom Has an Address, v4 Natalia teaches complex topics through practical examples and personal attempts, failures, and discoveries. Lynleit remains a whimsical, loyal student and friend; intellectual asymmetry is visible without a superior-subordinate social rhythm. The worked diagram, decision diary, resignation anecdote, and Myka call implement that direction in v4. Preserve the curse outcome and the earlier comic callbacks. Limit: an anecdote must earn its place by changing the listener's understanding. Do not manufacture a major invention, past relationship, or magical success merely to supply an example. Version 3 derives from the earlier Version 2 text in commit 868fc31 , before the rewrite in b06c821 . Version 4 builds on v3 and revises Natalia's teaching and the teacher-student dialogue. Version 5 retains that text and adds Mikhail's mock blessing. Version 6 adapts the author's Russian exchange. Version 7 restores nine author-approved performance beats and supplies shared canon. Versions 1 through 6 remain accessible alternates. Historical implementation: Doom Has an Address, v5 Mock encomium and bathos: Mikhail gives each phrase of an exaggerated honorific the cadence of a blessing. Lynleit's stopped pen interrupts the register. She asks him to speak normally; the unchanged mundane insult answers that request. Keep the declaration short enough that the listener's confusion remains the turning point. His seated patience, her successive attempts to leave, and the later notebook joke retain their original timing. Delayed recognition: the address to her father's household lets a first-time reader detect private knowledge without yet identifying its source. The author has confirmed Fionn's Magi-lineage association with the Cult of Inanna and Lynleit's indirect association without direct participation. That withholding governed v5. The author's v6 exchange replaces it by naming Inanna and discussing the lineage openly. Jungian editorial lens: inherited identity, conscious self-description, desire, and embarrassment can pull in different directions. Here the imposed honorific makes an expectation personal before Lynleit can dismiss it as theory. This is a craft reading of the scene, not a diagnosis, a new Jung quotation, or a rule that shame causes transformation. Natalia's existing attributed definition remains the Chapter's psychological reference; see the Jung Society source above. Limit: Mikhail's phrase "divine whore" is his mocking allusion. It establishes neither an authentic liturgical quotation nor compulsory cult practice. His insult is not the narrator's judgment about sexual inexperience. No borrowed character name, catchphrase, or imported fictional theology belongs in the scene. Author direction and working implementation: Doom Has an Address, v6 Author direction: sexual subjects involving the main cast should be psychologically revealing, funny, raw, and memorable where the scene supports comedy. Adapt the supplied exchange, preserving its useful lore and slapstick rather than merely making the language respectable. This does not require erotic comedy in every intimate or frightening scene. Register clash and mock encomium: Mikhail rises to deliver an ornate invocation, then sits, drinks, and speaks crudely. The register changes are deliberate acts by the speaker. His knowledge supplies the material; his timing makes it embarrassing. Keep his practical answer and its uncertainty intact so the scene remains a consultation. Prop business and status negotiation: Lynleit's cup repeatedly gives her hands somewhere to go. Mikhail notices and names it; she answers with the porcelain retort. Preserve her capacity to resist. Her increasingly abstract principles defend a private discomfort, while her ordinary professional openness remains unchanged. Escalation and selective compression: keep repetitions that change the stakes: inappropriate wording, rejected objection, personal genealogy, an attempted exit, and the final threat. Cut acknowledgments or objections that only confirm the previous line. The authorial source's elaborate pauses become selected action beats rather than a fragment after every movement. Subtext and explicit exposition: v6 names Inanna and states the lineage's long association. Do not label that information inferred. The cup, formal defence, and threat carry the private embarrassment without a narrator explaining the double insult. Mikhail's monastic composure and Lynleit's defensive formality are character-specific, not universal male or female behavior. Scene breaks and closing tag: a break isolates Mikhail's private last joke from Lynleit's corridor reaction. The notebook callback preserves the earlier Chapter, while the priest's coda belongs to the author's new exchange. Limit: the priest's accusation is personal mockery, not an objective finding that Lynleit has failed a religious duty. The ancestry is not the source of her desire for Kyrien. A Jungian reading may attend to the difference between her declared indifference and her behavior, but it does not establish a clinical diagnosis or give Mikhail access to her unspoken thoughts. Author-approved restoration: Doom Has an Address, v7 Performance beats and comic delay: the author approved the priestly calm, Lynleit's hope for discretion, finger-counting assessment, delayed reply to the insult, accidental defence, porcelain setup, withheld joke, ancient-versus-present problem, and farewell/coda pacing. Preserve these as turns in the exchange rather than compressing them into a description of teasing. Blocking and prop continuity: a restored gesture must fit the actions around it. Lynleit returns the cup during the porcelain setup; later she leaves it alone rather than setting it down again. The prop reveals divided attention without narration explaining that her hands need occupation. Withheld response: after repeatedly exploiting her hesitation, Mikhail lets one averted glance pass. The reader can notice this change without a verdict announcing tenderness. A character's restraint can be visible through an expected action they do not perform. Reaction and reply: Lynleit's denial of agreement, correction from defence to principle, and porcelain retort keep her an active participant. Allow the silence after an insult to land before either speaker resumes. Limit: these are approved choices for this exchange, not instructions to give every joke a long pause or every provocative character a reassuring moment. Natalia's explanation, Mikhail's uncertain treatment, and the later outcome remain unchanged. Author direction: 8 September 2026 Subplot hierarchy: intimacy develops inside the ongoing political, magical, and institutional story. It must not reorganize every character's priorities around romance. The hotel refuge is grief and nonsexual comfort; do not eroticize it or use it as a shortcut to the later sexual milestones. Embodied motive and rationalization: Lynleit's curiosity and attachment precede the research she uses to manage embarrassment. Distinguish general knowledge from skill adapted to one person. Reuse an established tell sparingly rather than narrating a lesson about the callback. Ellipsis and unfinished prose: The Bench under the Lamp v2 leaves a marked writer gap between the supplied approach and aftermath. Do not disguise an undrafted passage as a deliberate finished ellipsis, or replace the omitted action with an invented kiss. Its preface describes only what the prose shows or supports; the Moment's continuity keeps the author's separate milestones explicit. Delayed comic consequence: let the bench seem finished, let Lynleit enjoy her success, and move the pair down the path before the whiskey request. Kyrien's decision not to demand an explanation preserves the last exchange. The flask should already have an ordinary use, not appear solely to serve this joke. Prequel restraint: Arc 0 develops unfinished habits through candidate experiences rather than repeating adult personalities in younger bodies. Keep its unselected scenes in development records. Fionn's own work and household remain its center. Limit: these directions do not make grief a prescription for sex, ancestry an obligation, alcohol a treatment, or every private gesture an interpretable symbol. Author correction: source fidelity and character blocking Blocking: retain the supplied approach, setting, and sequence where drafted. A substitute romantic gesture changes the scene even if the emotional destination seems similar. The park revision removes the unrequested kiss and preserves the original research-success line. Character exposition: preparation need not equal experience. Lynleit brings theoretical knowledge, learns that a particular person does not behave exactly like an account on paper, and becomes interested in his responses beyond her initial wish to prove herself. Kyrien also observes her. Keep that reciprocal observation distinct from a one-sided demonstration of mastery. The complete intimate passage remains for the author, not concealed inside instructional prose. Editorial lacuna: use > [WRITER: concise non-graphic completion notice] for an undrafted passage. The amber callout is an editorial marker, not a fictional event. Preserve the source in the timestamped backlog archive and retain the surrounding dialogue and aftermath. Do not count the gap as shown or inferred evidence in the preface. Character attention: author answers from 12 September 2026 Use the Cognition and Physical Competence reference for the full facts and uncertain type readings. Focalization and divided attention: Lynleit can seek help articulating an internal answer while concealing distress. Trusted reassurance need not remove her unease. Kyrien can continue reasoning in the background and arrive at an overall realization before he can explain it. Write the available observations; do not give either character unexplained access to the correct answer. Social play and reassurance: Sherie enjoys mischief without a professional purpose. An unexpected response first changes her reading of the emotional situation. Felix enjoys generating alternatives even at ease; in danger he can offer a hopeful interpretation while privately continuing to test it. This distinction between reassurance and belief need not be announced after each joke. Physical characterization: keep Lynleit's confirmed agility, Kyrien's endurance and precision, and Felix's trained field competence independent of type labels. Demonstrate capability through the task when a scene calls for it. No particular training method or failure example becomes canon through this guidance. Limit: these answers describe tendencies, not compulsory beats. They do not prescribe a new scene, a guaranteed correct intuition, or a relationship milestone. Author clarification and working implementation: Only Eyes for You, v2 Pragmatic misinterpretation: Felix answers a reprimand about flirting with nuns as though Lynleit asked for romantic loyalty. The two lines supplied by the artwork establish the mismatch. Let her correction keep the disagreement alive rather than explaining his tactic in narration. Running gag and accumulated irritation: the author establishes repeated church visits by Lynleit and Fionn, accompanied by Felix and Reiner. Felix repeatedly flirts with the nuns while Reiner behaves. A promise already broken at another church gives the final outburst a history without requiring every visit to be dramatized. Lynleit reaches the end of her patience; the scene is not a jealousy reveal. Blocking and straight-person contrast: Reiner holds doors, waits with Fionn, and calls Felix away. His restraint makes Felix conspicuous without another stream of jokes. Track the tie and the Bible through the exchange. The nun's ordinary request for her book interrupts the escalation; Lynleit returns it while still holding Felix's tie. See the Moment. Limit: the recurring visits, four participants, contrast, and eventual irritation are author-confirmed. The exact dialogue around the illustrated lines remains a scene draft. Do not invent Fionn's reaction, the substance of the church business, or exact chronology. Felix's wider flirting does not erase his fixation on Lynleit, and her correction is not reciprocal desire. No new physical or magical capability follows from the slapstick. Author's Desk

Prose Style History Historical notes relocated from Prose Style v10 on 19 September 2026. These record how particular revisions were made, including superseded choices. V1 remains unchanged and directly accessible. The linked Moment follows v2 while retaining its v1 link. No event phase, Holumn mechanism, identity for the platform woman, or account of Fionn's later reprimand is invented. The revision replaces the repeated one-line narration with connected recollection and varied paragraphs. It retains the phone and wall tests, duplicated meeting room, voices and warnings, static window, mother's voice, all of Lynleit's practical tests, wrong door, ammunition failure, covering and flame, refusal to choose, guarded call, handoff exchanges and seventeen-day aftermath. Both sleeves are rolled clear before flame use, applying an existing character rule. The coat remains unexplained to the witness. Other characters' intentions are no longer stated as facts he could know. First person acceptance review All sixteen rules apply and pass editorial review. Evidence below identifies passages by distinctive wording rather than unstable paragraph numbers. This review does not claim that automated checks establish prose quality. Rule Judgment and passage evidence --- --- FP01 Pass. The six-year employee remembers the evacuation plan, workplace routes, bag and sister's message; he cannot distinguish ventilation sounds or explain the rescue. FP02 Pass. The opening distinguishes later questions from the experience. He learns Lynleit's name only from the envoy; the monastery and platform are explicitly later. FP03 Pass. Leaving work at 22:49, pressing 1 and replying to his sister establish the immediate purpose without an unrelated biography. FP04 Pass. He first interprets the descent as a parking call, checks the buttons at minus two, and tests the window by changing his position. FP05 Pass. He follows crying because another lost person would be company; he follows Lynleit because he has no better way to choose; he stays when neither ordinary exit feels usable. FP06 Pass. Rail, paint, concrete, wall, jacket sleeve and covered position remain available before pursuit and flame. Backward steps locate the corridor door against his back. FP07 Pass. The ceiling, repeated-room test, stall, mother's door, backward corridor, reload, coat, flame and waiting at the handle unfold through successive attempts and responses. FP08 Pass. Ordinary contractions, direct admissions and practical verbs carry the account. Professional interpretation remains in Lynleit's speech rather than the witness's vocabulary. FP09 Pass. Connected narrative paragraphs alternate with the preserved short exchanges; isolated emphasis is reserved for recognition and the final recalled number. FP10 Pass. Repeated questions about walking, Church custody and memory change what the witness learns. The two elevators and repeated clock checks have different consequences. FP11 Pass. Fear affects his jacket zip, grip, backward walking, refusal of the lift and need for answerable questions. Relief at possible disbelief remains his admission. FP12 Pass. Door direction prevents an attempted exit; instructions determine covering; the call and handoff retain the meals, Mass and positives exchanges without explaining their jokes. FP13 Pass. He cannot tell what Lynleit learned from the coin, why she does not stop him leaving, or what the envoys communicate through a glance. FP14 Pass. Dents, a second phone, the voice at the latch, failed gunfire and moving handle earn escalation. The returned office permits exhaustion and humor. FP15 Pass. The narrator returns to work using stairs, then fails to place the platform woman beyond the recalled number. The chapter does not identify her or certify memory alteration. FP16 Pass. All encounters and dialogue derive from the existing chapter and approved character rules. No supplied transcript incident, technical claim or folklore is transferred. The Nasu advisory check retains observed paint limits and the timing of escape without promoting either to a universal rule. No relationship or attraction changes require a tension-record revision. No behavior-note record targets this chapter; existing unrelated anchors remain untouched. Reader-knowledge classifications and preface events retain their prior factual scope. There Is No Eleventh Floor: 29 September 2026 The author supplied the first-person office-worker account and specifically approved its narrative voice, rescue, gun use and aftermath. Intake preserves its recurring questions, numbered disorientation, practical tests, blunt exchanges and monastery coda. Added real-time passages follow the witness checking the wall, repeated offices, window, corridor and covering rather than replacing his experience with a list of terrors. The follow-up replaces routine burn scars with belt-carried protective gloves and a small recoverable exertion cost. It requests practical victim coverage, covert cooperation from the leviathan-hide coat, a theatrical flame boundary, a compact silver pistol with a spare magazine and a final throw, and guarded Church dialogue. The final text gives the phone call and envoys their ordinary questions about denomination, meals, waking time and relatives without explaining the hidden machinery to the witness. The original file is retained unchanged in the backlog archive. It is provenance, not a second registered Chapter version overriding the author's corrections. The permanent transcript-reference rule was adopted separately; no transcript samples were available or analysed. The scene does not supply a new general house style or require every Chapter to use first person and short paragraphs. The Nasu advisory check separates usable observations from claimed laws: painted edges constrain some figures; a refusal to choose precedes one escape; flame buys time without destroying the whole incident. No additional Holumn mechanism was canonized to complete the audit. The coat's material remains archive knowledge rather than the narrator's discovery. Limit: the recurring visits, four participants, contrast, and eventual irritation are author-confirmed. The exact dialogue around the illustrated lines remains a scene draft. Do not invent Fionn's reaction, the substance of the church business, or exact chronology. Felix's wider flirting does not erase his fixation on Lynleit, and her correction is not reciprocal desire. No new physical or magical capability follows from the slapstick. The Shared Night v2: author correction, 30 September 2026 Preserve the briefing's specific jokes and Natalia's distinctions while removing Hiyu and Yulia, the kiss and the settled domestic-dream account. Sherie uses recovered choice to keep distance; her enjoyment of Felix does not become a romantic commitment. Keep the nonsexual emotional direction for Lynleit and Kyrien as a writer gap until its events are chosen. Their childhood histories must not be invented for an emotional payoff. These are scene decisions, not a new universal style rule. The office reprimand after There Is No Eleventh Floor is recorded as an outline. Its perspective must remain separate from the bystander's first-person testimony. The cat chase is a possible continuation, not yet a fixed next scene. Author's Desk

entries.text: Prose Style History · v6 Historical Writing Reference The River Choir in three first-person chapters: voice, panel continuity and the FP01-FP16 evidence review. Prose Style History Historical notes relocated from Prose Style v10 on 19 September 2026. These record how particular revisions were made, including superseded choices. They are not a style corpus for new prose. Use the current house style; consult this history for provenance, continuity, comparison, and explicitly approved passages. The complete earlier reference remains available as v10. The River Choir: three first-person parts, 1 October 2026 The author requested full-length Kyrien, Lynleit and Kyrien accounts, with the second returning to the moment before the operation fails and the third beginning as Kyrien reaches shore. Part I, Part II and Part III follow that order. The previous complete third-person Chapter remains available as v1-v3. This is a scene revision, not a change to the third-person default elsewhere. Sources, preserved material and working choices Read the current Chapter, owning character and incident records, cognition reference, first-person standard, house style, dread direction and reader-knowledge boundaries. Visually inspected all seven River Incident r6 sketches (IMG-000140 through IMG-000146) and all four After the River panels (IMG-000111 through IMG-000114). The new prose follows the grip, blue flame, surface support, fish dress, sewn eyelids, fingertips at the water, wet park questioning and overhead movement. It does not promote the annotations into a sensory power or identify the shape. Preserved the failed watches, practical camera limit, card rematches, rope joke, brief waist catch, empty holds, split banks, jacket loss, forbidden water walking, back-to-back recovery, withheld admission and coat-offer joke. The two complete accounts of the failure overlap deliberately. Kyrien cannot narrate the underwater images he never saw; Lynleit cannot know he is in the trees. The new sections do not advance the later hotel refuge or intimate park encounter. The author permitted connective invention. The preliminary exit inspection, specific card exchanges, snagged line, surviving phone pouch, call to count the team, bench detour, barrier reunion and return to the unfinished cards are working-draft staging. They supply actions and an ending, not new powers, guaranteed Holumn limits, exact dates or completed institutional investigations. The gate is opened without inventing a lock-breaking technique. The park lamp is beyond a bend and cannot contradict the original unlit view from the bridge. Keep the unresolved shape in Questions. Both protective gloves and both rolled sleeves precede flame. Some earlier sketches show bare hands; the later explicit character rule governs this prose without authorizing image replacement. The lost blue suede jacket remains ordinary clothing, not the leviathan-hide coat. Water walking is familiar to Lynleit from secret practice, while Kyrien's observation remains his first unmistakable exposure to magic. No new childhood incident explains the already-established fear of drowning. FP01-FP16 acceptance review Each part is a past-tense first-person recollection, with no later solution smuggled into the witness account. All sixteen rules apply to each full chapter. The table records editorial passage evidence; automated warnings are a separate aid, not a certificate of voice. Rule Part I: Kyrien Part II: Lynleit Part III: Kyrien --- --- --- --- FP01 Pass. “I checked the other end of the bridge” and his correction about visibility from the water put routes, practical objections and sparse speech first. Card losses irritate him. Pass. She wants a usable objection, has relied on Reiner's confidence, and keeps counting people while frightened. “I wanted him to call anyway” conflicts with her wish to hide. Pass. He tests a hull and bank shelf before accepting water walking, answers literally and keeps checking the search on the other bank. FP02 Pass. He has seen the envelope but not heard its whole discussion; fingers are felt through cloth, not identified as drowned souls. Pass. Secret night practice and Church danger belong to her existing knowledge. She sees Kyrien swim away but never knows he watches her crossing. Pass. “I couldn't see the eyes from where I was” precedes Lynleit's later description; Maren's testimony comes through the phone. FP03 Pass. The limited inspection, camera window, mother-care message and mundane van downtime supply the baseline. Pass. Holding the wet board returns to the shared task immediately before failure; no new biography delays the continuation. Pass. Getting a knee out of mud and counting shapes at the steps establish the immediate need to recover and find Lynleit. FP04 Pass. The pale camera mark is checked against the live feed; an imagined cable gives way to the felt grip that changes location. Pass. A hand around a boot becomes visible before she tries to strike its wrist. Scales become whole fish as a mouth turns into view. Pass. Changing viewing angle eliminates the imagined board; returning his head to its previous position tests whether the overhead movement was parallax. FP05 Pass. He checks exits, objects about the light, cuts a snag and finally chooses reachable roots because his strokes are not taking him cityward. Pass. She withholds flame while rescuers surround Maren; she chooses the nearer bank rather than test the silent girl. Pass. Cover conceals his position from an unknown attacker; the phone secures a head count; cold makes indefinite watching untenable. FP06 Pass. Bridge, two banks, downstream exit, three boats, line fitting and forked root remain traceable before use. Pass. Hull, ankle grips, jacket shoulder, overhead light, palm, knee and boots locate each attempt and each new support. Pass. Low branches preserve the water sightline; the bench detour stays on the landward side and rejoins the path beyond the shape. FP07 Pass. Routine watches compress around changed clues and games; boarding, first pull, line cut and failed swimming unfold step by step. Pass. Swimming, failed grips, jacket entrapment, flame and standing each change the available next action; no summary substitutes for the escape. Pass. Observation, reunion, questioning, call, shape assessment and bypass are dramatized rather than skipped to safety. FP08 Pass. “I meant nothing I could point to” and the brief exchanges retain practical, intelligible recollection without borrowed slang. Pass. “I had shut my mouth” and “I wanted to hurt them” remain direct; technical lore does not interrupt suffocation. Pass. “Anything with an edge would have helped” and “It was closer” fit Kyrien's manner; he does not acquire an occult vocabulary. FP09 Pass. Connected inspection and game paragraphs alternate with short radio exchanges, then tighten around the root. Pass. The account has room for repeated attempts but isolates “It held” at the decisive new support. Pass. Observational paragraphs carry the water and branch tests; uneven dialogue interrupts them; withdrawal resumes continuous action. FP10 Pass. Repeated watches change the clue or card advantage; “city side” becomes an instruction he cannot follow. Pass. Reaching up, kicking and testing a step recur with a new grip, release or footing problem rather than repeating a verdict. Pass. Repeated questions about seeing something increase pressure; checking the branches distinguishes shape motion from imagined movement. FP11 Pass. Pride spoils a card count; irritation at swallowing water and a hurting ankle interfere with purposeful action. Pass. Fear makes her want an upward-pulling hand and hesitate to lift a supported foot; concern for the team persists alongside secrecy. Pass. He puts down an impractical wet jacket, admits fear, watches a slow pair of hands and moves before cold further limits them. FP12 Pass. Lynleit's response to the steps changes the planned light; the rope joke and card challenge preserve familiar friction. Pass. Reiner's directions and Maren's report change the rescue attempt; her order to the girl obtains no answer or proof of understanding. Pass. Questions about pain, the head count, bank warning and “Are you scared?” change movement and disclosure; the card warning restores a familiar exchange. FP13 Pass. Her attention is visible in gaze and card handling; he does not claim knowledge of her water-walking secret or of Felix's private reasoning. Pass. Kyrien's pause prompts a question rather than a correct mental reading. The girl's bewilderment remains Lynleit's question. Pass. “That was what I made of the questions” qualifies her fear of being seen. Other people's exact experiences are reported, not entered. FP14 Pass. The tightening line and failed direction of swimming earn the escalation after ordinary work and competitive amusement. Pass. More grips make careful swimming insufficient; the surface gives limited relief before a second figure emerges. Pass. A stable surface revises his understanding; a reunited team eases one fear before the still-branch movement demands another decision. FP15 Pass. His knee finding mud ends a particular escape attempt, not the whole unresolved operation. The next-part link makes the handoff explicit. Pass. Boots reach land, a real branch supports her, and she calls for Kyrien without settling who saw her. Pass. He shields the unfinished cards from his wet sleeve and closes their box; the shape remains unidentified and his witnessed secret unreported. FP16 Pass. The operation, people, equipment and jokes derive from MAGIARCHY sources or authorized connective drafting, not transcript incidents. Pass. Existing fear and abilities govern the escape; no sample folklore, profession, dialogue or new magical law is imported. Pass. The park imagery comes from the project's panels; no transcript incident supplies the detour, ending or explanation. Nasu, genre and relationship review The Nasu audit checks physical causality, witness limits and productive unresolved implications here. The boats' missing crews are not retroactively witnessed; the held surface gives escape without a universal explanation; the girl's touch does not prove a sensing mechanism. The park shape moves while nearby branches remain still, but neither narrator classifies it. Kyrien's withholding is explicitly known to the reader in first person, while its full personal motive and Lynleit's degree of certainty remain open. The sexual-tension review retains the already-approved repeatable card interaction and momentary waist catch. It does not manufacture an attraction from drowning, turn first aid into seduction or add a romantic milestone. The existing Lynleit/Kyrien guidance therefore remains unchanged. The back-to-back posture is physical recovery with established familiarity; Chapter and Moment facts do not label a confession that never occurs. Operational surveillance, competitive humor, vulnerable survival and disturbing observation remain distinct experiences rather than a fixed genre ratio. Both narrators can act effectively and still misjudge, fail or be afraid. Earlier confident summaries about what the girl must think were replaced by Lynleit's unanswered question, and a glove mismatch in Kyrien's first sight of her was corrected before acceptance. There Is No Eleventh Floor revision: 1 October 2026 Chapter v2 applies the supplied-transcript standard at the author's request. V1 remains unchanged and directly accessible. The linked Moment follows v2 while retaining its v1 link. No event phase, Holumn mechanism, identity for the platform woman, or account of Fionn's later reprimand is invented. The revision replaces the repeated one-line narration with connected recollection and varied paragraphs. It retains the phone and wall tests, duplicated meeting room, voices and warnings, static window, mother's voice, all of Lynleit's practical tests, wrong door, ammunition failure, covering and flame, refusal to choose, guarded call, handoff exchanges and seventeen-day aftermath. Both sleeves are rolled clear before flame use, applying an existing character rule. The coat remains unexplained to the witness. Other characters' intentions are no longer stated as facts he could know. First person acceptance review All sixteen rules apply and pass editorial review. Evidence below identifies passages by distinctive wording rather than unstable paragraph numbers. This review does not claim that automated checks establish prose quality. Rule Judgment and passage evidence --- --- FP01 Pass. The six-year employee remembers the evacuation plan, workplace routes, bag and sister's message; he cannot distinguish ventilation sounds or explain the rescue. FP02 Pass. The opening distinguishes later questions from the experience. He learns Lynleit's name only from the envoy; the monastery and platform are explicitly later. FP03 Pass. Leaving work at 22:49, pressing 1 and replying to his sister establish the immediate purpose without an unrelated biography. FP04 Pass. He first interprets the descent as a parking call, checks the buttons at minus two, and tests the window by changing his position. FP05 Pass. He follows crying because another lost person would be company; he follows Lynleit because he has no better way to choose; he stays when neither ordinary exit feels usable. FP06 Pass. Rail, paint, concrete, wall, jacket sleeve and covered position remain available before pursuit and flame. Backward steps locate the corridor door against his back. FP07 Pass. The ceiling, repeated-room test, stall, mother's door, backward corridor, reload, coat, flame and waiting at the handle unfold through successive attempts and responses. FP08 Pass. Ordinary contractions, direct admissions and practical verbs carry the account. Professional interpretation remains in Lynleit's speech rather than the witness's vocabulary. FP09 Pass. Connected narrative paragraphs alternate with the preserved short exchanges; isolated emphasis is reserved for recognition and the final recalled number. FP10 Pass. Repeated questions about walking, Church custody and memory change what the witness learns. The two elevators and repeated clock checks have different consequences. FP11 Pass. Fear affects his jacket zip, grip, backward walking, refusal of the lift and need for answerable questions. Relief at possible disbelief remains his admission. FP12 Pass. Door direction prevents an attempted exit; instructions determine covering; the call and handoff retain the meals, Mass and positives exchanges without explaining their jokes. FP13 Pass. He cannot tell what Lynleit learned from the coin, why she does not stop him leaving, or what the envoys communicate through a glance. FP14 Pass. Dents, a second phone, the voice at the latch, failed gunfire and moving handle earn escalation. The returned office permits exhaustion and humor. FP15 Pass. The narrator returns to work using stairs, then fails to place the platform woman beyond the recalled number. The chapter does not identify her or certify memory alteration. FP16 Pass. All encounters and dialogue derive from the existing chapter and approved character rules. No supplied transcript incident, technical claim or folklore is transferred. The Nasu advisory check retains observed paint limits and the timing of escape without promoting either to a universal rule. No relationship or attraction changes require a tension-record revision. No behavior-note record targets this chapter; existing unrelated anchors remain untouched. Reader-knowledge classifications and preface events retain their prior factual scope. There Is No Eleventh Floor: 29 September 2026 The author supplied the first-person office-worker account and specifically approved its narrative voice, rescue, gun use and aftermath. Intake preserves its recurring questions, numbered disorientation, practical tests, blunt exchanges and monastery coda. Added real-time passages follow the witness checking the wall, repeated offices, window, corridor and covering rather than replacing his experience with a list of terrors. The follow-up replaces routine burn scars with belt-carried protective gloves and a small recoverable exertion cost. It requests practical victim coverage, covert cooperation from the leviathan-hide coat, a theatrical flame boundary, a compact silver pistol with a spare magazine and a final throw, and guarded Church dialogue. The final text gives the phone call and envoys their ordinary questions about denomination, meals, waking time and relatives without explaining the hidden machinery to the witness. The original file is retained unchanged in the backlog archive. It is provenance, not a second registered Chapter version overriding the author's corrections. The permanent transcript-reference rule was adopted separately; no transcript samples were available or analysed. The scene does not supply a new general house style or require every Chapter to use first person and short paragraphs. The Nasu advisory check separates usable observations from claimed laws: painted edges constrain some figures; a refusal to choose precedes one escape; flame buys time without destroying the whole incident. No additional Holumn mechanism was canonized to complete the audit. The coat's material remains archive knowledge rather than the narrator's discovery. Narvean fog: 23 September 2026 The author establishes fog as a recurring national problem, especially in selected areas, with unusual fog during certain Spill incidents. The river Chapter v3 adds interrupted sightlines while retaining the near-bank view needed for Kyrien's discovery and the city-side view needed for Felix's fallback. Dialogue, the underwater struggle, and the recovery sequence remain intact. The Last Man Out v2 adds the park's fog to its outline without inventing Heyk's missing assault or evacuation sequence. The fog section of Dread and Action Direction owns the reusable writing guidance. These revisions do not establish a single fog mechanism or give the characters the archive's knowledge of the Spill. After the Failed Attempt v3: 23 September 2026 The author's backlog supplies the sequence from paid professional legal work through institutional refusal, an interval, the shop humiliation, the dinner attempt, and reluctant recruitment. V3 replaces the outline with scene prose while retaining earlier versions. The mother's apology and the lawyer-payment exchange use the supplied wording, with only typography normalized. Names, the exact attack choreography, the prosecutor's magical status, and the later prohibition remain undecided. The consultation's concrete success precedes its defeat; the lawyer remains competent and present in the later interview. Tea, shopping, shifts, and paid care keep the mother and household visible outside the revenge plot. A marked viewpoint change gives Lynleit knowledge Kyrien lacks. The private employment discussion negotiates material terms without a confession. These are revision choices for this Chapter, not new compulsory formulas in the house style. Earlier Chapter examples In Doom Version 3: The examination routine restores the old teacher-student relationship before Natalia supplies the ego hypothesis. The academically respectable answer sets up the instruction to consult a priest. Mikhail's apparent consideration of centuries of theology delays an exceptionally blunt answer. His repeated use of Lynleit's name accompanies successive stages of her exit. “It worked” and “By failing” make the same recovery mean different things to the speakers. The later “I haven't asked anything” exchange recalls the earlier call. The repetition now exposes Lynleit's anticipation. Natalia's final question works because the preceding silence has made Lynleit keep talking. Do not compress this into a summary that says Natalia teased her. Do not explain the punchline afterward. A joke may need several apparently unnecessary lines to establish its timing. Teaching examples retained from v10 Use worked examples and instructional scaffolding : begin with an object, action, or familiar problem; let the listener make a prediction; introduce the difficult term after its purpose is apparent. Have the listener apply the idea to a new case rather than merely say that it makes sense. These are craft tools, not a compulsory sequence for every conversation. Her personal examples should include an attempted approach, an observable result, and what she changed afterward. Failure can be useful teaching material without secretly making every failed experiment a triumph. In Doom v4, the decision diary exposes her habit of inventing reasonable explanations after choosing; comparing predictions with actions gives her a better question, not a universal answer. Her resignation and a missed call from Myka provide different examples of habits and attachment. Limit analogical transfer explicitly where it matters. Names on paper illustrate the shared attachment; crossing them out is not a spell. Concern for a niece illustrates attention reorganized around another person; it does not prove romantic desire or guarantee the cure. Keep Natalia's practical warmth distinct from certainty about an untested hypothesis. Use personal stories where they clarify this problem, not as decorative memoirs between lectures. Research sources and allusion Physicians are ordinary medical professionals without knowledge of magic unless the author explicitly establishes an exception. Do not invent a class of physicians treating thaumaturgy. A medical examination, if used, must preserve that ignorance and show or account for concealment. Doom Version 3 uses Magi's examination of the curse and does not add an off-page physician visit. Natalia introduces the ego hypothesis and attributes the psychological definition to Jung. Her application of it to the curse belongs to fictional magecraft, not to Jung's claim. Brief quotations must be verified; store their source here rather than interrupting dialogue with research apparatus. The short definition retained in v3 and v4 is reproduced in the C. G. Jung Society of Sydney's account of ego, shame, and embodiment. Only that definition is quoted. The curse mechanism and Natalia's proposed use of reciprocal change are fictional. The substitute-king example has a historical basis in the Assyrian report of a substitute assuming the omens; Natalia's explanation of supernatural recognition is an in-world interpretation, not a verified historical effect. Style decisions in use Author direction: 5 September 2026 Preserve original banter and comic repetition. Natalia originates the ego idea and quotes Jung. Do not introduce magic-aware physicians. Limit: a joke's timing does not excuse duplicate explanations elsewhere. Working implementation: Doom Has an Address, Version 3 Past-tense narration, sectioned focalization, exposition through adversarial dialogue, callbacks, exit beats, and an elliptical encounter. Limit: these devices do not require every Chapter to be comic or withhold its central action. Under review: later Chapters Refine the house style from what the author accepts in finished scenes. Limit: no new event or character trait becomes canon through this document. Author direction and implementation: Doom Has an Address, v4 Natalia teaches complex topics through practical examples and personal attempts, failures, and discoveries. Lynleit remains a whimsical, loyal student and friend; intellectual asymmetry is visible without a superior-subordinate social rhythm. The worked diagram, decision diary, resignation anecdote, and Myka call implement that direction in v4. Preserve the curse outcome and the earlier comic callbacks. Limit: an anecdote must earn its place by changing the listener's understanding. Do not manufacture a major invention, past relationship, or magical success merely to supply an example. Version 3 derives from the earlier Version 2 text in commit 868fc31 , before the rewrite in b06c821 . Version 4 builds on v3 and revises Natalia's teaching and the teacher-student dialogue. Version 5 retains that text and adds Mikhail's mock blessing. Version 6 adapts the author's Russian exchange. Version 7 restores nine author-approved performance beats and supplies shared canon. Versions 1 through 6 remain accessible alternates. Historical implementation: Doom Has an Address, v5 Mock encomium and bathos: Mikhail gives each phrase of an exaggerated honorific the cadence of a blessing. Lynleit's stopped pen interrupts the register. She asks him to speak normally; the unchanged mundane insult answers that request. Keep the declaration short enough that the listener's confusion remains the turning point. His seated patience, her successive attempts to leave, and the later notebook joke retain their original timing. Delayed recognition: the address to her father's household lets a first-time reader detect private knowledge without yet identifying its source. The author has confirmed Fionn's Magi-lineage association with the Cult of Inanna and Lynleit's indirect association without direct participation. That withholding governed v5. The author's v6 exchange replaces it by naming Inanna and discussing the lineage openly. Jungian editorial lens: inherited identity, conscious self-description, desire, and embarrassment can pull in different directions. Here the imposed honorific makes an expectation personal before Lynleit can dismiss it as theory. This is a craft reading of the scene, not a diagnosis, a new Jung quotation, or a rule that shame causes transformation. Natalia's existing attributed definition remains the Chapter's psychological reference; see the Jung Society source above. Limit: Mikhail's phrase "divine whore" is his mocking allusion. It establishes neither an authentic liturgical quotation nor compulsory cult practice. His insult is not the narrator's judgment about sexual inexperience. No borrowed character name, catchphrase, or imported fictional theology belongs in the scene. Author direction and working implementation: Doom Has an Address, v6 Author direction: sexual subjects involving the main cast should be psychologically revealing, funny, raw, and memorable where the scene supports comedy. Adapt the supplied exchange, preserving its useful lore and slapstick rather than merely making the language respectable. This does not require erotic comedy in every intimate or frightening scene. Register clash and mock encomium: Mikhail rises to deliver an ornate invocation, then sits, drinks, and speaks crudely. The register changes are deliberate acts by the speaker. His knowledge supplies the material; his timing makes it embarrassing. Keep his practical answer and its uncertainty intact so the scene remains a consultation. Prop business and status negotiation: Lynleit's cup repeatedly gives her hands somewhere to go. Mikhail notices and names it; she answers with the porcelain retort. Preserve her capacity to resist. Her increasingly abstract principles defend a private discomfort, while her ordinary professional openness remains unchanged. Escalation and selective compression: keep repetitions that change the stakes: inappropriate wording, rejected objection, personal genealogy, an attempted exit, and the final threat. Cut acknowledgments or objections that only confirm the previous line. The authorial source's elaborate pauses become selected action beats rather than a fragment after every movement. Subtext and explicit exposition: v6 names Inanna and states the lineage's long association. Do not label that information inferred. The cup, formal defence, and threat carry the private embarrassment without a narrator explaining the double insult. Mikhail's monastic composure and Lynleit's defensive formality are character-specific, not universal male or female behavior. Scene breaks and closing tag: a break isolates Mikhail's private last joke from Lynleit's corridor reaction. The notebook callback preserves the earlier Chapter, while the priest's coda belongs to the author's new exchange. Limit: the priest's accusation is personal mockery, not an objective finding that Lynleit has failed a religious duty. The ancestry is not the source of her desire for Kyrien. A Jungian reading may attend to the difference between her declared indifference and her behavior, but it does not establish a clinical diagnosis or give Mikhail access to her unspoken thoughts. Author-approved restoration: Doom Has an Address, v7 Performance beats and comic delay: the author approved the priestly calm, Lynleit's hope for discretion, finger-counting assessment, delayed reply to the insult, accidental defence, porcelain setup, withheld joke, ancient-versus-present problem, and farewell/coda pacing. Preserve these as turns in the exchange rather than compressing them into a description of teasing. Blocking and prop continuity: a restored gesture must fit the actions around it. Lynleit returns the cup during the porcelain setup; later she leaves it alone rather than setting it down again. The prop reveals divided attention without narration explaining that her hands need occupation. Withheld response: after repeatedly exploiting her hesitation, Mikhail lets one averted glance pass. The reader can notice this change without a verdict announcing tenderness. A character's restraint can be visible through an expected action they do not perform. Reaction and reply: Lynleit's denial of agreement, correction from defence to principle, and porcelain retort keep her an active participant. Allow the silence after an insult to land before either speaker resumes. Limit: these are approved choices for this exchange, not instructions to give every joke a long pause or every provocative character a reassuring moment. Natalia's explanation, Mikhail's uncertain treatment, and the later outcome remain unchanged. Author direction: 8 September 2026 Subplot hierarchy: intimacy develops inside the ongoing political, magical, and institutional story. It must not reorganize every character's priorities around romance. The hotel refuge is grief and nonsexual comfort; do not eroticize it or use it as a shortcut to the later sexual milestones. Embodied motive and rationalization: Lynleit's curiosity and attachment precede the research she uses to manage embarrassment. Distinguish general knowledge from skill adapted to one person. Reuse an established tell sparingly rather than narrating a lesson about the callback. Ellipsis and unfinished prose: The Bench under the Lamp v2 leaves a marked writer gap between the supplied approach and aftermath. Do not disguise an undrafted passage as a deliberate finished ellipsis, or replace the omitted action with an invented kiss. Its preface describes only what the prose shows or supports; the Moment's continuity keeps the author's separate milestones explicit. Delayed comic consequence: let the bench seem finished, let Lynleit enjoy her success, and move the pair down the path before the whiskey request. Kyrien's decision not to demand an explanation preserves the last exchange. The flask should already have an ordinary use, not appear solely to serve this joke. Prequel restraint: Arc 0 develops unfinished habits through candidate experiences rather than repeating adult personalities in younger bodies. Keep its unselected scenes in development records. Fionn's own work and household remain its center. Limit: these directions do not make grief a prescription for sex, ancestry an obligation, alcohol a treatment, or every private gesture an interpretable symbol. Author correction: source fidelity and character blocking Blocking: retain the supplied approach, setting, and sequence where drafted. A substitute romantic gesture changes the scene even if the emotional destination seems similar. The park revision removes the unrequested kiss and preserves the original research-success line. Character exposition: preparation need not equal experience. Lynleit brings theoretical knowledge, learns that a particular person does not behave exactly like an account on paper, and becomes interested in his responses beyond her initial wish to prove herself. Kyrien also observes her. Keep that reciprocal observation distinct from a one-sided demonstration of mastery. The complete intimate passage remains for the author, not concealed inside instructional prose. Editorial lacuna: use > [WRITER: concise non-graphic completion notice] for an undrafted passage. The amber callout is an editorial marker, not a fictional event. Preserve the source in the timestamped backlog archive and retain the surrounding dialogue and aftermath. Do not count the gap as shown or inferred evidence in the preface. Character attention: author answers from 12 September 2026 Use the Cognition and Physical Competence reference for the full facts and uncertain type readings. Focalization and divided attention: Lynleit can seek help articulating an internal answer while concealing distress. Trusted reassurance need not remove her unease. Kyrien can continue reasoning in the background and arrive at an overall realization before he can explain it. Write the available observations; do not give either character unexplained access to the correct answer. Social play and reassurance: Sherie enjoys mischief without a professional purpose. An unexpected response first changes her reading of the emotional situation. Felix enjoys generating alternatives even at ease; in danger he can offer a hopeful interpretation while privately continuing to test it. This distinction between reassurance and belief need not be announced after each joke. Physical characterization: keep Lynleit's confirmed agility, Kyrien's endurance and precision, and Felix's trained field competence independent of type labels. Demonstrate capability through the task when a scene calls for it. No particular training method or failure example becomes canon through this guidance. Limit: these answers describe tendencies, not compulsory beats. They do not prescribe a new scene, a guaranteed correct intuition, or a relationship milestone. Author clarification and working implementation: Only Eyes for You, v2 Pragmatic misinterpretation: Felix answers a reprimand about flirting with nuns as though Lynleit asked for romantic loyalty. The two lines supplied by the artwork establish the mismatch. Let her correction keep the disagreement alive rather than explaining his tactic in narration. Running gag and accumulated irritation: the author establishes repeated church visits by Lynleit and Fionn, accompanied by Felix and Reiner. Felix repeatedly flirts with the nuns while Reiner behaves. A promise already broken at another church gives the final outburst a history without requiring every visit to be dramatized. Lynleit reaches the end of her patience; the scene is not a jealousy reveal. Blocking and straight-person contrast: Reiner holds doors, waits with Fionn, and calls Felix away. His restraint makes Felix conspicuous without another stream of jokes. Track the tie and the Bible through the exchange. The nun's ordinary request for her book interrupts the escalation; Lynleit returns it while still holding Felix's tie. See the Moment. Limit: the recurring visits, four participants, contrast, and eventual irritation are author-confirmed. The exact dialogue around the illustrated lines remains a scene draft. Do not invent Fionn's reaction, the substance of the church business, or exact chronology. Felix's wider flirting does not erase his fixation on Lynleit, and her correction is not reciprocal desire. No new physical or magical capability follows from the slapstick. The Shared Night v2: author correction, 30 September 2026 Preserve the briefing's specific jokes and Natalia's distinctions while removing Hiyu and Yulia, the kiss and the settled domestic-dream account. Sherie uses recovered choice to keep distance; her enjoyment of Felix does not become a romantic commitment. Keep the nonsexual emotional direction for Lynleit and Kyrien as a writer gap until its events are chosen. Their childhood histories must not be invented for an emotional payoff. These are scene decisions, not a new universal style rule. The office reprimand after There Is No Eleventh Floor is recorded as an outline. Its perspective must remain separate from the bystander's first-person testimony. The cat chase is a possible continuation, not yet a fixed next scene. Author's Desk

entries.title: Questions to Be Answered
entries.subtitle: Editorial Ledger
entries.text: Questions to Be Answered Editorial Ledger Unanswered questions about chronology, family reveals, Holumn effects, and the limits of established lore. Questions to Be Answered This is the author's living editorial ledger. It separates unresolved canon questions from questions that determine placement on the shared Story and character timelines. Each unresolved question carries a confidence score based only on confirmed material. Answers belong in the wider site architecture, not in these tables. Questions that have been answered or made redundant are removed. Preferred development approaches are preserved in Prose and Scene Guidance, separate from the missing facts listed here. Current questions Story, character, world, relationship, institution, location, and event questions are ordered from least answered to most answered. entries.subtitle: Character Arc Direction
entries.text: Sherie: Kyrie Eleison · v1 Character Arc Direction Sherie knows about Holumns by The Shared Night; the earlier discovery and her eventual reckoning remain undated. Sherie: Kyrie Eleison Author-confirmed direction, 28 September 2026. This gives Sherie's personal arc an intended shape, not a completed sequence of events. Sherie's profile owns her established life; Kyrie Eleison (Movement I) is her associated recording. The woman who enjoys the game Sherie is a sympathetic side protagonist, a diplomatic apprentice with purposes of her own. She enjoys social play even when nobody needs persuading. Beauty, sexuality, charm and psychological pressure also give her real leverage. She likes discovering what will move a person and seeing her judgment work. That pleasure can encourage her to treat attraction as a tool long after the other person has stopped treating the exchange lightly. Her saying about catharsis and catastrophe belongs here. It is a risk she can recognize and still enjoy taking. Do not make her suddenly inept to produce a downfall: her successes should help explain why she believes she can manage a worsening situation. The promised cost The intended arc moves through increasingly consequential games into one that becomes catastrophic. Sherie must pay a serious personal price for how she has used people, power and desire. The exact game, those affected, and the cost have not been chosen. The descent may involve punishment, sacrifice, a reckoning or an experience that feels like hell to her. These are possible forms of the same direction, not four required events. Sexuality itself is not the offence, and a catastrophe must not turn her into a villain whose earlier warmth was all false. Her pleasure, competence, affection and manipulative habits can belong to the same person. Eventually "Lord, have mercy" should become emotionally appropriate to her circumstances. It need not become dialogue, a Church ritual or a literal divine judgment. The soundtrack can make the plea audible while the scene gives her something particular to fear or lose. Salvation remains possible afterward; its means and outcome are open. Building the causal chain The following is advisory development, not added canon. The Nasu audit favors a consequence she helps create over an arbitrary punishment delivered because she is seductive. Development task What a future scene needs to establish --- --- A successful game What Sherie wants, whose desire she uses, and what the success encourages her to try again. Escalation A consequence she recognizes but still thinks she can contain. Let another person's aims continue outside her view. Catastrophe A traceable connection to her choices, without pretending she intended every resulting harm. Reckoning Something she cannot repair simply by obtaining the response she wants. Responsibility and vulnerability must cost her something concrete. Possible salvation A credible opportunity to act differently or receive help, without automatically cancelling the damage. Her diplomatic obligations offer an existing place for these pressures to meet the larger political story. No new mission, adversary, victim, bargain or rescue is assigned by this document. Choose the decisive events before creating a Moment or numbered timeline phase. What she knows Sherie is not a Magus and initially knows nothing about magic. A much later discovery of the supernatural world is possible and may carry a serious personal cost. Neither the discovery nor its connection to her catastrophe is settled. Her competence in reading people does not let her recognize hidden magecraft without evidence. The river operation can reveal magic to Kyrien and the reader without telling Sherie what happened. Her request for an investigation, access to officials and association with MSF do not grant her their concealed knowledge. Events, Witnesses, and Reveals keeps these distinctions explicit. Felix is a person within this life The private-game direction retains its affection, trust, discretion and uneven attachment. Sherie's genuine ease with Felix must not become a retroactive lie. Their shared play can reveal the difference between influencing someone and caring what happens to him, but he is not yet designated the victim, cause or savior of her catastrophe. His fixation on Lynleit continues to matter. Her own flaws do not make his hurtful inattention deserved. Nor does his care supply an automatic cure for her decisions. Their ordinary company and professional duties need enough space that the reckoning threatens a life the reader has actually come to know. The sound and the mythic comparison The musical brief is beautiful, dark, intense and sexually charged: deep D minor, roughly 120 BPM, multiple female voices, and an almost operatic repetitive structure. Seduction and exhilaration carry an undertone of judgment, danger and approaching consequences. These are supplied creative directions, not independently measured properties or in-world magical instructions. The mythic comparison places Sherie between conduct Ishtar might admire and territory where Ereshkigal demands payment. Use it to think about power, descent and cost. It establishes neither goddess as a story actor, gives Sherie no Cult membership, and does not require a literal underworld. Thematic Direction owns that separation. Kyrie Eleison is Sherie's personal theme. It is not automatically the unnamed recurring motif proposed for Sherie and Felix's relationship. A recording's title, artwork and sacred language do not decide her faith, magical status or fate. Decisions still needed The Questions ledger tracks the catastrophic game, its cost, the possibility of salvation and any late supernatural discovery. No exact Arc, antagonist, death, punishment, sacrifice or rescue is fixed. Her existing negotiation and card-game scenes remain unchanged. Author's Desk

entries.subtitle: Country Profile
entries.text: The Duchy of Narvea · v1 Country Profile A concise visual guide to the mapped Baltic country where the story takes place, including its cities, diplomatic legacy, divided authority, institutions, and multilingual culture. The Duchy of Narvea At a glance The Duchy of Narvea is the main country in which the story takes place. It is a large, sovereign Baltic state stretching along much of the eastern Baltic coast, from the approaches to St. Petersburg toward the frontier near Gdansk. Narvea is a constitutional duchy with two real centers of authority: the Ducal Crown and the parliamentary state . The Duke is an independent sovereign, not a subordinate noble. Parliament and the Prime Minister control ordinary government. Sovereignty resides jointly in the Crown and the Nation. Identity Narvean is a civic identity shared across a culturally varied population. Citizens may belong to different regional, linguistic, religious, urban, or rural communities while identifying fully and politically as Narvean. The country modernized without erasing its older institutions. Modern ministries, elections, police, and armed forces exist beside a ducal court, inherited ranks, ceremonial precedence, and a separate Ducal Guard. European diplomacy Narvea historically became a center of European diplomacy. Opposing powers gathered there to resolve disputes before they escalated into open conflict, giving the duchy influence far beyond its size or military strength. During the Napoleonic Wars of 1803 to 1815, Narvea played an important and constructive role in containing the continental crisis. The settlements of this period also began shaping the country's borders into their modern form. In 1917, negotiations held in Narvea contained an eastern political crisis before it could become a revolution. Territory Long Baltic coastline and several major ports Important agricultural regions and trade routes Multiple linguistic, religious, and cultural regions Strategic frontier with Russia Strong commercial and military importance in the Baltic The country's exact borders are not fully recorded. entries.title: The Oneiric Confluence · v1
entries.subtitle: Holumn Research
entries.text: The Oneiric Confluence · v1 Holumn Research Shared-dream evidence with Sherie's no-kissing boundary, a six-person briefing and unresolved Lynleit/Kyrien content. The Oneiric Confluence HI-009. Common name: The Shared Night. The Holumn rules and the main events of The Shared Night are canon. The chapter's dialogue remains a draft and its chronology is unplaced. This does not change the separate non-canon status of Anima's dream studies. Shared experience Affected sleepers encounter one another in a common dream environment. Independent accounts preserve matching conversations, actions, private details and emotional sequences. Windows, colours, distances, objects and the order of minor events can differ. The emotionally important parts tend to agree more closely. Overlapping sleep strengthens the impression of synchronization. It does not prove real-time contact. Natalia leaves open whether the participants meet within ordinary chronology or within a shared psychic space whose events are ordered differently when remembered. The initial reports include a customs officer shot by his supervisor in a nonexistent station, two students searching an impossible library for room zero, an accountant and secretary whose shared memory damages their working relationship, and two neighbours discussing grief over tea. No corresponding injuries, disappearances or physical marks are reported in this early cluster. Physical harmlessness is not established as a universal rule. Volition inside the dream Personality remains recognizable. Inhibition and the ability to refuse can weaken. A dreamer may know that an action contradicts their waking intentions while experiencing the impulse as their own and being unable to stop it. Another may hesitate, redirect a scene, question what is happening or briefly regain a choice. The material is not limited to sexual desire. Appetite, jealousy, aggression, tenderness, dependency, fear, domination, surrender, loneliness, grief, possessiveness, cruelty, affection and resentment can acquire form. Remembering pleasure in something one rejects can be more disturbing than remembering fear. Natalia's formulation is that the Holumn appears to weaken the waking ego's monopoly on authorship. That is her account of the effect, not a complete explanation of its mechanism. "The mask belongs to you too. Your restraint is you. Your anger is you. Your kindness is you. Your appetite is you. Your horror at the appetite is also you." "Do not confuse sincerity with totality." "A capacity revealed is not necessarily an intention confessed." A dream is not a reliable confession, proof of a fixed sexual preference, or a revelation that waking restraint was false. Neither participant can simply assign an unwanted action to the other's hidden wishes. Three working explanations These remain competing hypotheses, potentially overlapping. None is the settled cause. Hypothesis What it proposes What it leaves unresolved --- --- --- Depth Ordinary censorship weakens and disowned impulses or complexes gain autonomy. Why particular people meet and why some material becomes shared. Confluence The participants' expectations create a third imaginal field, with patterns neither would generate alone. How that field selects actions or relates to time. Holumn dramaturgy The phenomenon selects and intensifies material that the dreamers keep avoiding. Whether this selection is intentional, and why one conflict is staged rather than another. Natalia draws overlapping circles to explain the second possibility. "A relationship can contain things neither person contains in isolation." Colleagues may find themselves armed, people denying attachment may be forced into proximity, grief may bring back a dead person, and declared independence may become a shared house. These are possible forms, not a dictionary that translates each image into one meaning. Recognition and its limits Consciously identifying and expressing a pressure can sometimes restore a gap between impulse and action. It need not remove the image, desire, anger or danger, and it does not necessarily wake either person. Sherie and Felix experience a release, renewed pressure and another release. Their eventual ability to step away precedes their deliberately chosen kiss. Natalia's proposed explanation is: "An unconscious content does not need to seize consciousness as violently once consciousness agrees to see it." Her correction to Lynleit's simplification remains important: "So once you admit what's bothering you, the dream stops forcing you." "Sometimes." "That's what I said." "No. You made it sound like plumbing." Recognition is a condition worth investigating, not a universal escape instruction. No end to the wider incident has been established. The group's encounters Sherie and Felix Their recurring sexual dreams begin before either consciously initiates those encounters. Sherie initially treats them as private dreams. Felix recognizes enough correspondence to suspect otherwise before she discovers it during the briefing. The red room, windows and black water make denial difficult. Her anger concerns being witnessed, losing choice and discovering that he knew more than he said. They quarrel, joke and try to assign the embarrassing material to each other. Those accusations are not findings. Their later conversation also recalls an ordinary tender interval, when she slept against him and asked whether he was still there. They agree to test whether they can refrain from touching or kissing. Inside the next dream, acknowledging how each can feel absent even in the other's company helps them notice a change in the pressure. After it eases enough for them to leave one another alone, Sherie chooses to pull him closer and kiss him. The scene ends with their usual provocation, a waking exchange of messages and an arrangement for coffee. It does not establish that Felix's attachment to Lynleit has disappeared, that they form an official couple, or when their waking sexual intimacy begins. The chapter uses explicit sexual language but keeps the sexual acts off-page. Its humour belongs to these people handling exposure badly; the Holumn itself is not limited to comic or intimate outcomes. Lynleit and Kyrien They share a quiet house beside water, rain, tea, cards, two bedrooms and a cat. No overt sexual encounter occurs. The house may matter as ordinary companionship, but the furnishings do not prove a wish for marriage, predict their children or move their established sexual milestones. Natalia allows the house to remain a house rather than immediately reducing every object to a symbol. Hiyu, Yulia and Reiner Yulia reports Hiyu throwing a filing cabinet down stairs at her while calling it an experiment. Hiyu's recognition of his own vocabulary does not make attempted murder his waking intention. Yulia's precise, forensic handling of the discussion remains funny without making her prudish or helplessly embarrassed. Reiner observes the briefing, then leaves when the contrast between the dreams becomes too much for him. Natalia and Lynleit Natalia studies dreams, complexes, magical pathology and the imaginal structures through which psyche and magic meet. She observes the whole event and its associations before offering an interpretation. "Do not murder an image by making it symbolic too quickly" captures her objection to convenient one-to-one answers. Her expertise gives the group useful distinctions, not omniscience. Lynleit often sees the shape of an argument and simplifies too quickly. She also repeats Natalia's explanation almost word for word while claiming to have arrived at it independently. Natalia notices. Preserve the affection, irritation and practical intelligence on both sides rather than turning Lynleit into an incompetent student or Natalia into a lecturer no one can interrupt. Unresolved complications and development An echo persisting after one sleeper wakes is an author-proposed possibility, not an observed event in the chapter. If used later, distinguish the remembered participant from a representation that may continue acting without them. The awake person's lack of later memories would matter; it must not be erased to force agreement between accounts. Other possible consequences include fear of sleep, damaged friendships, dream violence, remembered cruelty or pleasure, and mistaken accusations based on supposed confessions. They are development possibilities, not additional incidents already suffered by this cast. The Nasu audit identifies usable effects and a bounded recognition response, but no established vector, selection rule, global duration or reliable cure. Keep those limits open. The psychological theories explain how Natalia reasons; they must not become a universal account of all Holumns or an explanation for Lester's origin. See incident testimony, the Moment, reader knowledge, and the Questions ledger. Natalia
