entries.title: Thematic Direction · v1
entries.subtitle: Writer's Direction
entries.text: Thematic Direction · v1 Writer's Direction Inanna's limited lore role and wider tonal association, Anima's three roles, and the boundaries of thematic integration. Thematic Direction Author-approved creative direction, 19 September 2026. This reference governs future writing and design; it adds no scenes, rituals, powers, or historical events. Several forces in one life MAGIARCHY's political, supernatural, horror, and espionage story allows sacred experience, violence, beauty, desire, family, and ordinary inconvenience to affect one another. An inherited duty can enter a private quarrel. A frightening supernatural problem can require research and provoke an indecent joke. Intimacy can change trust or carry political and metaphysical consequences. Let these combinations arise from the situation. Do not assemble every scene from the same ingredients. Work, professional duties, friendship, domestic life, and the main conflict continue after a relationship becomes intimate. The Intimacy Reference owns the scale and inclusion rules; Prose Style owns their expression in prose. The Inanna shadow The author's tonal orientation is that MAGIARCHY could be a story Inanna or Ishtar might keep on her own shelf. This is an internal creative comparison, not a statement for World pages or a historical claim about a real religion. Mysticism, magic, horror, war, sex, politics, espionage, murder, beauty, sacred power, inheritance, family, desire, violence, abrupt realism, and human cost may occupy the same event. The association is felt through their consequences, not through repeated invocations of Inanna. A reader needs no knowledge of Mesopotamian religion to follow the story. The Cult of Inanna remains one relatively small strand of explicit lore within a much larger Magi world. Its association with Fionn's lineage and Lynleit's indirect connection are confirmed. It does not explain all magic, female characters, attraction, politics, or the world's visual language. Keep unestablished practices, obligations, and covenants open. Mikhail's mock honorific is neither a rank nor authentic liturgy, and his provocation creates no sexual duty for Lynleit. Mascot, symbol, and template Anima, unofficially nicknamed Inanna, is the author's mascot outside story canon. Her symbolic role gathers beauty, danger, eroticism, ritual, sacred power, mystery, confidence, theatricality, and physical humanity into one design. It does not identify her with an in-world deity or Cult member. Her third role is practical: a female anatomical baseline for production. Character Image Production owns the approved templates and the required character-specific differences. Anatomy does not transfer costume, cultural identity, personality, or sexuality. Keep the mascot's own mask, palette, ornaments, and flowing fabric separate from that baseline. The inhabited world Hidden World Foundation owns the setting's period: contemporary life with substantial 18th- and 19th-century institutional inheritance. Ancient religious material can survive beneath modern intelligence work without turning the streets, clothing, or technology into generalized ancient fantasy. Applying this direction Consult the owning references before writing intimacy, changing Cult or lineage lore, designing female characters, or altering the setting. Keep most of this reasoning in writer and production guidance. Public records need the relevant facts, not an explanation of the author's thematic intentions. Preserve successful scenes and distinct designs. Do not invent more sex, more Cult lore, or more ancient imagery merely to make this direction visible. Author's Desk

entries.title: Thematic Integration Audit: 19 September 2026
entries.subtitle: Archive Audit
entries.text: Thematic Integration Audit: 19 September 2026 Archive Audit Current-source review of intimacy, Inanna, production templates, and the contemporary setting: corrections, preserved material, and open author decisions. Thematic Integration Audit: 19 September 2026 Scope: the current/default eight Chapters and 25 Moments, character appearance and relationship records, the shared tension registry, relevant World pages, Gallery mascot/template records, and active writer and production guidance. Historical revisions were used only to preserve prior publications. This audit applies the author's permanent thematic direction and the advisory Nasu framework; it does not select new canon. Already fitting Doom v7 combines survival, identity, research, theology, family history, embarrassment, and comedy. The uncertain proposal and incomplete attempt stay unchanged. Its density is useful without making it a formula for other scenes. The river's card games show attention without replacing the operation. The hotel refuge is nonsexual. The park milestone, later intercourse, pregnancy, and family revelations remain distinct. The church interlude gives Felix's flirting a comic consequence and leaves Lynleit's irritation non-romantic. Sherie and Felix retain their slowly developing familiarity and uneven recognition. Cult references in the Magiarchy record, relevant profiles, and Doom concern established lineage. They do not give Lynleit a sexual obligation or make the Cult the source of her attraction or abilities. Contemporary communications, surveillance, vehicles, firearms, research, and professional life already coexist with Narvea's aristocratic and Church institutions. Old buildings and clerical dress do not make the setting premodern. Anima's production sets already have Template labels, separate variants, original downloads, and non-canon metadata. Her ordinary artwork is separate from the production collection and character database. Existing female descriptions differ in stature, build, face, hair, and clothing; no character was redesigned against the new baseline rule. Corrections and durable additions The Intimacy Reference now states its specialist scope: the amount of space it devotes to sex is not the amount the story should devote to it. Added a proportional inclusion test and the continuation of duty and ordinary life after intimacy. Removed unsupported sexual-style predictions for Helena, Fionn, Yulia, Hiyu, Reiner, Drake, and Natalia. Patience, reserve, or curiosity alone did not establish those predictions. Confirmed relationships, attraction, and broader relational interpretations remain. V12 and its tension-data snapshot preserve the prior publication. The Cult question no longer presupposes that an ancestral covenant still creates a present obligation. Its confidence remains 10 percent; no answer was supplied. Thematic Direction owns the author-facing Inanna/Ishtar association. Prose Style contains only the short reusable principle; Scene Guidance contains the practical revision test. Character Image Production distinguishes Anima's mascot, symbolic, and anatomical roles, specifies what a character brief records, and separates body reference from costume, personality, and sexuality. Both production records state the anatomical use concisely. Hidden World Foundation owns the explicit 21st-century setting with substantial 18th- and 19th-century institutional inheritance. The World overview gives a short linked introduction rather than duplicating the explanation. AGENTS and the maintenance charter route future relevant work through these documents. Earlier document revisions and the live tension dependency were snapshotted before changes. The Intimacy reader mistook non-character headings for profiles. Its section handling now preserves introductory guidance, the relationship comparison, and later continuity sections outside the character cards, including in earlier versions. Decisions still belonging to the author Existing Questions and Contradictions remain authoritative. This pass does not decide the Cult's present covenants, private histories without scene evidence, the exact main-plot placement of Doom, the park's undrafted passage, Kyrien's discovery of the son, or the circumstances of Arc 2 reconciliation and the daughter's birth. No new answer or confidence increase follows from thematic guidance. Deliberately unchanged to avoid overstatement No extra sexual encounters, preferences, Cult practices, ancestry, powers, obligations, dates, institutions, or visual motifs were added. No approved joke, sensual appearance wording, or family milestone was removed to meet a numerical quota. Inanna's symbolic role was not placed on unrelated public lore pages. Anima was not promoted to a story character, and her costume was not spread across the cast. No new F/M/S notes, capability scores, timeline phases, or reader revelations were needed. The Nasu audit supported retaining Doom's uncertain treatment and consequential comedy. It did not justify expanding the Cult or treating a theme as a supernatural mechanism. The changes concern guidance and a concise setting statement, not a rewrite of existing Chapters or Moments. Author's Desk

entries.title: What Can You Tell Me About Magi?
entries.subtitle: Magistry
entries.text: What Can You Tell Me About Magi? Magistry A dialogue on the nature, secrecy, religion, and politics of Magi. What Can You Tell Me About Magi? Journalist: "What can you tell me about Magi?" Fionn: "What do you already know?" Journalist: "That you can do things other people cannot. Nobody will tell me how." Fionn: "We perceive conditions most people miss. With training, we can alter them. Encourage a fire, weaken material, redirect attention. The result may look impossible to someone who cannot see how it was done." Journalist: "So it is natural." Fionn: "It occurs within nature. That doesn't make it safe." Journalist: "And miracles?" Fionn: "A separate question. The Church considers certain acts an imitation of sacred miracles. A harmless result can still be forbidden." Journalist: "Who decides what counts?" Fionn: "The Church has a considerable interest in that decision." Journalist: "You sound less certain than before." Fionn: "I'm describing an agreement, not a law of physics." Journalist: "Why keep all this secret?" Fionn: "Because the institutions containing it depend on secrecy. A witness can expose people, methods, and threats we have not learned to control." Journalist: "Does that mean the witness has to die?" Fionn: "It means the authorities will consider how to prevent the exposure." Journalist: "Including killing them." Fionn: "Yes." Journalist: "Would you?" Fionn: "You have not given me a case." Journalist: "I have given you a person." Fionn: "And I have not given you permission to assume the decision is simple." Journalist: "The Church approves these decisions?" Fionn: "It holds final sanction over suppression. Magi have resources the Church needs, and powers it has reason to fear. Cooperation has not removed either fact." Journalist: "Then the Church rules you." Fionn: "A Magiarch governs a territory. There is no lawful universal ruler of Magi." Journalist: "Could the Magiarchs organize one?" Fionn: "Not without breaking the arrangement with the churches." Journalist: "That sounds political." Fionn: "It is." Journalist,Fionn

entries.title: Bone Archive
entries.subtitle: HI-008 · Bodily trace and discontinuous memory
entries.text: Bone Archive HI-008 · Bodily trace and discontinuous memory HI-008 bone-archive Bone Archive Bodily trace and discontinuous memory event curse The Bone Archive preserves experiences that have no place in the surviving account of a person's life. They return through memory and the body: an unexplained scar, a familiar pain, or a practiced movement its owner never learned. An officer steps aside before a shot is fired and later discovers a scar where the bullet would have entered. Anticipation, an unnoticed old injury, and a mistaken recollection can account for separate details. The officer's escape and scar alone do not prove that a previous history existed. An experience can survive without a continuous history to support it. Whether these traces come from discarded events, imposed experiences, or another disruption of continuity remains unresolved. No physical library or keeper has been identified. Recovered experience may provide knowledge or a practiced response while restoring remembered suffering. Attachments can persist toward people who do not share the remembered relationship. Records of bargains can survive without a recoverable account of their making; their authenticity does not establish the justice of the acts they concern. No countermeasure is known. The Archive cannot be relied on to undo events or predict the future. How its experiences are accessed, selected, repeated, or escaped is unknown. Bodily traces and surviving records make discontinuous experience materially consequential. No causal connection to the Spill or to Lester's origin is established. event,curse

entries.title: Doom Has an Address
entries.subtitle: HI-006 · Operational encounter and curse
entries.text: Doom Has an Address HI-006 · Operational encounter and curse HI-006 doom-has-an-address Doom Has an Address Operational encounter and curse event curse A Holumn transfers its own terminal condition to whoever consciously destroys it. When Lynleit and Kyrien kill it together, one fatal curse identifies both egos as a single causal answer and remains distributed across them. Fatigue, slow healing, and persistent exhaustion appear as a physical illness to anyone unaware of the curse. The linked decline has no explanation within that account. Natalia identifies the attachment as recognition of the ego, using Jung's definition of conscious identity. A joint killing gives the curse two subjects, each capable of restoring the condition in the other while both remain recognizably the same people. The subjects weaken over several weeks. Sleep ceases to restore them, injuries heal too slowly, Lynleit's magecraft becomes exhausting, and ordinary exertion eventually becomes difficult. Suppressing either attachment causes the other to restore it. The curse begins weakening the morning after Lynleit and Kyrien's incomplete attempt at intimacy and later disappears. The curse recognizes the egos responsible for the Holumn's destruction. The advisers identify the death of either subject as a way to release the survivor. Lynleit and Kyrien instead undergo enough reciprocal identity change to break its recognition. That outcome does not establish a reliable treatment for other subjects or curses. Destroying this Holumn transfers its fatal condition to its killers. Lynleit and Kyrien survive after an incomplete attempt at intimacy changes both identities enough to break its recognition. story.html?chapter=doom-has-an-address event,curse

entries.title: Sleepers
entries.subtitle: HI-007 · Kyrien's encounter
entries.text: Sleepers HI-007 · Kyrien's encounter HI-007 sleepers Sleepers Kyrien's encounter Human figures hang roughly twenty to fifty metres above ground or water, heads lowered and limbs loose. Most of those Kyrien sees resemble men in trench coats and hats. Their faces are obscured by height and angle. No police or government account is available. No Magus or Church interpretation is available. Clothing shifts in the wind and figures sway slightly. They do not attack, follow, communicate, or visibly react to being watched. Whether they are people is unknown. No weakness or countermeasure is known. Kyrien does not attempt to harm them. The manifestation remains passive while Kyrien observes it. Its connection to the Spill is unknown. moments.html?moment=sleepers-above-the-river

entries.title: The Drowned Choir
entries.subtitle: HI-003 · Operational encounter
entries.text: The Drowned Choir HI-003 · Operational encounter HI-003 the-drowned-choir The Drowned Choir Operational encounter embodied environmental A pale girl rises from the river with her eyes sewn shut by fishing line and a dress made from dead fish. She enslaves the souls of people drowned in the river and uses their hands to pull new victims beneath the surface. Maren and the surviving officers report trained swimmers being pulled down by an unexpected force. An ordinary investigation could attribute their accounts to darkness, panic, current, exhaustion, or witnesses influencing one another. There is no visible attacker aboard the empty contraband boats. The girl is an embodied Holumn controlling the river's accumulated drowned souls. Their hands seize victims beneath the water. She remains silent in this encounter. Submerged hands seize swimmers by the legs and pull downward. Lynleit's blue flame burns them even beneath the water and forces their grip open. They cannot pass through the surface layer beneath her feet once her water walking manifests. The girl's tilted head reads as confusion when Lynleit remains above the river. Unusually heavy mist interrupts visibility across the river, but the near water remains visible from the park bank. Its source and mechanism are not established by this encounter. Lynleit's blue flame burns the submerged hands. Once the surface supports her, the hands beneath her cannot reach through it. This is an observed boundary around her escape, not a proven restriction across the entire river. No method of freeing the enslaved dead or defeating the girl is confirmed. The Drowned Choir takes the contraband crews before the boats reach the bridge. The current carries the empty vessels onward. The Drowned Choir is distinct from the river leviathan. story.html?chapter=the-water-beneath-her-feet embodied,environmental

entries.title: The Last Piece
entries.subtitle: HI-002 · Missing-person incident
entries.text: The Last Piece HI-002 · Missing-person incident HI-002 the-last-piece The Last Piece Missing-person incident event curse A puzzle purchased at a market compels its owner to finish it. When the final piece is placed, the owner disappears and enters the missing-persons archive. Investigators see a purchased object, a developed obsession, and a disappearance. The puzzle may be treated as an unrelated possession, a clue to voluntary flight, or an instrument used by another person. The compulsion and completion belong to the same rule. Placing the final piece completes the condition that permits the disappearance. Attention narrows into compulsion. When the puzzle is completed, the owner disappears and has not been found. The object remains. No countermeasure is confirmed. Refusing completion appears safer than solving the object, but the strength and transfer of the compulsion remain unknown. The puzzle ties a disappearance to an ordinary act: placing the final piece. event,curse

entries.title: The Nameless Street
entries.subtitle: HI-005 · Urban legend and direct encounter
entries.text: The Nameless Street HI-005 · Urban legend and direct encounter HI-005 the-nameless-street The Nameless Street Urban legend and direct encounter environmental event curse A lost visitor may enter a deserted old street whose lanes, stairs, courtyards, and hills cannot be reconciled with the surrounding city. Following anyone encountered there may prevent the visitor from returning to ordinary streets. Felix sees Lynleit stop responding, move toward a city bench, and faint after lunch. Dizziness, a severe headache, a dream, or a neurological episode can explain the only part of the incident another person directly observes. In Lynleit's encounter, impossible routes isolate her and a crying child leads her to a fall. Whether the girl, the boy, and the red balloon are permanent features of the Holumn remains unknown. The visitor is separated without perceiving a threshold, becomes dizzy and disoriented, and cannot navigate the district by ordinary geometry. Lynleit follows a crying girl to a broken fence, is pushed toward a dead boy below, and returns to a city bench before impact. The urban warning instructs visitors not to follow anyone encountered on the street. It is not known whether refusing the lure guarantees escape or why Lynleit returns after following it. Lynleit cannot reconcile the street with Vilen's geography. Her memory of the dead boy returns when she later finds Fionn's body, but no causal connection between the two events is established. environmental,event,curse

entries.title: The Oneiric Confluence
entries.subtitle: HI-009 · Shared-dream incident
entries.text: The Oneiric Confluence HI-009 · Shared-dream incident HI-009 the-oneiric-confluence The Oneiric Confluence Shared-dream incident event Sleepers remember encounters in a common dream environment. Their personalities remain recognizable while ordinary inhibition and the ability to refuse weaken. Coincidence, private dreams or unreliable recollection, until independently matching details become difficult to dismiss. A Holumn connects sleepers through shared dream experience. Its relation to waking chronology and the source of particular actions remain uncertain. Corresponding conversations and emotionally important events survive waking, with discrepancies in peripheral details. Reported dreams include violence, intimacy, grief and ordinary companionship. Early reports show no corresponding injuries. Naming and recognizing a pressure can sometimes restore a gap between impulse and action. This neither ends the dream nor guarantees safety or lasting control. Unconscious experience ceases to be reliably private. Shared recollection can damage trust even when the body wakes unharmed. story.html?chapter=the-shared-night event

entries.title: The River That Is Too Deep
entries.subtitle: HI-004 · Accumulated incident pattern
entries.text: The River That Is Too Deep HI-004 · Accumulated incident pattern HI-004 the-river-that-is-too-deep The River That Is Too Deep Accumulated incident pattern embodied environmental Something immense moves beneath the city river despite stretches too shallow to contain it. Impossible waves damage boats and kayaks, while drowned bodies lose pieces to bites larger than any expected river predator could make. Each report can be separated into wake damage, submerged debris, boating accidents, postmortem animal activity, or exaggerated witness comparison. Together they remain difficult to explain without inventing a cause the river should not contain. The leviathan may be an animal-like Holumn, the river giving itself predatory mass, or a depth that exists only when the manifestation passes through it. The river behaves as though it can briefly contain a body larger than its physical depth. Water displacement, impact damage, and feeding traces persist after the shape itself is gone. No countermeasure is confirmed. Its dependence on the river may be a boundary, but it is not yet known whether the water contains the Holumn or belongs to it. The damage suggests a moving mass larger than the river's measured depth could contain. This leviathan is a separate Holumn from the Drowned Choir. embodied,environmental

entries.title: The Voice on the Line
entries.subtitle: HI-001 · Victim testimony
entries.text: The Voice on the Line HI-001 · Victim testimony HI-001 the-voice-on-the-line The Voice on the Line Victim testimony disembodied curse Have you heard of a telephone call that answers to you in your own voice? At first I thought whoever was on the phone was repeating me. But it was my own voice. At first it felt like an echo, as all it did was repeat my words. But then it started calling me incessantly, and it was talking to me, in bizarre ways. In my own voice. Police and communications specialists would first investigate harassment, recording fraud, a compromised exchange, equipment failure, or a witness in psychological distress. Magi and special envoys treat the change from repetition to unsolicited speech as the decisive detail. Something learned the witness's voice, then began using it without the witness. The calls become incessant. The voice stops merely repeating the witness and begins speaking independently. No countermeasure is confirmed. The calls use an ordinary telephone line. No visible body accompanies the borrowed voice. disembodied,curse

entries.title: There Is No Eleventh Floor
entries.subtitle: HI-010 · Architectural entrapment and rescue testimony
entries.text: There Is No Eleventh Floor HI-010 · Architectural entrapment and rescue testimony HI-010 there-is-no-eleventh-floor There Is No Eleventh Floor Architectural entrapment and rescue testimony event An office worker enters an elevator in a ten-floor building and encounters impossible floors, repeated rooms and luring voices. Lynleit brings him back; six minutes have elapsed on the office clock. Disorientation, panic and unreliable recollection can describe the witness's distress, but do not account for the spatial and material observations in the rescue testimony. The incident imposes a hostile sequence of routes and thresholds. Whether its figures are parts of one Holumn or separate manifestations is unknown. Floor numbers mislead, routes repeat or change, clocks disagree, and voices borrow familiar identities. Some grasping forms stop at yellow paint. Gunfire interrupts but cannot stop the final pursuer; blue flame follows the painted edges through the distorted stairwell and buys time to leave. Physical continuity and repeated tests offer temporary guidance. Waiting rather than choosing another route precedes an elevator's appearance. Neither this escape nor the painted boundary is established as universally reliable, and the Holumn is not shown destroyed. An ordinary workplace becomes an imposed state of entrapment without a known entry condition. Rescue leaves the witness vulnerable to Church suppression and lasting doubt. A direct causal link to the Spill is not established. story.html?chapter=there-is-no-eleventh-floor event

entries.title: Leviathan-hide coat
entries.subtitle: IA-001 · Anomalous garment
entries.text: Leviathan-hide coat IA-001 · Anomalous garment A blue garment left to Lynleit through Fionn's concealed intervention. It changes form without accepting commands and shields only what Lynleit deliberately covers with it. Held by Lynleit Lynleit lynleit Fionn fionn Arranged the substitution before his death A material called the hide of leviathan The nature and source of the material are not identified. Blue coat Its familiar full-length form and the appearance in which Lynleit first understands what Fionn left her. Scarf A smaller form chosen by the garment without instruction from Lynleit. Blue suede jacket The garment can imitate the fitted jacket Lynleit lost during the Drowned Choir attack. Other clothing The coat can assume other wearable forms. Lynleit cannot choose which form appears on a given day. Minor magical protection The material can shield a covered body from minor magically induced damage and phenomena. Protection by coverage Wearing the garment is not sufficient. Lynleit must use it to cover the threatened part of her body. Protection of another person Lynleit can remove the garment and place or throw it over someone who needs immediate protection. Autonomous form The garment decides its own appearance and movement. Lynleit cannot command it; it can choose to cooperate with her, as it does while covering the office-building witness. Protection is local to the area physically covered by the garment. The garment does not provide passive protection merely because Lynleit is wearing it. Lynleit cannot command its form or rely on it to assume the form most useful to the situation. How much magical force the coat can withstand is unknown. Arc 1 Early Arc 1, before the river revelation Quiet cooperation Lynleit throws the coat over a witness before a blue-flame outburst. Its edges settle around him of their own accord. He notices something he cannot explain; Lynleit still does not know the garment's nature. The rescue occurs early in Arc 1, while Fionn is alive and before Kyrien's river revelation. Arc 1 The river operation The lost jacket The Drowned Choir tears away Lynleit's fitted blue suede jacket while dragging her underwater. She later complains about losing it because she liked it. Arc 1 Middle of the main story Fionn's concealed substitution After Fionn's death, Lynleit discovers that he had discreetly replaced the blue coat she wore with the leviathan-hide garment. Arc 1 After the discovery An inherited protection Lynleit carries the garment after discovering its properties. It sometimes takes the form of the suede jacket she lost. Chapter There Is No Eleventh Floor story.html?chapter=there-is-no-eleventh-floor A witness shelters beneath the coat before Lynleit knows it has a will of its own. Moment The Coat Fionn Left Behind moments.html?moment=the-coat-fionn-left-behind Lynleit discovers the substitution and the garment's properties. Chapter The Water Beneath Her Feet story.html?chapter=the-water-beneath-her-feet The river operation in which Lynleit loses the jacket later imitated by the coat. Character Lynleit character.html?character=lynleit#equipment-title Lynleit carries the coat and uses it to shield herself or others. Character Fionn character.html?character=fionn Fionn arranged the substitution without explaining it to Lynleit.

entries.subtitle: IA-003 · Magecraft protection
entries.text: Lynleit's protective gloves IA-003 · Magecraft protection Special black leather gloves protect Lynleit's skin during outbursts of her blue flame. She keeps them draped over her belt, usually hidden beneath her coat. Carried by Lynleit Lynleit lynleit Black leather; protective construction unspecified Pair of black leather gloves Carried together over the belt and pulled on before a blue-flame outburst. Skin protection The gloves protect the skin they cover from Lynleit's blue flame. She relies on them rather than accepting burns as a normal cost of competent use. Practical preparation When putting on a glove to use blue flame, she rolls up the corresponding sleeve so her clothing does not catch fire. With both gloves, she rolls up both sleeves. A nearby person still needs separate coverage. Unprotected or carelessly exposed skin risks damage and scarring. The gloves do not remove the strain of using blue flame or protect an uncovered bystander. Their maker, construction, acquisition and limits against other forces are unknown. entries.title: A Meeting Beyond Authority
entries.subtitle: MOM-005 · Unknowing Convergence
entries.text: A Meeting Beyond Authority MOM-005 · Unknowing Convergence At night on a hill overlooking Vilen, Sherie leads an illegal negotiation in which Drake seeks limited access to MSF resources without surrendering sensitive evidence. Sherie secures MSF assistance through negotiations neither the government nor Court has authorized. A hill overlooking Vilen Sherie believes her uncle when the Court does not. Sherie is Drake's niece and is training under him to become a diplomat. The approach to Lynleit is entirely Sherie's idea and strategy. Sherie develops the plan against Drake's wishes, persuades him to participate, and takes charge of the meeting and negotiations. Drake remains opposed to the illegal approach but attends after Sherie overcomes his resistance. After the negotiation succeeds, Sherie asks Drake to praise and pamper her for her first achievement. Drake still cannot decide whether an alliance with Lynleit is a strategic advantage or a dangerous mistake. Drake remains the story's main strategic mind before and after this event. The meeting takes place at night on a hill overlooking Vilen. Drake does not hand sensitive evidence to people outside the aristocratic circle. He and Sherie request access to selected MSF resources and capabilities in exchange for concessions or favors. Sherie and Drake bring Heyk as their bodyguard and confidant. Lynleit brings Felix, Reiner, and Kyrien as her bodyguards and confidants. The main negotiation belongs to Lynleit, Sherie, and a reluctant Drake, while the others contribute opinions and warnings. Lynleit regards the request as dangerous. Felix openly protests, while Kyrien stays silent and tests the suspected conspiracy against his own past grievances. What concessions or favors do Drake and Sherie offer for the confirmed river-surveillance operation? What access or resources does Lynleit refuse beyond the limited operation? What would finally convince Drake that the alliance should be preserved or abandoned? Sherie must persuade Drake that Lynleit is worth the legal and political danger of contact. Sherie claims praise and pampering for her success while Drake remains uncertain about what she has created. The private agreement then produces a narrow intelligence operation. The team may inspect the suspected shipment but cannot arrest anyone or seize material. Drake drake Sherie sherie Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Reiner reiner Kyrien kyrien Heyk heyk

entries.subtitle: MOM-001 · The Hidden Wager
entries.text: After the Failed Attempt · v1 · Archived MOM-001 · The Hidden Wager Lynleit interrogates Kyrien after his failed attempt against an MSF-protected Magus politician nearly harms her, then converts his prison risk into a secret recruitment without telling him she was present. Lynleit recruits Kyrien under threat of imprisonment without revealing that his attack nearly harmed her. Police office Kyrien has made a failed attempt to assassinate a politician who belongs to the Magi world. The politician is under MSF protection when Kyrien makes the attempt. Lynleit is present and is almost harmed unintentionally during the failed attack. Lynleit knows Kyrien nearly harmed her, but Kyrien does not know she was present. Lynleit never tells Kyrien that his attempt placed her in danger. The immediate aftermath brings him into a police office. Lynleit conducts the interrogation. Lynleit invokes an extraordinary transfer clause in MSF's government service contract, drafted under Fionn for extraordinary threats. The transfer gives her control of Kyrien's case, and she does not disclose the secret recruitment to Fionn. Kyrien faces prison unless he agrees to become Lynleit's secret helper. His freedom remains conditional on accepting Lynleit's demands, leaving him confined to her whims. Lynleit's private strategy is to keep Kyrien as a secret trump card against Helena. The recruitment occurs within the first few chapters, well before Fionn's assassination. Lynleit acts because her intuition warns her of near-future danger before she has enough evidence to define it. Lynleit is Fionn's biological daughter. Helena is Lynleit's stepmother and Fionn's wife. Lynleit already suspects Helena of being an enemy despite that family relationship. Kyrien's father held an important position in Narvea's military. The targeted politician was involved in causing his father's death. Kyrien obtained the knowledge and tools for the attempt through his father's military background. The attempt fails solely because the politician belongs to the Magi world. The politician's survival later creates consequences for Lynleit. Lynleit notices Helena probing Fionn's schedules, visitors to the family house, trusted officers, and Lynleit's own travel. Lynleit suspects murder because Helena appears to be studying the family too carefully. What is the politician's name, office, and exact role in Kyrien's father's death? How does the surviving politician later retaliate against Lynleit? What initial cover story conceals Kyrien's release and unofficial MSF association? Kyrien's father's death, the politician's involvement, the MSF protection assignment, and the military knowledge behind the attempt still need connective scenes. Kyrien enters Lynleit's service unwillingly without knowing that the handler controlling his case was nearly harmed by his attack. Lynleit must later decide who, if anyone, can be trusted with the recruitment. The arrangement preserves him as hidden leverage against Helena through the early investigation. Fionn's much later assassination vindicates Lynleit's warning without proving that she understood its source. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

entries.title: After the Failed Attempt · v3 · Current
entries.subtitle: MOM-001 · The Hidden Wager
entries.text: After the Failed Attempt · v3 · Current MOM-001 · The Hidden Wager Kyrien's legal campaign establishes credible evidence but cannot obtain accountability. After his failed attack at the Prosecutor General's dinner, Lynleit questions him with his lawyer present and offers confidential paid work. Lynleit gains cooperation without a confession or trust, while Kyrien tries to get home to his mother. Police office Kyrien works for years to pay competent lawyers while caring for his mother. The preliminary inquiry confirms knowingly distorted evidence. A closed review protects the prosecutor under a confidential national-security mandate. After an interval, a customer humiliates his mother and the shopkeeper asks her to stop making a scene. His mother apologizes: "I'm sorry. I thought I could manage the shopping." He decides to kill the prosecutor only after taking her home and caring for her. The prosecutor is promoted to Prosecutor General and survives the attempt at his appointment dinner, where MSF assists with security. Lynleit is present and nearly harmed; Kyrien does not know she attended. He escapes immediate capture and is detained later. His lawyer stays involved during questioning and the private employment proposal. Lynleit examines employment and payment records. Kyrien admits his family's mistreatment without confessing to the attack. Lynleit asks his lawyer to confirm his mother's welfare; she never threatens her. Lynleit privately recognizes suppression and feels she needs an ally outside her circle. She conceals magic and her attendance from Kyrien. The offer includes paid confidential work, release support, and care expenses, subject to approvals and legal review, not unconditional immunity. Kyrien agrees reluctantly if the written terms match the offer. His refusal to repeat his mother's apology suggests how difficult the humiliation remains to disclose. inferred What is the Prosecutor General's name, and is he himself a Magus? What exactly happens during the attempt, including the concealed magical contribution to failure? What continuing cover protects Kyrien's service from Fionn and Helena? His military-police commander father silently witnesses magic while protecting his officers from a fugitive's assault, then kills the fugitive in self-defence. Officials connected to the Magiarchy engineer a prosecution and obtain sanction to murder him, disguising it as suicide. Kyrien finances an inquiry that proves distorted evidence but fails to obtain accountability. The shop incident comes after an interval. Kyrien's work and care obligations continue. Lynleit never reveals her attendance. He remains ignorant of magic until seeing her walk on water at the river; she initially only suspects what he saw. Lynleit tells only Felix and Reiner in her circle. Much later a separate prosecutorial offence may allow revenge under an as-yet undefined Magi prohibition, without redress for the father's protected persecution. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

entries.text: After the Rescue MOM-031 · Early Arc 1, after the office-building rescue After Lynleit rescues the trapped office worker, Fionn questions the risks she took. Her appeal to Natalia's safety advice brings an unexpected answer. Show the distance between Lynleit's confidence and Fionn's assessment of her readiness, without treating rescue as wrongdoing. Fionn's office Fionn reprimands Lynleit in his office after the elevator and stairwell rescue. He is concerned about the recklessness and danger, not angry that she saved a bystander. He does not yet consider her capable enough as a Magus to survive such situations competently. Lynleit defends herself by citing clear and practical safety instructions from Natalia. Fionn surprises her by revealing that Natalia herself notified him of the incident. How soon after the rescue does the office conversation occur? Does Lynleit's pursuit of Ash immediately follow this conversation? The office-building rescue has occurred. Fionn is alive; Natalia and Lynleit are the other established Magi in this early part of the story. Myka and Lester have not entered it, and Kyrien has not yet discovered magic. The timing of the cat chase relative to the reprimand is not established. Lynleit lynleit Fionn fionn

entries.title: Ash in the Family House · v1 · Archived
entries.subtitle: MOM-002 · Vanishing Point
entries.text: Ash in the Family House · v1 · Archived MOM-002 · Vanishing Point Before the crisis reaches her home directly, Lynleit clumsily chases a grey male cat named Ash, catches him, then cannot bring herself to expel him into the rain. Lynleit catches Ash but lets him stay because it is raining. The Director's House The scene occurs in the early chapters, after danger has begun outside but before Lynleit's life starts to collapse. The grey cat is male and is named Ash. The family maintained an original house in Turon while Lynleit's mother was alive and Lynleit was in junior school. After her mother's death, the family moved to a Vilen residence for Fionn's access to the capital. Lynleit accepted the move only after securing the third-floor study-bedroom. The Vilen house is a three-floor family residence on a wooded hill above the river that flows toward the city center, with a small rear park and garden. Lynleit values the thick vegetation and the sound of leaves and branches in the wind. She regards nearby flowing water as life energy and seeks its emotional grounding despite her childhood fear of drowning. The garden-facing first floor contains glass-enclosed relaxation areas that preserve contact with nature through every season. Lynleit personally chases Ash through the house, revealing a clumsier and more childish side of her than her public role usually permits. Lynleit eventually catches Ash. She cannot bring herself to expel him because rain is falling outside. Ash decides to remain and becomes a permanent loiterer in the family home. Who else in the household accepts or resists Ash's permanent presence? The first disappearances have begun outside Lynleit's private life, but the full crisis, Fionn's death, and the destruction of her family security remain ahead. Ash remains inside the house as a quiet domestic echo of the danger Lynleit cannot keep outside. Later losses can turn the once-comic chase into an omen whose meaning becomes clear only in retrospect. Lynleit lynleit Ash ash

entries.title: Because There's a Battle to Be Fought · v1 · Archived
entries.subtitle: MOM-017 · Clear Her Name
entries.text: Because There's a Battle to Be Fought · v1 · Archived MOM-017 · Clear Her Name Lynleit asks Kyrien why he continues to help her and risk his life when no reward awaits him. He answers immediately: "Because there's a battle to be fought." Lynleit wants to spare Kyrien needless danger. He considers the fight sufficient reason to go. Unspecified Lynleit is bewildered by Kyrien's willingness to keep helping her and entering danger when no reward has been promised. She does not want to place him in danger without necessity. Kyrien answers bluntly and without hesitation: "Because there's a battle to be fought." For Kyrien, the existence of a battle is itself a reason to enter it. The impulse belongs to the same childish competitive streak that makes him want to win every game. Kyrien does not say that he is fighting for Lynleit, leaving the reader to judge how much of his persistence is self-directed and how much attachment has entered a motive he still describes as combat. inferred His need to prove his worth may be directed toward his own standards, the memory of his father, or both. inferred Which operation or immediate danger prompts Lynleit to ask the question? How does Lynleit respond to an answer that removes her from Kyrien's stated reason for staying? Does Kyrien understand at this point that attachment has become part of the battle he keeps choosing? Kyrien has repeatedly accepted danger beside Lynleit, but rescue, coercion, and operational necessity do not fully explain why he keeps returning. Lynleit can rely on Kyrien without mistaking his involvement for obedience or romance. His later free choice to remain after her authority fails confirms that the answer was not an excuse. Lynleit lynleit Kyrien kyrien

Their sexual relationship develops after the curse has ended, alongside Lynleit's work and the closing pressures of Arc 1. Unspecified location Their first completed sexual encounter occurs after Doom Has an Address, later in Arc 1. Several further encounters follow before Lynleit's pregnancy and disappearance. Their second encounter is lighter and more playful because neither needs to deny that the first threshold occurred. entries.text: Beyond the Cordon · v1 · Archived MOM-010 · The Quarantine Hiyu enters the quarantined park to test his impossible suspicion that magic is involved in the disappearances. Yulia goes with him to prove the theory wrong and keep him alive. Hiyu's theory takes him and Yulia into a danger neither understands. The quarantined park in Vilen Hiyu and Yulia are university students in their mid-twenties who study criminology. Yulia is a classical ISTJ and the top student in their class, with meticulous command of detail and criminological protocol. Hiyu is an ENTP whose personal investigations rely on intuitive threads, improvised methods, and rapid hypothesis generation. Without knowing that magic exists, Hiyu suspects it is involved in the disappearances. Yulia enters partly to prove him wrong and partly to prevent him from facing the danger alone. How do they bypass the cordon? What do they find, and how do they survive or escape? What lasting evidence, injury, or change in their relationship follows the trespass? The widening disappearance case gives Hiyu enough fragments to form an impossible but directionally correct theory. Yulia rejects the conclusion but refuses to let him test it alone. Their evidence connects two civilian students to the larger institutional response. Hiyu correctly suspects magic but still lacks any complete knowledge of it. Hiyu hiyu Yulia yulia

entries.title: Doom Has an Address · v4 · Superseded
entries.subtitle: MOM-021 · Later in Arc 1
entries.text: Doom Has an Address · v4 · Superseded MOM-021 · Later in Arc 1 Lynleit and Kyrien survive an identity-bound curse after an incomplete attempt at intimacy. Lynleit will not explain what she tried, and Kyrien does not know why they recovered. The curse ends before Lynleit can use its treatment to explain away her continued interest in Kyrien. Several locations, ending in a private room Lynleit and Kyrien consciously destroy the same Holumn together. Destroying the Holumn completes its mechanism and transfers its terminal condition to the people responsible for its death. Their joint action leaves one curse distributed across two identities rather than creating two separate curses. Both weaken, sleep ceases to restore them, minor injuries heal slowly, and ordinary exertion becomes difficult. Lynleit's magecraft also grows exhausting. Suppressing the condition in either person fails because the remaining attachment reconstructs it in the other. The traditional solution requires one of them to die first, collapsing the relation and releasing the survivor. Lynleit refuses the fatal solution and consults other Magi, Magiarchal records, prohibited theurgy, Natalia, and Father Mikhail. Natalia explains the shared attachment with two names on paper. She introduces the ego hypothesis and quotes Jung, using her failed decision diary, her departure from the Academy, and worry over Myka to distinguish descriptions of identity from changes in lived decisions. Father Mikhail independently confirms that conversion, marriage, war, parenthood, confession, and other identity-changing experiences have disrupted related curses. Mikhail tells Lynleit that sex could produce the necessary discontinuity only if a sufficient reciprocal attachment already exists. Lynleit does not tell Kyrien about the proposed method and gradually begins treating their relationship as a possible procedure. With the prognosis reduced to days, Lynleit attempts to initiate an encounter while behaving with unusual hostility and embarrassment. The attempt does not fully cross the boundary between them, but the curse begins weakening the following morning and is later gone. Lynleit's unread pages and repeated denials suggest that she remains interested in Kyrien after the curse is gone. inferred Kyrien knows Lynleit tried to sleep with him, refused to explain why, and became hostile whenever he mentioned the evening. Kyrien suspects the attempt and their recovery are connected, but Lynleit withholds the proposed treatment. The incomplete attempt and its aftermath change both identities enough to break the curse's recognition. Lynleit answers Natalia's questions, jokes about her old marking, offers to approve her research, and keeps the diagram. Natalia acknowledges what she cannot measure and does not promise a cure. What identity, appearance, and prior incident history belong to the Holumn before Lynleit and Kyrien destroy it? What operation places them in position to destroy it together? Which Magi first identify the traditional one-death solution, and how much of the prognosis becomes known outside the four people in this scene? What happens during the incomplete attempt? What lasting effects, if any, remain after the curse collapses? Which later encounter becomes Lynleit and Kyrien's first completed sexual threshold? Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge have already occurred. Kyrien has chosen to remain without Lynleit's former power to compel him. Doom is a later subplot in the second half of Arc 1, not a fixed immediate prelude to her disappearance. Both survive without completing the sexual encounter. Their first completed encounter occurs later in Arc 1, before their established sexual relationship and the pregnancy near the Arc 2 threshold. Its exact placement remains unresolved. entries.text: Doom Has an Address · Version 1 · Alternate MOM-021 · Later in Arc 1 After Lynleit and Kyrien destroy a Holumn together, its death becomes one terminal curse written across both identities. Research leads Lynleit to a form of survival that requires reciprocal change rather than either person's death. Turns the pair's accumulated trust and involuntary attraction into the mechanism of a Holumn conflict without making romance the story's primary objective. Natalia's scholarship and Father Mikhail's Church records independently identify transformation as the only survivable answer. Several locations, ending in a private room Lynleit and Kyrien consciously destroy the same Holumn together. Destroying the Holumn completes its mechanism and transfers its terminal condition to the ego responsible for its death. Their joint action leaves one curse distributed across two identities rather than creating two separate curses. Their bodies weaken, sleep stops restoring them, minor injuries heal slowly, magical tolerance declines, and ordinary exertion becomes increasingly difficult. Suppressing the condition in either person fails because the remaining attachment reconstructs it in the other. The traditional solution requires one of them to die first, collapsing the relation and releasing the survivor. Lynleit refuses to choose which of them should live and searches Magiarchal records, medicine, prohibited theurgy, Natalia's research, and Church records for another answer. Natalia identifies the curse as an attachment to conscious identity and explains that profound transformation may make the original ego unrecognizable to it. Father Mikhail independently confirms that conversion, marriage, war, parenthood, confession, and other identity-changing experiences have disrupted related curses. Mikhail tells Lynleit that sex could produce the necessary discontinuity only if a sufficient reciprocal attachment already exists. Although Lynleit normally treats openness as a leadership skill, she keeps this proposed solution from Kyrien because its sexual and personal implications embarrass her, and initially evaluates their relationship as a possible procedure. When their prognosis contracts from weeks to days, Lynleit initiates a sudden, clumsy, and almost argumentative encounter. Kyrien has enough time to understand what she is asking and responds deliberately. Their simultaneous and reciprocal crossing changes the identities recognized by the curse and makes its sympathetic attachment unstable. Sex is not itself the cure. The curse fractures because the encounter embodies a relationship change neither identity can dismiss as hypothetical. Both survive, but neither remains psychologically identical to the person who entered the battle. The final change leaves the reader to infer which former boundaries have ended and what ordinary shared life might become possible before Lynleit's disappearance. inferred What identity, appearance, and prior incident history belong to the Holumn before Lynleit and Kyrien destroy it? What operation places them in position to destroy it together? Which Magi first identify the traditional one-death solution, and how much of the prognosis becomes known outside the four people in this scene? Where does the final private encounter occur within late Arc 1? Fionn's death and the nonsexual hotel refuge have already occurred. Kyrien has chosen to remain without Lynleit's former power to compel him. Doom is a later subplot in the second half of Arc 1, not a fixed immediate prelude to her disappearance. The curse fractures and both survive. Their short sexual relationship becomes part of an emerging shared life before Lynleit disappears near the Arc 2 threshold and her pregnancy becomes legible only at the opening of the next arc. entries.title: Father Mikhail Discovers the Breach
entries.subtitle: MOM-015 · Divided Attention
entries.text: Father Mikhail Discovers the Breach MOM-015 · Divided Attention Father Mikhail becomes the first authority to discover that Lynleit has shared forbidden knowledge of magic with outsiders. Kyrien corrects her attempt to limit the breach to himself by revealing that Felix and Reiner also know. Mikhail's discovery forces Lynleit to answer for the witnesses and contributes to MSF's later Magi role. Unspecified private location Father Mikhail is the first authority to learn that Lynleit has disclosed forbidden knowledge of magic to outsiders. Lynleit is unprepared for the discovery and promises to resolve the exposure on her own terms. Mikhail asks whether Kyrien is the only witness, and Lynleit reassures him. Kyrien immediately states that Felix and Reiner also know. Mikhail responds by looking at Lynleit in judgment rather than escalating the confrontation openly. Lynleit again promises to handle the problem in her own way. Mikhail leaves her with the warning: 'What you do is none of my business, but don't be surprised if I'll be sent to clean up your mess.' The encounter becomes an early cause of MSF's later transformation into a partly Magi private enterprise reporting to the Magiarchy and the Church. After Mikhail leaves, Lynleit confronts Kyrien privately for exposing Felix and Reiner. Kyrien does not apologize or retreat. Lynleit does not use her authority to punish him. Their delay in stepping apart lets the reader register unwanted physical awareness inside the argument without turning the institutional conflict into a romantic scene. inferred Kyrien remains to help Lynleit address the breach after the argument. Kyrien gives no reason for correcting Lynleit, leaving the reader to infer whether literal honesty, distrust of institutional half-truths, or another motive drives him. inferred Mikhail does not define his authority. Lynleit catches him by his tie and raises a Bible; he answers her reprimand with another flirtation. Show the familiar friction between Lynleit and Felix during an embarrassing public exchange. A church The organ had fallen silent. Felix had not. Lynleit found him beside a pew, holding the end of his blue tie out of the way while a nun gathered a stack of music books. Two more waited in the aisle. He had put on the helpful expression she knew rather too well. "Do you rehearse every evening?" he asked. "Tuesdays." "I might become a regular." "Felix." He turned. "She was telling me when to come back." "She was telling you when the choir rehearses." "Yes. I was listening." A loose sheet slipped from the stack. The nun caught it against her skirt. Felix reached to help, added something in a lower voice, and smiled. Lynleit took hold of his tie. "We are leaving." "Already? I was just making friends." He sat down abruptly as she drew him back toward the pew. A Bible lay on the seat beside his hand. Lynleit picked it up before he could sit on that too. "You can make friends outside." Felix glanced past her toward the aisle. She pulled the tie a little farther. "Flirt with nuns one more time!" The book was above her shoulder now. Felix leaned back against the pew and raised both hands. "I only have eyes for you." Nobody moved. The sister with the music books looked from him to Lynleit. Behind her, the other two had stopped rearranging their pages. Lynleit could feel the heat climbing to her ears. "That is not what I said." "I thought it might help." "How?" His eyes went to the Bible. "Has it?" "Excuse me." Lynleit turned. The nun had shifted the music books to one arm and was holding out her free hand. "May I have that back?" For a moment Lynleit looked at the offered hand without understanding. Then she lowered the Bible. "Of course. I am sorry." She placed it carefully on top of the music books. One corner had caught beneath her thumb; she smoothed it before letting go. Felix cleared his throat. "The other hand, too, if you can spare it." She was still holding his tie. She released it. "Outside." Felix straightened the knot. "Together?" Lynleit looked at him. "Going," he said. He caught the loose end of his tie before it snagged on the pew and followed her into the aisle. entries.title: Sleepers above the River · v1
entries.subtitle: MOM-024 · Placement undecided
entries.text: Sleepers above the River · v1 MOM-024 · Placement undecided On an early morning walk, Kyrien notices motionless human figures suspended above the river. He takes a boat downstream to see how far they extend. Kyrien follows an unexplained manifestation out of curiosity. The figures remain passive. Vilen river and pier The traffic light changed while Kyrien was still half a street away. By the time he reached the crossing it had gone red again. No cars had passed. He waited with his hands in his jacket pockets. Across the road, a delivery van stood outside a shuttered shop, its rear doors open. There was nobody beside it. Most of the windows above the shops were dark, although daylight had begun to show between the roofs. Was everyone still asleep? He crossed when the light changed and took the street toward the river. His shoes sounded loud beneath the overhanging balconies. At the end of the street the wind reached him, colder than it had been among the buildings, and he pulled his collar up. Steps led down to an exposed strip of bank beside a wooden pier. Water slapped against its posts. On the opposite side, the upper windows of a row of houses had caught the morning light; below them the bank remained in shadow. Kyrien stopped at the foot of the steps and looked along the water. Something dark hung above it. For a moment he took it for something farther away, attached to a building across the river. He moved a few paces sideways. The thing shifted against the roofs. It was a man. Kyrien tipped his head back. Thirty metres up, perhaps forty. A dark trench coat reached below the man's knees, and a hat hid most of his lowered head. His arms hung beside him. One foot was slightly lower than the other. Kyrien looked above him. No cable. He followed the empty air to either side, looking for the end of a crane, then turned to check the buildings behind the pier. Nothing nearby reached high enough. When he looked back, the man was still there. A gust lifted the bottom of the coat and let it fall. The body turned a little, too slowly for Kyrien to be sure at first. The hands stayed loose. He went out onto the pier. Its boards shifted under his weight, and the change of angle showed him a pale strip between one sleeve and a glove. Or perhaps it was the hand itself. He couldn't make out the face. Farther downriver, above the embankment, another man hung against the light sky. This one was heavier. His coat was shorter, his hat broader. His head had dropped forward in the same way. Kyrien looked from one to the other, then found a third beyond a roof, where he had mistaken the dark shape for part of a chimney. Were they asleep? He stood with that possibility for a few seconds. From this distance he couldn't see anyone breathing. He couldn't see a rope around a neck either. Sleepers, then. He needed some word for them. The first had turned far enough to show its other shoulder. It had done nothing else. Kyrien walked to the end of the pier, watching for a change as he came closer. There wasn't one. A small rowing boat was tied beside the lower landing. Two oars lay inside it. He looked downriver again. The farthest sleeper disappeared behind the corner of a building when he leaned to his left; from the road above, he doubted he would have noticed it at all. He stepped into the boat, steadied himself against a post and untied the line. The hull knocked against the landing before he pushed it clear. For a little while he watched the pier recede. Then he set the oars in their places and pulled toward the middle of the river. The blades made two broad disturbances in the otherwise quiet water. There were gaps between the figures. Past the first bend he went long enough without seeing one that he turned to look back. The man over the embankment was still visible behind him. Ahead, a narrow coat hung above a stand of trees. Kyrien counted five before he lost sight of the first. They were at different heights. One was little higher than the nearby roof; another hung well above it, perhaps fifty metres from the water. A sleeve stirred. Farther off, the hem of a coat moved in the opposite direction as the wind changed. He let the current carry the boat beneath the next one. From directly below he could see the soles of two shoes, trouser cuffs and the hands hanging clear of the coat. One hand was open. The fingers of the other curled slightly inward. The head remained beyond the shoulders and the brim of the hat. Kyrien rested the oars and watched. The boat drifted on. He had to turn on the seat to keep looking up. A shoe moved against the sky as the whole figure swayed, then settled. He faced downstream again and took up the oars. Beyond the next stretch of bank, another hat and pair of lowered shoulders came into view. Kyrien walks alone through Vilen early in the morning and reaches the river. Human figures hang without visible supports, their heads lowered and limbs loose. Most appear to be men in trench coats and hats. Kyrien looks for cables and a crane but finds neither. He privately calls the figures Sleepers and takes a rowing boat downstream. The figures neither attack nor communicate nor visibly react to his attention. Some figures would be difficult to notice from the street; their positions do not suggest a display arranged for Kyrien. inferred Kyrien continues downriver. The scene stops before his journey ends. When does this encounter occur, and what happens after Kyrien continues downstream? Are the figures human, and who can see them? What, if anything, does their appearance foreshadow? The preceding events and story phase are undecided. This is a solitary walk, not an MSF assignment. The continuation and main-plot connection remain undecided. No connection to the Drowned Choir or river leviathan is established. Kyrien kyrien

entries.text: The Nameless Street · v1 · Archived MOM-014 · Divided Attention During a casual walk after lunch with Felix, Lynleit enters a deserted labyrinthine street, follows a crying girl with a red balloon, sees a dead boy below a broken fence, and is pushed from the same ledge before waking on an ordinary city bench. Lynleit returns with a memory of a dead boy that later resurfaces when she finds Fionn. Vilen old town and an untraceable street The Nameless Street is an urban myth in the old town of central Vilen. Under unknown conditions, a lost visitor may enter it alone. Its buildings and routes form a labyrinth that does not obey the surrounding city. The warning attached to the myth is not to follow anyone encountered there, because those who do may never return to ordinary streets. Days before Fionn's murder, Lynleit is walking with Felix after a work lunch when she abruptly finds herself alone, dizzy, unsteady, and suffering a severe headache. A little girl carrying a red balloon appears, loses it, and runs away crying. Lynleit catches the balloon by its thread and follows the girl's cries so she can return it. The girl eventually stands beside a broken fence above an abrupt drop, looking down at the body of a dead boy. Lynleit releases the balloon in shock. The girl smiles and pushes her from the ledge. Before reaching the ground, Lynleit wakes on a bench in the ordinary city center while Felix fans her face with a piece of paper after her apparent faint. Whether the street is a place, an illusion, or another kind of Holumn remains unresolved. When Lynleit later sees Fionn's body below the hill at the family house, the memory of the boy stupefies her and gives Helena leverage to accuse her of pushing Fionn. Felix does not explain why he accepts Lynleit's implausible account without laughing, leaving his response to be read through their long friendship. inferred What conditions admit a visitor to the Nameless Street, and why does it take Lynleit on this day? Are the girl and boy inhabitants, repeated roles, former victims, or images produced by the street? Does the fall release Lynleit, or does another interruption return her to the bench? Does the street anticipate Fionn's death, draw from Lynleit's future, or leave a pattern that later events happen to reactivate? What does Felix observe between Lynleit's last ordinary step and her collapse? Lynleit is already watching Helena study her family, but Fionn remains alive and the danger has not yet broken into an open accusation. Several days later Fionn is found below the hill at the Vilen family house. Lynleit's involuntary recognition of the dead boy gives Helena a true emotional reaction that can be assigned a false cause. Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Fionn fionn Helena helena

entries.text: The River Choir I: The Empty Boats Beneath the Bridge · v1 · Archived MOM-006 · Unknowing Convergence A covert MSF team descends from a bridge to inspect small night shipments requested by Drake and Sherie. The tarp-covered wooden boats arrive empty, the Drowned Choir attacks from below, and Kyrien secretly witnesses Lynleit burn the drowned hands and stand on the river. The river attack separates the team. Kyrien witnesses Lynleit's forbidden ability and keeps it secret. A Vilen river bridge linking a city street to the quarantined park Sherie and Drake ask Lynleit to assemble a loyal MSF team and investigate recurring night traffic on the Vilen river. Drake's intelligence identifies small boats moving only on the darkest nights. No operator is visible, the pattern appears intricate, and contraband remains a plausible explanation. The chosen bridge links a city street to the quarantined park. The plan requires Felix to freeze the bridge's civil safety cameras, maintain communications, and remain on the city side as fallback while the river team descends by rope, inspects the boats, and leaves by rope at the next bridge. Several nights produce no boats. Each unsuccessful watch consumes the limited camera window and exposes Lynleit or Kyrien to small oddities emerging from the quarantined park that the mission gives them no freedom to pursue. After an unsuccessful watch is formally aborted, Lynleit and Kyrien play short card games while the camera feed and bridge equipment are restored. Kyrien wins the first game through technical play, and Lynleit requests a rematch because she cannot read him. Across the failed watches, Lynleit learns that Kyrien briefly stops breathing before a risky play. Kyrien learns the small hand movement that precedes one of Lynleit's decisions. Their continued rematches and attention to each other's physical tells allow the reader to recognize attraction before either character names or prioritizes it. inferred The successful interception occurs on the fifth watch. The unsuccessful watches reveal a branch breaking before the wind reaches the trees and a pale interruption in a frozen camera feed. The boats are small wooden craft with dark tarps over shallow holds. Fixed rudders keep them aligned while the current provides most of their movement. When the boats finally appear, Reiner, Lynleit, Kyrien, Maren, and Ivo descend and find them empty. Felix remains ashore. The final card game remains unfinished when the boats appear. When an empty boat shifts, Kyrien briefly steadies Lynleit at the waist near the Sparrow holster above her tailbone. Lynleit allows the contact, and Kyrien releases her before she asks. The empty boats, drowned hands, and pale girl imply that the Drowned Choir took the contraband crews before the interception, although the surviving officers cannot prove that connection. inferred The river attack begins while the officers search the empty boats for another explanation. The officers are capable swimmers. Reaching shore becomes difficult because unseen hands seize their legs and pull downward. After reaching land, Maren describes the sensation of hands gripping and pulling her legs. Reiner, Maren, and Ivo reach the street-facing city bank with Felix's fallback line without understanding what attacked them. They do not realize that Lynleit remains behind. The hands of different sizes and states of decay suggest many drowned victims, rather than one submerged attacker. inferred Only Lynleit sees the hands clearly. They seize her most violently and drag her underwater. Lynleit wears a fitted blue suede jacket for the operation because it interferes less with ropes and wet timber than her usual coat. The hands tear the blue suede jacket away during the underwater struggle. The attack activates her childhood fear of drowning. Fury releases her blue flame at unsafe volume, and the fire catches and burns the drowned hands even beneath the water. After breaking the surface, Lynleit's palm meets resistance. She brings a knee and then both boots onto the same yielding layer until she stands above the river. The drowned hands reach upward from the darkness but cannot pass through the surface layer beneath Lynleit's feet. A pale girl emerges wearing a dress made from dead fish. Fishing line sews her eyes shut. The girl's silence and tilted head imply that a person standing on water contradicts the rule by which she takes victims. inferred Kyrien is present as Lynleit's concealed unofficial asset rather than an acknowledged MSF officer. The force in the river separates Kyrien from the official team and drives him toward the quarantined park side of the river. Kyrien reaches the park bank, enters the trees, and observes Lynleit's confrontation on the river from inside the quarantine. Only Kyrien witnesses Lynleit walking on water. Lynleit tests each step across the yielding surface and backs toward the park bank while the girl remains still. Kyrien is too careful to acknowledge what he saw and feigns innocence convincingly. Lynleit reaches the park side of the river without the jacket, where Kyrien is waiting among the trees. They remain inside the night park, drenched and struggling to catch their breath. They sit with their backs pressed together to share body heat while they recover. The contact makes each of them aware of the other's breathing through their soaked clothes, continuing the physical tell-reading established during the card games without displacing the danger of the river. Lynleit indirectly asks whether Kyrien saw anything strange during the escape. Kyrien denies seeing anything, and his careful performance of innocence gives Lynleit nothing she can safely test. Kyrien's decision to protect the secret, made without an order from Lynleit, implies the first voluntary trust inside their coerced alliance. inferred What form does the river's scar take, and in what sense does the place remember the encounter? What intelligence survives the failed operation beyond the officers' separate accounts? Does the submerged blue flame leave a lasting injury on the Drowned Choir or only force the hands to release Lynleit? The hilltop agreement gives Drake and Sherie access to a small loyal MSF team without granting them control of the agency. Their first request is a limited investigation of apparently unmanned river shipments, with contraband still the leading material explanation. Felix, Reiner, Maren, and Ivo carry an account of impossible resistance from the city bank but no shared sight of its cause. Kyrien observes the river from the quarantined trees, and Lynleit later joins him on the park bank without the blue suede jacket. Their back-to-back recovery combines the physical awareness established during the failed watches with a mutual silence around what he witnessed. Lynleit later complains about the lost jacket. Much later, after Fionn's murder, the hotel-room refuge deepens that physical trust into emotional reliance. Sherie sherie Drake drake Lynleit lynleit Felix felix Reiner reiner Kyrien kyrien

entries.text: The River Choir I: The Empty Boats Beneath the Bridge · v5 · Current MOM-006 · Unknowing Convergence The River Choir, Part I. Kyrien checks the exits, endures four failed watches and boards the empty boats on the fifth. When the river takes hold of the team, the forbidden bank is the only ground he can reach. The limited inspection separates the team and forces Kyrien into the quarantined park without an explanation for what attacked them. A Vilen river bridge linking a city street to the quarantined park Kyrien inspects the bridge, locked park barrier and city steps before the covert boat operation. Four failed watches exhaust the camera windows; a breaking branch and a pale camera interruption remain unexplained. Lynleit and Kyrien play repeated card games during operational downtime. He watches her hands; she watches his fingers and face. Their attention to each other begins to exceed what either needs to win a card game. inferred On the fifth watch, heavy mist interrupts the view across the river. Three wooden boats arrive with fixed rudders and empty tarp-covered holds. Felix stays ashore while Reiner, Maren, Ivo, Lynleit and Kyrien descend by rope. Kyrien steadies Lynleit at the waist when the boat shifts and releases her as she catches the rail. Maren is pulled over the side. Reiner tries to hold her, then enters the water; Ivo follows to help. Lynleit puts on black gloves and rolls up her sleeves. Kyrien cuts a snagged line before their boat rolls. Kyrien feels fingers holding his leg but cannot see their source. Reiner, Maren and Ivo move towards the city steps while he struggles towards the park roots. Kyrien reaches the mud on the park bank without understanding the attack. What evidence remains aboard the empty boats? What causes the initial pull that takes Maren over the side?
