entries.text: Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea ren-arms Ren Arms Rennel, Narvea An established Narvean firearms manufacturer based in Rennel, the Ducal capital. Its pistol models traditionally carry bird nicknames. Each bird broadly corresponds to the physical character, size, role, and perceived personality of the pistol.

entries.title: The Church
entries.text: The Church # the-church Institutional record Known facts only World / The Church † Religious institution Knowledge kept behind doctrine Every church knows about the Magi at the highest point of its hierarchy. That knowledge descends only through controlled channels, leaving most clergy and church staff inside the same protected ignorance as the public. Public role Faith and authority Awareness Every church head Covert arm Special envoys Clergy access Highly restricted 01 Distributed knowledge The institution does not know as one body 01 MAJORITY OF THE CHURCH Ordinary faith Most clergy, staff, and worshippers operate inside the same protected ignorance as the wider public. Religious office alone does not grant access to magical knowledge. 02 HEAD OF THE HIERARCHY Guaranteed awareness The head of every church knows about the Magi and directs that church's response to the hidden world. 03 CONTROLLED OPERATORS Special envoys Each church maintains a contingent of operatives who carry the title of special envoy and act in the name of its head. OTHER RELIGIOUS TRADITIONS Pagan cults among the Magi Ancient pagan religions, including the Cult of Inanna, belong intrinsically to the Magi world. Their place in magic is distinct from the Church's official religious doctrines. Read about pagan traditions → 02 Special envoys Priesthood is the cover, not the profession OFFICIAL APPEARANCE Envoys of the heads of churches Special envoys are trained and presented as priests, allowing them to move through religious institutions with a credible public identity. Their primary training covers political operations, intelligence, combat, and covert intervention. Authority Act for a church head Cover Priesthood Structure Contingent within each church 01 Politics Institutional access, negotiation, leverage, and influence. 02 Espionage Covert placement, observation, clandestine activity, and the possible penetration of rival institutions. 03 Intelligence Collection, assessment, and controlled circulation of knowledge. 04 Combat Operational force when diplomacy and concealment fail. 05 Assassination Some envoys are trained for assassination. 06 Specialization Each envoy develops one or several operational specialties. Separate traditions Shared purpose does not mean shared doctrine. Both traditions maintain covert, assassination-capable priesthoods while regarding the other's system as dangerously unaccountable. ORTHODOX CHURCH Trust before procedure Orthodox envoys favor personal chains of trust, confession-like secrecy, and discretionary judgment. Authority moves through relationships whose moral burden rests heavily on the person exercising it. CATHOLIC CHURCH Procedure before discretion Catholic envoys favor dossiers, compartmentalized offices, and codified authorization. Authority moves through records and separated functions intended to prevent any one operative from holding the whole design. PLAUSIBLE, NOT CONFIRMED Special-envoy capabilities make covert or illegal infiltration of Magiarchates and other factions possible. The same risk also runs in reverse, because church structures may themselves be penetrated. 03 Institutional relations Every relationship is conditional WITH THE PUBLIC Protect ignorance Magic remains outside ordinary understanding, and Church knowledge is kept narrow. WITH THE MAGIARCHY Sanction, constrain, and verify Cross-national church structures face Magiarchates that are kept territorial and separate. Both sides hunt unsanctioned Magi, but the Church often doubts that Magiarchs will act decisively enough. WITH THE STATE Reveal only what is necessary Negotiations can occur near public institutions without making their magical subject visible to ordinary officials or officers. WITH RENEGADE MAGI Hunt through special envoys Magi without a jurisdiction who practice outside church supervision or permission are treated as criminals. Special envoys pursue them alongside the resources of the responsible Magiarch. 04 Accepted boundaries Not every possible act is permitted FORBIDDEN MIRACLE-MAKING Harmless effect, prohibited form The Church distinguishes pressure-based magecraft from miracle-making that resembles wizardry or imitates acts associated with Jesus, saints, saviours, and other sacred figures. Walking on water crosses that symbolic boundary. Lynleit conceals the accidental talent because exposure would bring strong punishment even if she had harmed nobody. Open Lynleit's profile → 05 Canon doctrine Suppression doctrine THE PRACTICAL RULE Protect the boundary of public knowledge Suppression doctrine is a shared responsibility of the Church and the Magiarchy for keeping witnesses of magic from carrying dangerous knowledge back into ordinary society. The Church holds final sanction over the doctrine, while Magiarchal resources may investigate, contain, absorb, or remove witnesses under that authority. It is not one fixed punishment. The response depends on what the witness knows, how credible they are, how much exposure has already occurred, and whether the witness can be contained without creating a larger crisis. 01 · IRREVERSIBLE Elimination Murder, assassination, or kidnapping may be considered when the Church believes exposure cannot be contained by other means. 02 · PRESSURE Coercion Extortion, intimidation, bribery, and threats can redirect a witness without making the magical truth public. 03 · REFRAME Discrediting A witness may be framed as mentally ill, unreliable, or otherwise incapable of persuading anyone who hears the account. 04 · ABSORPTION Church integration Some witnesses are forced into Church staff or clergy, where their access, movement, and story can be controlled from inside the institution. 05 · SERVICE Magiarchal integration Others may be absorbed into Magiarchy service staff or a supervised operational role, turning dangerous knowledge into a controlled obligation under Church-sanctioned authority. UNRESOLVED BOUNDARY Suppression can include coercion, forced service, or killing. Church sanction does not settle disagreements over whether a particular witness must be silenced. The Prosecutor General Kyrien's father's case A senior prosecutor helps government officials connected to the Magiarchy fabricate a case against Kyrien's father, a military-police commander who has silently witnessed magic. When repeated allegations fail to make him submit, the directing officials obtain sanction for his murder and present it as suicide. Some participants know the magical purpose; others act under confidential national-security instructions. The later inquiry finds distorted evidence, but a closed review protects the prosecutor, who is publicly vindicated and promoted to Prosecutor General. Read the family history → Read the Chapter → 06 Witness care and suppression After the rescue A rescued witness Seventeen days away from home After Lynleit brings an office worker out of an impossible building, special envoys examine him and take him into Church custody. His relatives have already been contacted. He spends seventeen days in a monastery, where meals and a bed accompany repeated questioning and explanations that make his account harder to repeat or trust. He returns to work but continues to avoid elevators. Read the witness's account → Read the incident record → 07 Story contact Father Mikhail finds the first witness breach Early in September, Fionn and Lynleit enter a church for confidential negotiations while Felix and Reiner wait outside. Later, Father Mikhail becomes the first authority to discover that Lynleit has disclosed forbidden knowledge to Kyrien, Felix, and Reiner. When she insists on handling the breach herself, he warns her: “What you do is none of my business, but don't be surprised if I'll be sent to clean up your mess.” The confrontation begins the pressure to place part of MSF under Magiarchal and Church accountability. Open the confrontation → Meet Father Mikhail → ✎ Page notes The Church Use notes to define doctrine, hierarchy, and boundaries without treating open questions as facts.

entries.title: The Director's House
entries.text: The Director's House # director-house Residential location record Family home · discreet MSF node World / The Director's House Residence · family seat · operational node The Director's House The family keeps two houses. The original stands in Turon, where Lynleit lived with her mother during junior school. After her mother's death, Fionn moved the family to Vilen for better access to the capital. The Vilen house is a three-floor residence whose offices, library, and discreet working rooms also support MSF operations. Floors Three Family houses Turon and Vilen Setting Vilen hillside above the river Rear grounds Small park and garden Operational role Residential mini-HQ 01 Family history Two houses, one family history Distant city House on the hill Rear garden City river Behind the house, a compact private park descends toward the river-facing edge of the hill. Thick vegetation and mature trees surround the residence closely enough for wind in the leaves and branches to remain part of its daily sound. Below, the river flows toward Vilen's city center. Lynleit regards flowing water as life energy: its movement gives her emotional grounding even though she has feared drowning since childhood. 02 Vertical plan Floors and private rooms 03 Highest floor Lynleit's chosen room A desk between trees and water After the family moved from Turon to Vilen, Lynleit made a third-floor study-bedroom her condition for accepting the new house. Its height lets her look beyond the trees toward the river while she works. Wind moving through leaves and branches gives the room the natural sound she finds most inspiring. 02 Middle floor Interior The second floor The rooms on this floor have not been described. 01 Garden level Glass and greenery Glass-enclosed rooms The rear side of the first floor opens into glass-enclosed relaxation areas facing dense greenery. In summer they extend domestic life among the trees. In winter the same rooms preserve the sight and sound of the landscape while protecting everyone inside from cold, rain, and wind. READING Library The family has a substantial library for reading, study, and research. WORK Several offices Private meetings and administrative work take place in offices within the house. 03 Dual role Residence and command space occupy the same address FAMILY NEST A place that belongs to the family first The family sleeps, studies, and rests here. Fionn's work shares the house with its bedrooms, garden, and glass-enclosed relaxation rooms. SHARED THRESHOLD Privacy becomes operational access The director can receive trusted people, review sensitive work, and continue agency business without leaving the protection and familiarity of home. MINI-HQ A discreet extension of MSF The offices and library support selected meetings, planning, and confidential work. MSF's formal headquarters remains in Turon. 04 Story connections Events at the house RESIDENT Lynleit Her third-floor room brings together the distant view, surrounding trees, and flowing water she uses for inspiration and emotional grounding. → DIRECTOR Fionn His public family seat also supports the confidential demands of MSF leadership. → INSTITUTION MSF The house is a residential operational node, distinct from the agency's formal headquarters in Turon. → HOUSEHOLD Ash enters the house Lynleit catches the grey cat after a clumsy chase, then cannot bring herself to put him out in the rain. → ✎ Page notes House Use notes to refine rooms, access, and domestic details without turning open architecture into canon.

entries.title: The Duchy
entries.text: The Duchy # narvea National reference record Country profile World / The Duchy of Narvea COUNTRY RECORD NAR · 001 Primary setting The Duchy of Narvea A large, sovereign Baltic country built around two sources of legitimacy: the Ducal Crown and the parliamentary state. Sovereignty resides jointly in the Crown and the Nation. Government Constitutional duchy State identity Multinational and civic Parliamentary capital Vilen Ducal seat Rennel MSF headquarters Turon Region Eastern Baltic Story role Main country Diplomatic role European meeting ground Jump to Territory Cities Authority Diplomacy Institutions Culture Fog 01 Territory A state along the eastern Baltic Narvea reaches from the approaches to St. Petersburg toward the southwestern Baltic frontier near Gdansk. National flag Ducal standard Show details for Rennel Show details for Turon Show details for Bird's Nest Show details for Port City Show details for Vilen Map of Narvea Hover, focus, tap, or select a city Mapped roles Why these cities matter Five centers divide Narvea's political, diplomatic, and strategic life. 01 Rennel · Ducal seat Home of the Crown, Court, ceremony, and dynastic archives. It represents continuity and sovereign legitimacy. 02 Turon · MSF headquarters The private contractor's concentration of officers gives it unusual local power. Constitutional loyalty and divided logistics restrain it, but politicians know the final safeguard is the officers' own decency. 03 Bird's Nest · Diplomatic ground Rival nations meet here to negotiate. Every country uses a different name for the city. 04 Port City · Western gateway Narvea's principal western connection to Baltic trade, maritime movement, and foreign access. 05 Vilen · Parliamentary capital Parliament, Cabinet, ministries, courts, and financial institutions make it the center of the modern state. 02 Dual capital tradition One country, two political worlds Rennel is the Ducal capital, Vilen the governmental capital, and Turon the military center and home of MSF. Rennel City image unavailable THE CROWN Ducal capital Rennel Located in the old Narva region. It represents dynasty, continuity, military tradition, nobility, and ceremony. Ducal Palace and Court Privy Council Ducal Guard headquarters Dynastic and heraldic archives Formal audiences Vilen City image unavailable THE STATE Parliamentary capital Vilen Narvea's center of government, law, administration, commerce, and modern political life. Its enormous urban park becomes the first visible center of the disappearances. Parliament and Cabinet Government ministries Major courts Financial institutions Vast park at the center of the first disappearances Turon City image unavailable THE PRESSURE POINT MSF headquarters Turon Turon is home to the headquarters of MSF, a fully private intelligence business that sells services to the government while retaining control of its own succession and internal affairs. Its officers give the company enough local force to mount a small rebellion or attempt secession if it ever chose to do so. Officer culture, divided logistics, constitutional loyalty, and a genuine lack of separatist ambition keep that possibility theoretical. MSF headquarters and senior officer corps Operational strength beyond ordinary agency needs Potential leverage over the central government Political anxiety that ultimately depends on personal restraint No rebellion is openly planned. The possibility simply remains in the backrooms of Narvean political life, where senior officials cannot afford to ignore it. 03 Constitutional balance Parliament governs. The Crown safeguards. Parliament chooses and controls the government, passes laws, and authorizes public money. The Duke gives constitutional form to those decisions and intervenes only through narrowly defined reserve powers. C Ducal sphere The Duke Head of state and constitutional guardian. Formally appoints the Prime Minister who commands parliamentary confidence Promulgates laws already passed by Parliament without rewriting them Represents the state, receives ambassadors, and maintains the Court and Ducal Guard Uses narrow reserve powers only during constitutional emergencies CROWN CONSTITUTIONAL BALANCE NATION P Democratic sphere Parliament & Government Elected authority and the executive accountable to it. Parliament grants or withdraws confidence in the Prime Minister and government Parliament debates, amends, and passes laws and approves taxation and spending The Prime Minister directs Cabinet, ministries, and the civil service The government sets domestic, defence, economic, social, and ordinary foreign policy 04 Diplomatic tradition The room where Europe stepped back Narvea became a trusted meeting ground where opposing European powers could settle their differences before rivalry became open conflict. NEUTRAL GROUND Authority meets here before force. Narvea's influence rests less on commanding Europe than on keeping its rivals in the same room long enough to avoid escalation. Method Conference and settlement Legacy Borders shaped without continental war 1803 to 1815 NAPOLEONIC WARS Narvea helped contain a continental crisis Its mediation played an important and constructive role during the wars. The settlements of this period also began shaping Narvea's borders into their modern form. 1917 EASTERN SETTLEMENT Revolution was prevented Opposing powers gathered in Narvea and contained an eastern political crisis before it could become a revolution. 1939 CONTINENTAL SETTLEMENT Europe avoided a major war Another Narvean conference stopped escalation between European powers, allowing the continent's borders and history to take a different course. NOW LIVING LEGACY Diplomacy became ordinary culture The habit of mediation still shapes how Narvean institutions understand authority, legitimacy, and public service. LANGUAGE AS CIVIC PRACTICE Multilingualism is expected, not exceptional. People in authority are expected to know several languages, but the custom reaches far beyond diplomatic circles. Narveans often move between languages in ordinary conversation for precision, courtesy, emphasis, or simple habit, even when no negotiation is taking place. THE CITY WITH MANY NAMES Bird's Nest is only one of its titles. Most negotiations between rival nations take place here. Every country has its own name for the city; Narveans call it Bird's Nest. 05 Institutions Parallel systems, one state Responsibility is divided deliberately. Similar-looking institutions can answer to different centers of authority. STATE · 01 Narvean Armed Forces The national Army, Navy, Air Force, reserves, and intelligence services answer through the constitutional government. National defence CROWN · 01 Ducal Guard An elite Crown formation protecting the ducal family, residences, and selected constitutional institutions. Dynastic security STATE · 02 Narvean Police Ordinary law enforcement remains under civilian authority, most likely through the Ministry of the Interior. Public order CROWN · 02 Privy Council Advises the Duke on constitutional questions, appointments, security, foreign affairs, and emergencies. Sovereign counsel BRIDGE · 01 Council of State A standing bridge between Crown and government for constitutional review, administrative law, major appointments, disputes, and emergency continuity. Its most dangerous cases begin when ordinary state sovereignty collides with supernatural authority the public constitution cannot acknowledge. Jurisdictional paradox Service and precedence Rank is not the same as office Narvea maintains its own hierarchy of court and civil ranks. A person's rank controls formal precedence, while their actual work may be diplomatic, judicial, academic, military, or administrative. 01 Chancellor of Narvea 02 Actual Privy Councillor 03 Privy Councillor 04 Actual State Councillor 05 State Councillor Drake's rank 06 Collegiate Councillor RANK AND OFFICE Drake is a State Councillor by rank and an Official for Special Assignments by office. He serves as an elite executive troubleshooter attached to a high-ranking personal office. Free from routine administration, he carries delegated authority into confidential criminal investigations, political counter-espionage, emergency corruption audits, and diplomatic errands. Open Drake's profile → 06 Cultural character Layered, regional, distinctly Narvean Narvean is a shared political identity, not a single ethnicity. Different regions keep their own language, faith, architecture, and historical memory. CIVIC IDENTITY The state is the common ground. Regional, linguistic, religious, urban, and rural communities can all be fully Narvean. INSTITUTIONS Old military customs, ducal administration, civic government, and modern Narvean constitutionalism. FAITH Catholic and Orthodox traditions coexist across different regions. PUBLIC LIFE Baltic merchant culture, old aristocratic ceremony, and modern parliamentary politics. CENTRAL TENSION A modern country that never fully discarded inherited hierarchy. Why it matters to the story A crisis in Narvea can become an argument over who has the right to act. The Crown, government, and older institutions must cooperate, but they do not share all their knowledge or accept responsibility for the same consequences. 07 Weather and visibility Narvean fog Fog is a recurring national problem, especially in certain areas. It delays journeys, restricts observation, and makes searches harder. Much of it is ordinary weather. During the Spill Some Holumn incidents produce unusually dense or extensive fog and mist. Vilen's quarantined park and river encounters are particularly affected. Familiar routes become difficult to follow by sight, and people can lose visual contact while remaining close enough to hear one another. Fog alone cannot tell a resident whether anything supernatural is happening. Holumns and the Spill → NARVEAN STATE ARCHIVE Read Markdown ↗ Document history → ✎ Page notes The Duchy Waiting 01 Add city images Replace the Rennel, Vilen, and Turon placeholders when approved city art is available. Notes are updated with the site code and published through GitHub Pages.

entries.title: The Magiarchy
entries.text: The Magiarchy # the-magiarchy Magical governance framework Territorial order World / The Magiarchy Territorial magical order A hierarchy that ends at the border The highest official position a Magus can obtain is Magiarch. Each Magiarch oversees magical affairs and relations with the churches inside a defined territory, but no Magiarch may turn that authority into a larger united organization. Highest office Magiarch Jurisdiction One territory Primary relation Magiarchy and churches Higher union Explicitly forbidden 01 Highest office The Magiarch is the ceiling of lawful magical authority OFFICIAL APEX Magiarch The office is usually held by the main Magus assigned to oversee the Magiarchy within a single territorial jurisdiction. 01 Territorial oversight Each Magiarch holds authority within a defined country or district. No universal magical hierarchy exists above them. 02 Church relations The office manages the local relationship between organized Magi and the churches that monitor and counterbalance them. 03 Factional leadership A Magiarch and the Magi aligned with them become a political actor with interests, allies, rivals, and local pressures. RECOGNITION PROCESS Authority is requested, judged, or won Several methods are known, and some carry far more respect than others. 01 Formal application A Magus with a substantial network, friendships, and connections submits a claim to the Church. Church approval gives the office its ordinary seal of legitimacy. 02 Contested decision When several candidates possess credible claims, church authorities and respected Magiarchs from other jurisdictions may share the decision. 03 Fitness contest A deadlock may be settled through a duel or another controlled competition intended to measure fitness for the office. 04 Sanctioned war The radical path permits rival Magi to fight to the death under Church supervision. Innocents cannot be harmed, and the existence of magic must remain hidden from the wider world. RECOGNITION CAN BE WITHDRAWN The Church may revoke recognition and destroy a Magiarch's legitimacy, but it cannot directly install a replacement. Withdrawal of recognition can therefore leave a vacancy without giving the Church the right to choose who fills it. 02 Territorial scale Jurisdiction follows practical size COMMON MODEL One country A single Magiarch may oversee the whole territory when its size and magical population can be managed as one jurisdiction. LARGER TERRITORY One district A large country may be divided into several Magiarchates. Each governs its own district independently, with no national magical superior. WHO DRAWS THE LINE Church authorities certify Magiarchate boundaries according to practical governability. The same transnational religious hierarchy that prevents Magi from forming a transnational command therefore decides where each supposedly independent magical jurisdiction begins and ends. 03 Structural counterbalance Magiarchal power is fragmented because the churches are not MAGIARCHATES Territorial and separate Magiarchs are explicitly forbidden from uniting into a larger organization. Their lawful authority stops with their territory. COUNTERWEIGHT CHURCHES Organized across borders The churches retain cross-national organization, giving them a wider structure that counterbalances the concentrated power of Magi. WHY THE BAN EXISTS A united organization of Magiarchs would overturn the intended balance and create open conflict with the churches. Examine the church counterweight → 04 Relations without a sovereign Magiarchates exist in an anarchic order NO HIGHER MAGICAL GOVERNMENT There is no lawful authority above the Magiarchs capable of reliably settling disputes between them. Anarchy here does not mean constant chaos. It means the absence of a superior power that can compel every Magiarchate to obey. 01 Self-preservation Each faction must judge threats and protect its own position. 02 Alliance Cooperation depends on interest, trust, and temporary alignment. 03 Rivalry Competing aims can produce pressure resembling conflict between states. 04 Uncertainty No Magiarch can be certain how another faction will use its power. PLAUSIBLE METHOD · NOT CONFIRMED Institutions may penetrate one another Rival Magiarchates, criminal Magi, and church networks may covertly or illegally place operatives, informants, or influence inside one another's structures. If this occurs, visible affiliation cannot be treated as proof of who truly directed an action. 05 Outside the sanctioned order A Magus without jurisdiction becomes a common enemy CRIMINAL STATUS Unbound and unsanctioned A Magus is treated as a criminal when they belong to no territorial jurisdiction and practice outside church supervision or permission. 01 No jurisdiction The Magus does not belong to a recognized Magiarchate. 02 No church sanction Their practice proceeds without church supervision or permission. CHURCH RESPONSE Special envoys The churches use their covert operatives to identify, pursue, and suppress Magi outside the sanctioned order. Examine special envoys → SHARED TARGET MAGIARCH RESPONSE Territorial resources The responsible Magiarch is expected to use the resources under their authority to hunt the same offender. SUPPRESSION DOCTRINE Witness control is a shared responsibility of the Church and Magiarchy, but the Church holds final sanction. Magiarchal resources may carry out coercion, discrediting, forced service, kidnapping, or lethal removal according to circumstance and perceived exposure. Read the doctrine record → UNEASY COOPERATION Church authorities often doubt that a Magiarch will act decisively against another Magus, even while relying on that Magiarch to help pursue the offender. 06 Succession after Fionn The Magiarchate passes to Lynleit NARVEA Lynleit After Fionn 's death, his biological daughter eventually inherits the Magiarchate as Narvea's new Magiarch. During her later absence, Kyrien carries the directorate in her absence. The two heirs divide the offices Fionn once held together. Open Lynleit's profile → Open the MSF record → 07 Religion among the Magi Ancient pagan traditions PAGAN CULT Cult of Inanna Doom Has an Address → The Cult of Inanna and other ancient pagan cults and religions play an important role in magic. These traditions are intrinsic to the Magi world and distinct from official Church doctrine. Fionn's lineage has maintained its association with the Cult for three thousand years. Lynleit inherits that association without directly participating. Father Mikhail knows the lineage's history of covenants and the political importance of intimacy within that tradition. ✎ Page notes Magiarchy Use notes to define offices and inter-Magiarchate customs without turning open questions into canon.
